News.title: Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed to ‘energy ceasefire’ and pleads ‘do not break it’ after Putin diesel deal
News.content:
Next

DONALD Trump has said Russia and Ukraine have agreed an “energy ceasefire” following the US president’s diesel deal with Vladimir Putin.

It comes after Trump blasted Volodymyr Zelensky for hitting the Kremlin tyrant’s oil refineries in the wake of the Moscow-Washington agreement.



The US president said on Truth Social today: “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine.

“Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!”



Neither Kyiv nor Moscow has commented on Trump’s claim on an “energy ceasefire” and it remains unclear exactly what the term means.

Amid the spiralling row between Trump and Zelensky, the US leader called for a new Ukrainian president – sinking their fragile relationship to a new low.

Earlier today Zelensky vowed to hold presidential elections if Russia agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.

The Ukrainian leader also pledged to stop strikes on Putin’s oil refineries as part of any deal.

Trump yesterday called for a new Ukrainian president following Kyiv’s attacks on Russian energy depots which the US had warned against.

Washington has sought to blame soaring global energy costs on Ukraine’s tactical blitz campaign on Putin’s fuel facilities – despite Trump’s war in Iran driving up costs.



The US also struck a deal with Russia earlier this week to have millions of barrels of Russian diesel sold on American and international markets.

Zelensky told ABC: “Please tell Putin, give us two months, ⁠60 days ​of total ceasefire, ​60 ​days, and we ⁠will organise ⁠elections.”

The Ukrainian war hero previously made the same claim in February when he told Axios he would hold elections in exchange for a ceasefire of 60 days.

He added: “With all respect to President Trump, it’s up to our society, up to our people to choose one or another leader.”

Zelensky also said: “Of course, it’s up to Ukrainians when to vote, how to do it and to choose one or another person.



“But if to answer on this question, I know that Putin wanted very much to change the president in Ukraine.”

Zelensky also said earlier today on X he would stop strikes on Russian oil hubs if Russia does the same.

“The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia, and only it,” he said.

“It’s already possible today to stop the strikes on the energy sector, but Putin doesn’t want to do that.

“Ukraine will be ready to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries if Russia stops attacking our energy infrastructure.

“Any de-escalation steps must be mutual and come with genuine guarantees.”

News.title: Nepal hit by flash floods again as homes swept away and locals urged to evacuate – just weeks after flood disaster
News.content:
Next

NEPAL has been struck by flash floods with dozens of homes swept away, bridges destroyed and locals scrambling to evacuate.

It comes just two months after catastrophic floods and deadly landslides wiped out thousands of homes and killed more than 1,400 people.



Horrifying footage shows a wall of water and mud surging downhill and flattening a building complex.

At least five people are missing after a dry landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki River and triggered widespread flooding in the Gorkha district.



Emergency helicopters and army soldiers have raced to the scene and airlifted people away from the stricken riverbanks.

Four bridges and around two dozen homes have been swept away in the terrifying deluge as drone images show banks swamped with mud.

Nearly 50 people have been rescued – but a further five are still missing – according to a top district official.

Gorkha’s most senior official, Dharmendra Kumar Mishra said: “We have asked villagers living along the river ​banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe.”

Mishra added that two suspension bridges had been swept away and a hydroelectric prject had been damaged by the floods.

Power towers have also been knocked down and washed away in the floods.



The army rescued 18 workers at the hydroelectric camp, according to Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.



A wall of surging sludge has also devastated a critical highway bridge which connected the Gorkha district with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Uprety.

Six peope at risk of being killed by a landslide in Jagat have also been evacuated, said Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

People have also fled their homes in the riverside town of Arughat following government warnings, according to social media posts.

It comes after a horror wall of mud and water ravaged through parts of Nepal in August – leaving 1,457 people dead.

More than 5,000 people are still missing after huge landslides swept across the Himalyan country.



Around 7,500 homes were damaged or destroyed in the catastrophe and 33,000 people affected.

The horror floods unfolded after a glacier bropke off and melted into a tributary off the river Trishuli.

The extra water broke the banks of the river and engulfed entire towns in water and mud.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Apocalyptic scenes showed entire villages reduced to rubble and multi-storey buildings decimated.

Rebuilding efforts are estimated to cost at least $4.77 billion.

News.title: Man found dead on popular beach by coastal path after passersby spotted ‘person at water’s edge’
News.content:
BEACH DEATH Man found dead on popular beach by coastal path after passersby spotted ‘person at water’s edge’







Next

A MAN has been found dead on a popular beach path after a passerby spotted a person by the water’s edge.

Officers scrambled to the scene in Brighton at around 9.40am today after serious welfare concerns were raised.



Despite the best efforts of emergency services the man was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

Police enquiries are underway as the cordon remains in place on the beach.



A spokeswoman for Sussex Police said: “At around 9.40am on Sunday (October 11), officers responded to concerns for the welfare of a man who had been seen at the water’s edge on Rottingdean beach.

“The man was sadly pronounced deceased at the scene, and enquiries remain ongoing to establish his identity and the circumstances of how he came to be in the water.

“Emergency services continue to work in the area, and no further information is available at this time.”

News.title: Pensioner, 73, charged with murder after woman, 71, dies after being found with ‘serious injuries’ at house
News.content:
OAP CHARGE Pensioner, 73, charged with murder after woman, 71, dies after being found with ‘serious injuries’ at house







Next

A PENSIONER has been charged with murder after a 71-year-old woman died.

Cops and emergency services scrambled to an address in Bradley Stoke, Bristol, at around 2pm on Friday.

A 71-year-old woman was found with serious injuries and pronounced dead at the scene, said cops.

Gerald Bishop, of Sherbourne Avenue, was arrested and has now been charged with murder, Avon and Somerset Police said.





The 73-year-old was remanded in custody ahead of an appearance at Bristol Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Police say while the incident will be a shock to the local community, they do not believe there is an ongoing threat to those living nearby.

Supt Karen Corrigan said: “We would like to offer our sincere condolences to the woman’s grieving family at what will be a devastating time for them, and specially trained officers will provide them with ongoing support.

“The investigation is in its early stages, but we have arrested a man, who remains in police custody, while we seek to gain an understanding of this tragic incident.



“This will come as a great shock to the community, but we do not consider there to be any ongoing risk to the public and if anybody has any concerns, they are welcome to approach officers in the area.

“We will have an increased police presence in the area over coming days in order to carry our vital enquiries as part of this investigation and to provide reassurance to members of the community.”

News.title: Brave boy, 11, bitten by dog after rushing to help screaming woman as three ‘bullmastiffs’ ran loose in park
News.content:
BITE HORROR Brave boy, 11, bitten by dog after rushing to help screaming woman as three ‘bullmastiffs’ ran loose in park







Next

A BRAVE schoolboy who was bitten in a dog attack had rushed to help a screaming woman.

Frankee McKenna, 11, reportedly heard the woman screaming in the park after three loose dogs, said to be bullmastiffs, “went after her”.



He cycled over to help the woman but was bitten on the thigh and had to be rushed to hospital his mum Sarah said.

She told Manchester Evening News that she was “proud” of Frankee for being “very brave”.



Sarah said while she wasn’t at the scene, witnesses told her that three loose dogs – said to be “Bullmastiff” type – ran into Newton Heath on Thursday evening.

She continued: “They went after a lady who had three dogs with her further down the park.

“They were being aggressive and vicious so the youth club staff shouted the kids to get out of the park, so they all did then this lady was screaming.

“Frankee then got on his bike and rode over to her to help her. One of them then bit him on his thigh.

“The lady took him off his bike and put him in a tree away from the dogs.

“Then the police turned up some of them had guns and everything was taped off.”



Frankee was discharged from hospital after being given antibiotics and is said to be “fine”.

But “he won’t be going back to the park for a while” his mum added.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said one of the loose dogs had been seized and the other two were in kennels, the force have not confirmed the breed.

A 31- year-old man was arrested on suspicion of possessing an aggressive animal.

News.title: Huge Ibiza sex trafficking ring smashed as Spanish cops free 25 women who were lured with fake job offers as 4 arrested
News.content:
Next

A HUGE Ibiza sex trafficking ring that lured in 25 women with fake job offers has been busted by Spanish police.

Four suspects have been arrested and nearly £100,000 has been seized as part of the prostitution crackdown operation.



The alleged victims, mainly Venezuelan women aged between 18 and 25, were deceived when recruiters offered fake job offers in hospitality or manicure roles, police said.

After arriving in Spain, ring members would pick them up at the airport, confiscate their belongings and cash, and take them to network-linked properties.



They would then be forced to carry out sex work to repay debts of about £4,000.

Authorities said the arrests took place as part of Operation Gecaroni which concluded on October 5 after a months-long probe.

The four suspects have been accused of forced prostitution, drug trafficking and money laundering.

Local cops said the women were subject to “strict control” while stuck under the ring’s control.



They were also forced to remain constantly available for sexual services.

The ring leaders allegedly used coercion and threatened to alert immigration authorities if they complained.

Police said CCTV was used to track the women’s movements at properties they were forced to stay at in the Platja d’en Bossa entertainment district.

The sex trafficking network was mainly run during the summer holiday period in Ibiza.

It moved to other parts of the peninsula when the tourist season ended.



The group has also been accused of selling sexual enhancers and narcotics.

Ring leaders allegedly maintained a high standard of living with the profits.

Local authorities said the gangsters rented luxury homes and swanky vehicles.

The investigation has also highlighted an alleged money laundering scheme.

Officers conducted four raids and searches at homes linked to the ring in different parts of Ibiza.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nearly £100,000 in cash was seized, along with drugs, electronic devices and materials linked to the video surveillance of the women.

News.title: Fears of new Putin hit squad in Brit holiday hotspot as two Ukrainians drop dead days apart from ‘heart attacks’
News.content:
VLAD'S DIRTY WORK Fears of new Putin hit squad in Brit holiday hotspot as two Ukrainians drop dead days apart from ‘heart attacks’







Next

VLADIMIR Putin may have deployed another kill squad on European soil to hunt down Kremlin critics, a Ministry of Defence source has warned.

Cops are probing the potential poisonings of two Ukrainian community leaders found dead just 72 hours apart under suspicious circumstances.



One was discovered inside a hotel in Portugal’s Algarve, and the other at a sports complex in Barcelona.

A well-placed MoD source with extensive experience monitoring Russia told The Sun: “Two men – both fit and healthy, both outspoken critics of Putin and Moscow – suffer heart attacks three days apart?



“I don’t think many people are buying it as a coincidence.”

The body of Pavlo Sadokha, 56, a fierce critic of the Russian president, was found in his hotel room in Quarteira on September 13.

Read More World News KREMLIN’S GHOSTS Inside Putin’s secret black ops unit behind deadly Salisbury poisoning

Three days later, Roman Rodyk, who founded the Ukrainian Community in Barcelona, collapsed and died while playing basketball in the Catalan capital.

Both deaths had initially been attributed to heart failure, but sources say Rodyk was a non-smoker, did not drink, and was a fit and healthy sportsman.



Pavlo had a history of heart disease – but family said his health was “perfectly under control” – leading Portuguese prosecutors to launch a criminal probe into his death.

Investigators are now looking into whether poisoning with hidden toxins may have caused his cardiac arrest and disguised foul play.

The source said: “Whether you send a team or you contract a freelancer, they have an established support network in place there.

“They have reliable people to get them in, supply what they need, and get them out again.

“But a message is sent; ‘We can get to you anywhere’.”



Law enforcement agencies and intelligence chiefs remain on high alert for killers and saboteurs working on behalf of Moscow in the UK and Europe.

Detectives and investigators are acutely aware that Putin’s forces subcontract assassinations to Russian Organised Crime Groups, as The Sun has reported on before.

The MoD source continued: “Iberia is a hotspot for Russian activity.



“The authorities are starting to get on top of it, but OCG factions have had years to embed themselves. They have a real job on their hands.”

The Kremlin has a long history of using poisons and nerve agents against its enemies, including trying to disguise murders as natural deaths.

Recent cases include the Novichok attack in Salisbury, the murder of Alexei Navalny, and the attacks against Emilian Gebrev.

The MoD source said: “The Russian security services learned hard lessons after Salisbury. It wasn’t just embarrassing; it was a turning point.

“Russia had 150 intelligence officers expelled from their posts in Europe and beyond, so they had to rapidly rethink things, to evolve.



“Their Ops guys come into Europe on State-issued false documents, then they’re free to carry out their missions.

“Unless you have specific intel on an individual or a team, you’ll have a devil of a job stopping them all.”

Intelligence chiefs warned this year that Moscow is stepping up plots to kill its enemies across Europe.



Just days ago, US prosecutors charged five people over an alleged network of Russian-led assassins operating on American soil.

John Eisenberg, Assistant Attorney General for National Security, called the plot a “global assassination network”.

American soil has traditionally been regarded as a relatively safe haven for those speaking out against the Kremlin.

But operations are underway to recruit US citizens and foreigners to carry out killings on the Kremlin’s orders, Eisenberg said.

The cell’s leader, Yuri Khrameev, allegedly offered a US citizen about $25,000 to kill a target in Lithuania.



And one of the Cuban plotters reportedly organised logistics for attacks in the Czech Republic and Lithuania in 2024.

Commander Dominic Murphy, former head of the Metropolitan Police’s Counter Terrorism Command, said Moscow began using hired proxies after Salisbury.

The lead investigator on the bungled assassination attempts against Sergei and Yulia Skripal, said the following mass expulsions made it much harder for Russian officers to operate in Europe.



In May, three ranking Western intelligence officials from different countries told AP that Russia’s campaign of targeted killings has stepped up since the 2022 invasion.

They linked it to about 191 acts of sabotage, arson and disruption across Europe.

Lithuanian prosecutors have charged 13 people from at least seven countries over two plots they said were directly ordered by the GRU.

Meanwhile, Germany broke up two plots: one against the head of a German arms firm supplying Ukraine, and one against a Ukrainian military official.

Officials said Russia’s services are now bolder in their choice of targets, going after Russian activists, foreign supporters of Ukraine and military defectors.



One senior European intelligence official said: “This campaign is not by accident or chance.”

In August, Poland said it had foiled a Russian plot to kill an American citizen in Warsaw.

Putin has denied that Russia is waging a sabotage campaign against Europe.

Pavlo Sadokha led the Union of Ukrainians in Portugal.

Allies say he exposed Russian spy networks and was regularly threatened with violence.



Mykola Shymonyak, vice-president of Sadokha’s association, said: “Our objective is that all the possible hypotheses are fully investigated.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Detectives in Portugal say toxicology results are due next week.

Cops in Spain are yet to release the details of their investigation.

News.title: At least 11 dead and 27 injured after tour bus crashes into tow truck in horror smash in Turkey
News.content:
Next

AT least 11 people have been killed and 27 are injured after a horror bus crash in Turkey.

The horror unfolded when a coach turned over after smashing into a truck near the entry to a motorway, authorities said.



Shocking images showed the site of the crash after the bus, travelling from the city of Bursa and the seaside town of Izmir, rolled over.

Emergency services rushed to the scene near the Akhisar Toll Gates on the Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir Highway to help those wounded.



Ambulances, fire crews, and police were dispatched to the scene before rushing the injured people to hospital.

Local authorities said: “Health and rescue teams were directed to the scene, and efforts to rescue our citizens affected by the accident were quickly launched.”

Reports say the coach was carrying 34 passengers and three staff, while the truck that was hit was carrying one driver.

Of the 27 injured, 16 were taken to hospital.



It is unclear what the nationalities of the victims are.

Footage showed the aftermath of the tragedy, with emergency services sifting through the mangled wreckage.

The coach was reportedly a tour bus en route to the hot springs in Denizli.

Local authorities said: “Eleven of our citizens have died in the accident, and 27 have been injured.

“The injured citizens have been transported to hospitals.”



Manisa Governor Vahdettin Özkan arrived at the scene before paying respects to those who lost their lives.

He said: “First of all, I offer my condolences to the families of our deceased citizens.

“Besides that, we have 34 passengers, three crew members, and the truck driver.

“In total, there are 11 fatalities and 27 injured. Of these injured, 16 were sent to hospitals with yellow code, nine with green code, and one with red code.”

He added: “Currently, on-site investigations are continuing under the coordination of our Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are experiencing in a painful way how vital it is to strictly adhere to traffic rules.”

A probe has been launched to investigate the full circumstances of the crash.

News.title: Christa Pike 'angry' over botched execution and was 'ready to die'
News.content:
Christa Pike 'angry' over botched execution and was 'ready to die'

A close friend of death row inmate Christa Pike, who survived a botched execution attempt, revealed the conversation they days before the murderer was due to die

View 4 Images Christa Pike's friend claimed the murdered was 'ready to go' (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

Christa Pike, who survived two lethal injections, was allegedly "ready to go" and is "angry" at the botched execution attempt.

‌



‌



The death row inmate, who was sentenced three decades ago for the sadistic murder of her 19-year-old classmate, was set to be the first woman to be executed in Tennessee in over 200 years. Pike, 50, however survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on September 30.

‌



Pike was rushed to hospital and was discharged back to the prison where she has spent the past 30 years, her lawyers said. Pike's close friend has reportedly revealed the inmate was "ready" to die.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Christa Pike cries after being sentenced to death on March 30, 1996 (Image: WBIR-TV via AP)

Nine dead in horror Pennsylvania mass shooting including two children and pregnant woman READ MORE :

Marcy Wilson, 60, spoke to her murderer friend four days before the scheduled execution date and reportedly told Pike not to give up hope.

‌



Wilson, according to the Daily Mail, said Pike was however "ready to go" and was at peace with death. Wilson said Pike asked if she would want some of her ashes and a lock of her hair, to which Wilson said yes.

Wilson said: "It was really hard to talk about. I've never had a conversation with someone who knew when her expiration date was. She was pleased when I said yes.

"She was calm, she was happy, she was sad. It was every single emotion you can think of. She told me, "Marcy, I'm not afraid to die. I'm just afraid of the process'."

‌



View 4 Images Pike murdered her classmate Colleen Slemmer (Image: WVLT 8)

Pike's lawyers, on Wednesday, said the inmate had been shackled to the bed in a heavily guarded room and she felt "confused and angry".

Speaking to the press outside the Tennessee court house, her lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters Pike was "very aware that the state tried to execute her". Spivey said Pike asked two questions as soon as she woke up: "Where am I and who are you?"

‌



View 4 Images Pike's lawyer Randy Spivey speaks at a press conference outside court (Image: Ray Di Pietro/Shutterstock)

Spivey added that the inmate was unable to move, had "extraordinary" swelling to her hands and arms, and woke up with a blood clot and pneumonia. Pike's legal team said for days they believed the inmate was brain dead and thought she would be removed from life support.

Her attorneys were appealing for Pike to be removed from death row and have her punishment downgraded to life in prison following the botched execution.

Article continues below

Pike, aged 18, lured her classmate Colleen Slemmer into an isolated area of the University of Tennessee campus and brutally killed her January 1995, after believing Slemmer was interested in her boyfriend. Pike's boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and their friend Shadolla Peterson were also convicted of participating in Slemmer's murder.

News.title: Yorkshire Wildlife Park latest: Tiger will not be euthanised after fatal mauling
News.content:
The man who died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, near Doncaster, was seen 'dancing' before entering the enclosure, witnesses say

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has confirmed the fate of the tiger that mauled a man to death yesterday.

Police and paramedics raced to Yorkshire Wildlife Park, near Doncaster, at about 1.35pm following reports that a man had jumped into a tiger enclosure. South Yorkshire Police said the man was pronounced dead at the scene. The tiger was uninjured and remained inside the enclosure following the attack.

There were reports of gunshots fired shortly before the park was evacuated and an air ambulance arrived. Footage emerged online showing a man lying on the grass in the tiger's enclosure. He was heard shouting: "Stop, stop, stop, stop, stop!"

Yorkshire Wildlife Park today said Altai the tiger is "safe and well" and will not be euthanised.

A visitor said she had seen the victim in the 20 minutes before the tragedy. "The man who I saw on the bridge with his EarPods in dancing was happily enjoying seeing the tiger," she said. "I'm not sure if he was with a carer or family member but I honestly do think he just wanted to play with the tiger."

News.title: 'Change law to stop people who run over cats from driving away' plea
News.content:
'Change law to stop people who run over cats from driving away' plea

EXCLUSIVE: Ministers face calls to change to law to ensure drivers who run over cats are required to report it in the same way they have to for dogs and cattle

View 2 Images Maurice was seriously injured in a hit-and-run earlier this year (Image: Gofundme)

Drivers who run over cats should be legally required to inform police, ministers have been urged - with campaigners demanding a law change.

‌



‌



At the moment motorists are required to report collisions with a range of animals including dogs, goats and cattle, but this does not apply to cats. Lib Dem MP Freddie van Mierlo told the Mirror this needs to change - as drivers should do what they can to prevent suffering.

‌



It follows a hit-and-run in his Henley and Thame constituency, which saw a cat suffer horrific injuries to her back legs after being struck by a 4x4. The car drove off, leaving the pet - named Maurice - injured in the road.

‌



Mr van Mierlo said: "So the police reviewed the footage and don't believe it was deliberate, but the facts are that nobody stopped, and they weren't obliged to. Animals are sentient, and the idea that they could just be hit and be left by the side of the road to suffer is unacceptable.

Blow to Nigel Farage as Reform sheds over 50 newly-elected councillors in five months READ MORE :

View 2 Images Lib Dem MP Freddie van Mierlo has called for the law to be changed (Image: PA)

"And that's before we consider how important they are as pets and as members of our families." Earlier this year nearly 190,000 people signed a petition calling for the law to be changed, and the measure is set to be debated in Parliament next month.

‌



In June Maurice, who regularly sits at a toll bridge in Whitchurch on Thames in Oxfordshire, was struck in an incident caught on CCTV. Frantic staff found her the following day, and a fundraiser for her treatment has raised more than £10,000.

Mr van Mierlo said: "Most upstanding citizens, if they sadly hit a cat, they will stop and try and identify it and take it to a vet and do the right thing."

He said a change to the law would require people to stop, but would not see drivers prosecuted for criminal wrongdoing if the collision was an accident.

‌



A petition, to be debated in Westminster Hall by MPs, states: "It is legal in the UK to hit a cat when driving and not need to stop or report collisions, leaving them scared, alone, and in pain. Cats are important, loved, valued family members for many and we believe the law should reflect this.

"We want the Government to legislate to require drivers to stop, check and report any road collisions with cats if they’re injured on the road, and holds drivers accountable if they fail to stop and report a collision involving a cat on the basis they left a cat to unnecessarily suffer."

The RSPCA is calling for the law to change. The charity's head of public affairs, David Bowles, told The Mirror: “We know the worry and distress that comes from owners never knowing what happened to their cat, the uncertainty and heartbreak of not knowing whether they’re alive or dead, or not being able to say goodbye. Reporting if you hit a cat with your car to the police and scanning the cat for a microchip in order to contact the owners gives them the closure they deserve.”

Article continues below

A Department for Transport (DfT) spokesperson told The Mirror: “We know it's very distressing for pet owners when their pets are involved in road collisions.

“Although it's not mandatory to report road collisions with cats and we have no plans to change this, drivers should make every effort, if possible, to find and inform the owner."

News.title: The 'pay zero Council Tax' rule the government urges millions not to miss
News.content:
The 'pay zero Council Tax' rule the government urges millions not to miss

Most people aged over 18 have to pay Council Tax but the government has issued an alert to some who get it free of charge

View 2 Images Most people will have to pay Council Tax (Image: Getty)

The government has issued an alert warning a key group of people that they may not have to pay Council Tax - but the discount isn't automatic. It is urging people to apply if they meet certain criteria.

‌



‌



In a post on X on Sunday afternoon it told students that if everyone in their household is in full-time education they do not have to pay the fee. With millions of students heading to universities and higher education across the country this month and finances already tight, this could be welcome news to many.

‌



It said: "If everyone in your house is a full-time student, you pay zero Council Tax! To count as a full-time student, your course must:

‌



last at least 1 year

involve at least 21 hours of study per week

View 2 Images Some people might be exempt from Council Tax (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

To qualify you do not just have to be at university. It added those studying for a qualification up to A level who are under 20 might also be exempt. To qualify your course must:

‌



last at least 3 months

involve at least 12 hours of study per week

Content cannot be displayed without consent

However it also warned people need to act to get the help. It said: "The discount isn’t applied automatically. If you get a bill and need to apply for a discount, just search 'apply for a Council Tax discount' on http://GOV.UK."

‌



What is Council Tax

Council Tax is a local property-based tax in England, Scotland, and Wales paid by households to help fund public services run by local councils. It pays for essential community and regional services including:

Rubbish and recycling collection

Local schools and education services

Police and fire services

Libraries, parks, and leisure facilities

Adult social care and children's services

Street maintenance and lighting

How much does it cost?

The cost of council tax varies significantly based on where you live and your property's valuation band. Across England, the average Band D council tax bill is £2,392 per year.

‌



Because council tax is localised, your bill depends on your specific authority. You can check the rates in your local authority area here.

Who pays Council Tax

According to the government most people aged over 18 have to pay with full council tax based on at least two adults living at home. However some people are not counted 0 or "disregarded" - when working out how many people live in a property.

This means you might be able to apply for a discount on your Council Tax bill if you get one. You’re disregarded if you’re:

‌



under 18 years old

on certain apprentice schemes

18 or 19 years old and in full-time education

a full-time student at college or university

under 25 years old and get funding from the Education and Skills Funding Agency

a student nurse

a foreign language assistant registered with the British Council

severely mentally impaired

a live-in carer for someone who is not your partner, spouse, or child under 18

a diplomat

Apply for a discount or exemption

You need to apply for a Council Tax discount or an exemption, even if you’re disregarded. You’ll get 50% off your bill if everyone living in your household is disregarded. Students are exempt if all household members qualify.

You’ll get 25% off your bill if you pay Council Tax and either:

Article continues below

you live on your own

everyone else in your home is disregarded

Contact your local council if you’re unsure about whether you can get a discount or who’s responsible for paying.

News.title: Strictly Come Dancing 2026: Delta Goodrem sparks concern as fans spot problem
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing fans are reeling after a leaked spoiler has revealed a favourite couple are sent packing in the second elimination

The Strictly Come Dancing leaderboard is more sporadic than ever and sadly someone has to go home.

The results of the second elimination have been leaked online by those in the live studio audience, with fans reacting strongly to the shock outcome with a fan favourite given the boot.

Pop star Delta Goodrem scored 33 for her Disco-themed Salsa, which landed the first nine of the series while at the other end, former Man City star Shaun-Wright Phillips picked up just 15 points and was widely panned for his Quickstep.

There was more drama off-screen with Amy Dowden sneaking a moment in the dressing room to fire back at Brendan Cole for slamming her this week. Brendan said the professional was 'not good enough' to compete. Safe to say, Amy's had her say in the best way at the 'obsessed' former dancer.

News.title: Four more UK cities consider banning balaclavas weeks after nation's first
News.content:
Four more UK cities consider banning balaclavas weeks after nation's first

More parts of the UK could introduce balaclava bans after councils complain about anti-social and 'intimidating' behaviour

View 2 Images More UK cities could bring in balaclava bans (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

Four more UK cities are exploring ways to impose balaclava bans just a month after the face coverings were prohibited in a major city.

‌



‌



Nottingham became one of the first cities in the nation to bring in restrictions on balaclavas. It allows police to ask people to removed them if they "reasonably believe" the coverings are being used to hide their identity to commit a crime or anti-social behaviour.

‌



Officials in Newport, Coventry, Stafford and Wolverhampton could soon follow suit as they are all looking into ways to strengthen existing powers to challenge people wearing balaclavas.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Nottingham introduced a balaclava ban in September

Annette Farmer said she was forced to move her jewellery shop online following a shoplifting incident and two burglaries carried out by people wearing balaclavas.

‌



The business owner, speaking to BBC Radio Wales Breakfast, said: "I didn't feel safe any more. There are gangs hanging around with balaclavas.

"They're on bikes as well, speeding around the city, speeding around the river front... just basically doing what they want. It's intimidating, it's frightening."

Newport councillor David Fouweather said the city council was "sorry to lose her" and revealed a balaclava ban was proposed following a rise in incidents that left locals "feeling intimidated".

‌



Matthew Evans, another local councillor who proposed the ban, said people were using face coverings to "rob, burgle and deal drugs in our city centre" and "avoid detection". Cllr Evans also proposed "exemptions for religious reasons".

Stafford is set to bring in measures against balaclavas when the borough council updates its public spaces protection order (PSPO) around the end of 2026, according to the BBC. This ban could lead to a £100 fixed penalty notice for people breaching the order.

Councillor Jill Hood, during a meeting earlier this year, said: "I'm sure we've all seen the young people who appear to have black face coverings - used to intimidate or enable antisocial behaviour.

‌



"This will not be permitted. This supports public safety and reassurance in all restricted public areas, particularly busy town centre locations. Fear of crime can be just as intimidating as an actual crime occurring."

A petition was launched in Coventry calling for a ban on people riding bikes and scooters from wearing balaclavas. Coventry's Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO) is due to be updated in November and could see the order added and enforced.

The petition said: "It is not just the riding of bikes in the pedestrianised area that threatens public safety, but the sinister appearance of these individuals that is causing alarm and distress to those wanting to go about life in a transparent way."

Article continues below

Nottingham introduced its balaclava ban on September 15 and it allows authorities to hit people who defy police requests with a £70 fixed penalty notice or be prosecuted - courts can impose a maximum fine of £1,000.

News.title: Manisa tour bus crash leaves at least 11 dead and 27 injured in truck collision
News.content:
Manisa tour bus crash leaves at least 11 dead and 27 injured in truck collision

Eleven people have been killed and 27 others injured after a crash involving a tour bus and a truck in Manisa, western Turkey

View 2 Images An aerial view of the accident site after a tow truck and a tour bus collided in the Akhisar district of Manisa (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Eleven people have been killed and 27 others injured in a tour bus crash in western Turkey.

‌



‌



The bus overturned after colliding with a truck on a motorway in the Manisa province as it travelled from the city of Bursa to the coastal city of Izmir on Sunday morning, local authorities said.

‌



The Manisa governor's office said authorities received a report of the crash near the Akhisar toll gates at 11.11am local time (9.11am BST).

‌



"AFAD [Turkey's Disaster and Emergency Management Authority], police, gendarmerie, fire crews, and 112 emergency medical teams were promptly dispatched to the scene and have begun response efforts," Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci said on X.

"We are closely monitoring the situation in coordination with all relevant agencies," he added.

‌



View 2 Images The tour bus was travelling from the city of Bursa to the coastal city of Izmir when the crash happened (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Yorkshire Wildlife Park tiger that mauled man will not be put down – latest READ MORE :

Northern Lights alert as Met Office issues forecast for Aurora Borealis across UK READ MORE :

Photographs showed the bus lying across safety barriers with its windscreen smashed.

Those injured have been transferred to local hospitals for treatment, the governor's office added.

Article continues below

The cause of the collision is not yet known, and an investigation has been launched.

Ciftci referred to those killed as "our citizens" in his statement. But it remains unclear whether all those involved were Turkish nationals or whether any foreign nationals were among the passengers.

News.title: UK snow forecast as maps show five inches and flurries as far south as Devon
News.content:
UK snow forecast as maps show five inches and flurries as far south as Devon

Weather forecasting models suggest snow could be on the cards for some later this month, with flurries possibly even impacting some southern areas in England

View 4 Images The outlook for 9pm on October 20 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Brits could face snow within days, and weather models suggest some flurries might even reach southern parts of the UK.

‌



‌



The GFS weather model shows snow developing in northern parts of Scotland throughout the evening of October 20, initially falling at a rate of around 2mm per hour over higher ground.

‌



Data suggests the snow will intensify and slowly start moving southward over the subsequent hours. Maps for 6am on October 21 some flurries over the Peak District, while heavier snow falls on the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland.

‌



The weather system is expected to bring rain for most as it sweeps down the country. However, the GFS model shows some of the precipitation could briefly fall as snow on the morning of October 22 in Devon, Somerset and Dorset.

View 4 Images The outlook for 6am on October 21 (Image: WXCHARTS)

BBC Weather issues verdict on El Nino and polar vortex bringing major snow to UK READ MORE :

Met Office reveals how deadly Hurricane Isaias will impact UK weather next week READ MORE :

Snow depth charts suggest it won’t settle anywhere other than the Yorkshire Dales and the Scottish Highlands. As much as 15cm (5.9 inches) could land over the highest peaks in Scotland.

‌



Met Office forecast

The Met Office says “thicker cloud and some outbreaks of rain” are on the cards across the UK tomorrow, with an area of low pressure also bringing the “prospect of gales along coasts and over high ground in northern and western” areas.

View 4 Images The outlook for 9am on October 22 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Mike Silverstone said: “Currently, however, these conditions are not likely to result in the need for severe weather warnings.”

‌



Tuesday looks set to be “unusually mild for October”, especially in eastern and southeastern areas. A band of rain, bringing heavy showers at times, is expected to move across the UK before “fresher conditions arrive from the west”. Northern Ireland and Scotland might see some “lively showers”, the Met Office says.

View 4 Images Snow depth (cm) on October 22 (Image: WXCHARTS)

BBC Weather forecast

The BBC forecast states: “Tomorrow will then be a cloudy and damp day, with thick cloud for all, and some patchy spells of rain lingering in spots. A chance of some mist and fog over the hills and coasts. Breezy and mild.

Article continues below

“Windy on Tuesday with a band of cloud and rain moving in, followed by sunshine. Scattered heavy showers will push into northwestern Scotland by the evening.”

News.title: Riyadh airport attack another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
News.content:
Saturday's attack on King Khalid Airport in Riyadh is another dangerous moment in a region that is already fraught with tension and conflict.

Saudi Arabia wasn't ready for this.

In recent weeks the Houthis have stepped up their attacks on Saudi Arabian soil, but their attacks over the past few days have hit the country's critical infrastructure in the form of the capital's main airport, apparently penetrating Saudi air defences with ease.

The physical damage can be quickly repaired, but the country's reputation as a safe haven of stability is taking a battering.

As well as all the airport attacks, the Houthis have sought to take control of strategically significant positions along the Red Sea coast and around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. This further increases the risk to safe navigation along the vital maritime corridor - although the Yemeni government says it has "secured" the strait.

The civil war in Yemen between the country's government - which is internationally recognised and supported by Saudi Arabia - and the Houthis, who are backed by Iran, has been going on for more than a decade. It has left many thousands of people dead and plunged Yemen into one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

It is a complex and often confusing geopolitical conflict, and this latest escalation needs to be seen in the broader context of the tension between Iran, the United States and Israel.

News.title: Buildings swept away as flash floods hit central Nepal
News.content:
A flash flood has washed away houses, bridges and damaged a hydropower project along a river in central Nepal.

The army said on Sunday that it had rescued 49 people from flood affected areas, but five are still missing, the district's top official confirmed.

It is believed that the flood was caused by a landslide upstream of the Budhi Gandaki River in the Gorkha district.

Four bridges and nearly two dozen houses have been swept away, as well as a camp at a hydropower project along the river.

Nepal is still trying to recover from catastrophic floods and landslides that swept through its border towns with Tibet two months ago, wiping out thousands of houses, destroying critical energy infrastructure and leaving thousands dead and missing.

More on this story.

News.title: Wildlife park remains closed after fatal tiger attack
News.content:
Yorkshire Wildlife Park remains closed after a man climbed into a tiger enclosure and was fatally attacked by the animal.

Emergency services were called to the park near Doncaster, South Yorkshire, at about 13:30 BST on Saturday after reports of a man climbing down into the enclosure from a walkway.

An eyewitness described seeing the man wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. Police said the man sadly died at the scene.

A park spokesperson said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" remain with the man's family and confirmed the Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

The spokesperson says many people had contacted them about the tiger and he was safe and well.

Staff who were at the scene who were "deeply affected by events" would receive specialist support, they added.

South Yorkshire Police said the man's family were being supported by officers. "Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time," the force said in a statement.

It added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."

Earlier on Saturday, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".

News.title: UK does not support Trump's Russia diesel deal, says Streeting
News.content:
The UK does not support Donald Trump's deal with Vladimir Putin, which would see the US purchase millions of tonnes of diesel from Russia, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has said.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Broadcasting House, he said the agreement had been done in the context of the US president facing elections in November and at a time when politicians across the world were under pressure to ease the cost of living.

He argued that the US and other allies should focus on increasing pressure on Russia to shorten the war "and to secure Ukraine's freedom".

Trump's diesel deal is aimed at lowering fuel prices in America, which have risen following the US and Israel's conflict with Iran.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the agreement would allow Moscow to raise funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

In response, Trump suggested Ukraine should "get a new leader" who could reach a deal with Russia to end the long-running conflict between the two countries.

Streeting said it was a matter for Ukrainians to choose their leader but added that the country was "fortunate to have someone of his calibre, his courage and his integrity leading their war effort".

He added that responsibility for the war "lies squarely and solely with President Putin and his imperialist ambitions".

The defence secretary said it was not the first time there had been public disagreements between Washington and Kyiv, adding: "In these situations we see it as our role and our responsibility to try and bring our friends back together again."

He also sought to emphasise the US's support for Ukraine, saying there was "often an understatement" of how much help they had provided.

"We're seeing US support for Ukraine in a number of ways from the provision of weapons - and we do a lot of procurement through the Americans - through to intelligence support and through the diplomatic initiative that Washington is leading."

News.title: Three friends on their student debt: One paid off, one chipping away and one creeping up
News.content:
When Lizzy, Libby and Charlotte met as freshers in 2012, their main responsibility was making it to lectures on time after early morning sports practice.

Their student debt, growing with interest from the day they took out their loans, was the last thing on their minds.

"The conversation was just so much less relevant at that time," says Charlotte. "As our careers have gone on and our paths have diverged more and more... those conversations start to come more to the forefront."

The friends, now in their early 30s, went to the University of Newcastle in the same year tuition fees tripled to Â£9,000 a year in England and Wales, and new loans called Plan 2 were introduced. Each borrowed about Â£37,500 to cover three years of tuition and living costs.

This year marks a decade since the first students in their year started repaying.

They may have started out in the same position, but over that time their career trajectories, life choices and earnings have shaped how much they've repaid, how much interest they've racked up, and how much they owe - with very different outcomes.

Student loans have come under scrutiny this year and there's been a particular backlash over Plan 2 loans. The government has said it wants to make the whole system fairer and campaigners are waiting to see what, if anything, changes in this month's Budget.

News.title: Inside the room: What it was like to be with Blackpink's Lisa as race scandal erupted
News.content:
What's it like to be the main character of an online scandal?

That's one of the questions raised in a new documentary about Lisa Manobal â one quarter of K-pop phenomenon Blackpink and a breakout star of TV show The White Lotus.

The film captures an unfolding controversy, as leaked videos show Blackpink using racial slurs when they were teenage trainees in the K-pop system.

The clips, which emerged last year, showed the band covering US rap songs during rehearsals. Explicit language, including the n-word, was left uncensored.

The scandal blew up while Lisa was rehearsing for a pivotal performance at the Coachella Festival in 2025.

Offended and upset, some fans demanded an apology - but the band's record label, forbade the members from issuing a statement.

With Lisa's team in crisis mode, documentarian Sue Kim followed Lisa into her dressing room.

"I said, 'Look, I know this is new. I know you guys are wildly confused and hurt, but this is your time to say whatever you want to say - even if you're just processing your thoughts and telling us what you're feeling," Kim tells the BBC.

The film-maker "honestly expected her to say no".

Instead, Lisa lay down on a sofa and spoke from the heart.

"It's bad," the singer says in the documentary, with a mixture of shame and nerves.

Lisa explains she was "15 or 16" when the videos were shot and "didn't know that [word] was sensitive because I'm from Thailand and my first language is not English".

Having only heard the term in rap music, she was unaware of its offensive history.

"Now I would never ever do that because, now, I've got education," she says. "Now I know better.

"But I did wrong."

It is a vulnerable and human response - and nothing like the scripted PR apology you might expect. (Lisa has since apologised publicly, external in an interview with Variety, although some people remained unconvinced, external).

Kim says Lisaâs in-the-moment reaction is "one of the most important scenes" in her documentary, Always Lalisa, which hits cinemas on Monday, 12 October.

"There was no premeditation on Lisa's part, there was no media training," she adds.

"I asked her one question and she just talked for an hour, and everything came out, and it's all stream of consciousness.

"And what you see with Lisa in that moment is so genuine, it's impossible not to feel compassion for her."

News.title: AI is creating a 'human premium' for art made by people, but will it hold?
News.content:
The music platform Deezer says 44% of tracks uploaded to it are AI-generated. Its research also found that 97% of listeners couldn't tell what was AI-generated and what wasn't. But here's a third statistic: more than half of those surveyed said they did care if it was made by AI. They want humans to be involved.

Daniel Susskind, an economics professor at King's College London, says many of us place huge value on the human role in making art. It's what makes the creative process different from more functional, practical tasks, he thinks.

"I was once in a room of accountants, and one of them stood up and said, 'My clients come to me for the personal touch, the human process'," he remembers. "And I said, 'That isn't why they come to you, they come because they want their taxes done properly'."

But it's different with art, he says. "If I walk into the Sistine Chapel and look at the ceiling, I think not only is that extraordinarily beautiful, but isn't it amazing that a human hand, flesh and blood like my own, came up with that. A mind like mine dreamt that up," he says.

As Susskind describes it, what we value isn't just the destination, it's the knowledge that a human - one of us - got us there. We can wonder at that achievement.

News.title: Young men live in fear of being snatched off the streets and sold to Myanmar's army
News.content:
You do not stay out after dark if you're young and able-bodied in Hpa-An, the capital of Myanmar's southern Karen state. In recent months this has become conventional wisdom.

But Zaw Min has no choice.

"I worry, but I have to go out to work," says the 26-year-old tuk tuk driver, who asked that his real name be omitted out of fear for his safety. "My family call me all the time and remind me not to drive passengers too far; to be careful who I take as a passenger... I have to be vigilant all the time.

"People are panicked and frightened," he explains. "Some people I know have been taken."

Locals say plain-clothed members and supporters of the Myanmar junta have been roaming the streets of Hpa-An, arbitrarily arresting people in their teens, 20s and 30s and forcing them into military service.

According to leaked documents seen by BBC Burmese, authorities have been ordered to aggressively fulfil the military's recruitment quotas across jurisdictions, bolstering the junta's ranks as it endures a war of attrition against ethnic militias, pro-democracy groups and civilian-led resistance movements.

Zaw Min is the only one among his siblings who is at the age of recruitment. Many other "kids" his age have fled, he says â to Thailand, or the homes of relatives further afield. Those who remain are often under strict instructions from their parents: be home before dusk.

Myanmar has been locked in a bloody civil war since February 2021, when its own military launched a coup d'etat and ousted democratically elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Three years later, following a string of humiliating losses, plummeting morale and soaring rates of desertion, the junta enacted a mandatory conscription law that required all men aged 18 to 35 and women aged 18 to 27 to serve at least two years under military command. Those who refuse face up to five years in prison.

The enactment of the law "represents one of the most severe and impactful actions taken against the entire civilian population since the military coup", according to Maj Naung Yoe, military affairs official at the Myanmar Defense and Security Institute (MDSI) and a former military officer who defected and joined the anti-coup Civil Disobedience Movement.

News.title: MPs seek to overturn ruling that stops police being sued for failings
News.content:
Backbench MPs are seeking to roll back a court ruling they say will have "devastating consequences" for victims of crime by preventing them taking legal action against the police, even when there have been grave investigative failings.

The 2025 Court of Appeal judgment, which applies to England and Wales, held that police officers are immune from civil litigation both in their role as witnesses, and for conduct or statements they make when carrying out criminal investigations.

Conservative Andrew Mitchell and Labour's Jess Phillips have submitted an amendment to a bill being debated in Parliament next week seeking to counteract the ruling.

Separately, the judgment could also be overturned at a Supreme Court appeal this month.

The MPs are seeking to stop immunity applying, including in cases where police have fabricated evidence, been dishonest or negligent, and where there has been a reckless disclosure of confidential information relating to victims.

The ruling came in a case brought by a victim of serious domestic violence who fled her abuser for a secret refuge, but Sussex Police included her new address in a file sent to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) without sufficiently flagging its confidentiality.

A CPS lawyer subsequently disclosed her address in court during a bail hearing, thereby revealing it to her abuser. As a result, she had to flee again.

The woman said the disclosure of her address had meant the place she was supposed to be safe "no longer felt safe at all" and she was still living with the impact of what happened and that loss of security.

She brought claims against both the police and CPS, arguing their failure placed her in fear for her life, compelled her to leave her home, caused her to suffer loss of earnings, and resulted in her developing a psychiatric injury. Her claims were initially rejected, reinstated on appeal, then struck out again.

The key issue was who could be held legally responsible for what happened, and who would benefit from legal immunity. Witnesses and lawyers have what is known as "core immunity" for things they say in court, so that they can speak freely there.

The Court of Appeal ruling further expanded such immunity, holding that it extends to an extremely broad range of police activity, including conduct or statements which are part of an investigation leading to a potential prosecution

Most types of legal claim are thus blocked by this immunity, including cases about serious human rights abuses and data breaches, and there are no exemptions for unjustifiable conduct.

Officers can still be prosecuted in the criminal courts and held accountable by police misconduct processes.

News.title: UK launches flood taskforce to prepare for extreme winter weather
News.content:
The government has launched a new taskforce to respond to extreme weather, including the risk of flooding this winter.

After a summer of record-breaking temperatures, the group will meet this week to assess how prepared the UK is for what the Met Office described as the "heightened potential" for wet, windy, stormy weather in the coming months.

"We're facing extreme weather, with flood and drought intertwined but the government is taking decisive action," Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) Minister Emma Hardy said in a statement ahead of the meeting.

The Environment Agency has warned approximately 6.3 million homes and businesses in England remain at risk of flooding.

Defra will host the first meeting on Wednesday, bringing together the Met Office, Environment Agency and mayoral authorities as well as the farming, water and insurance industries.

Hardy said: "This will put communities and businesses at the heart of our work and will make sure the UK is ready for whatever the weather brings next."

The government has committed at least Â£10.5bn until 2036 to protect homes, businesses and critical infrastructure from the growing threat of flooding.

The Met Office has said the current seasonal outlook suggests an increased likelihood of wetter than average conditions during autumn, in part due to the El NiÃ±o weather event.

It has warned that this year's iteration of the climate phenomenon is likely to be the strongest in living memory, with the peak not expected until the end of the year.

The Environment Agency has said that while flooding is not guaranteed, the odds of repeated storms, prolonged rain and saturated catchments are higher than average this winter.

It has urged households to check their flood risk, sign up to alerts and make a flood plan to prepare for any emergencies.

The warnings follow 12 months of extreme weather across the UK, with the summer of 2026 the country's hottest on record.

Last winter brought four named storms to the UK - Bram, Goretti, Ingrid and Chandra - and several significant flooding events, with the Met Office reporting that England received 42% more rainfall than its winter average.

News.title: Northern Lights dazzles skies across the UK
News.content:
Residents across the UK were left stunned as the sky was illuminated by the spectacular colours of the Northern Lights on Friday and Saturday evenings.

The natural phenomenon, known as the Aurora Borealis, is the result of increased solar activity.

Such occurrences are mostly visible near the Arctic Circle and northern Scotland, but particularly strong activity levels meant they could be seen across Wales and as far south as Devon, Hampshire and Kent on Saturday night.

The Met Office has said sightings could continue to be possible during clear skies until Tuesday.

News.title: Worker paralysed in 30ft fall from pylon gets £10m payout
News.content:
A maintenance worker whose life was "turned upside down" when he fell 30ft from a power line and was left paralysed has won at least Â£10m in compensation.

Gavin Pugh was dismantling a pylon in April 2022 when he unknowingly clipped his safety line to a section that was only secure at one end.

His safety rope slipped loose, causing him to plunge to the ground and suffer life-changing injuries to his brain, neck, shoulder, ribs and internal organs which mean he needs a wheelchair for the rest of his life.

Pugh, who was 33 at the time, sued his employer, Wood Transmission and Distribution Ltd, after the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) found "adequate safety arrangements" had not been in place.

News.title: Man, 36, arrested six years on from double murder
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the fatal shooting of two men more than six years ago.

Junior Ajose, 36, and Cheriff Tall, 21, were shot dead at a lockdown party in the Moss Side area of Manchester in the early hours of 21 June 2020.

A Greater Manchester Police (GMP) spokesperson said a 36-year-old man was detained in Turkey and transported back to England on Saturday, where he was met at Stansted Airport by GMP officers. He remains in custody.

Det Ch Insp Neil Higginson from the force's major incident team said: "This arrest demonstrates our unwavering commitment to securing justice for Junior and Cheriff and their loved ones."

"Over the last six years, myself and my officers have been carrying out multiple warrants, analysing evidence, examining devices that have been seized during the investigation and pursuing every opportunity to identify those responsible," he added.

Ajose and Tall, who did not know each other, were both shot in the head in a car park off Caythorne Street shortly before 01:00 BST and died in hospital.

GMP said it was estimated that between 300 and 400 people were present in the car park that night.

The force issued a further appeal for information on the fifth anniversary of their deaths last year.

Higginson said they were continuing to appeal for information that could help them to establish the full circumstances of what happened that night and to identify any outstanding suspects.

A Â£50,000 reward remains available for key information that leads to the conviction of the killer.

News.title: Russo named England player of the year
News.content:
Forward Alessia Russo has been named England women's player of the year.

The 27-year-old, who also won the award two seasons ago, has been a key player in the 2025-26 campaign, featuring in all 10 games and scoring five goals.

Last week she scored the third goal as England beat Greece 3-1 in their 2027 World Cup play-off semi-final first leg.

Arsenal's Russo pipped Chelsea pair Lucy Bronze and Hannah Hampton to the award, which is voted for by fans.

"To receive the award is really special, particularly as it comes directly from the fans. I am so grateful for their support," said Russo.

"A big thank you also to my team-mates - it is always about the collective."

England host Greece in the second leg at Leicester's King Power Stadium on Tuesday.

News.title: Lost monastery masonry may have been reused for hospital's drain
News.content:
The culvert once drained waste water from King James VI Hospital, which was built around 1749-1750 and was converted into flats in the 1970s.

The drain was discovered during the dig in a grassy open space at the former hospital.

Covering the top of the drain were flat stones, which are believed to be medieval masonry.

Archaeologist Dr Gavin Lindsay told BBC Scotland News: "You can see clear chisel marks from when they had been worked very carefully to create these beautiful smooth sides.

"They are clearly far more elaborate, and far more effort had gone into their production, than you would do for a drain in the 1700s."

The selection of masonry also include stone floor slabs.

Dr Lindsay said a stone mason who visited the dig suggested the slabs' smooth surfaces were the result of people walking on them over many years.

"Possibly by many monks' feet, and to push it a bit further, maybe King James's feet had been across it," said the archaeologist.

News.title: Woman racially abused at work by boys awarded £15k
News.content:
A black council worker who was subjected to "serious racial abuse" and faced with "dismissive" managers after she complained has been awarded Â£15,000.

The woman was an intervention worker in West Berkshire Council's Youth Justice Support Team when two boys inflicted the abuse in April 2024.

An authority manager "clearly felt that absorbing that kind of abuse simply 'went with the territory'", an employment tribunal concluded.

A West Berkshire Council spokesperson said it "respects the findings of the tribunal and will reflect carefully on the points raised".

The worker joined the council in July 2023 before she resigned in June 2024.

When she complained to managers about the racial abuse, they were found to have focused on her response after she referred to them as "little boys".

The tribunal found she had suffered "severe provocation" and that the council "failed to recognise the seriousness and unpleasantness of the [boys'] racial abuse".

David McMullen, who helped the woman in her case as a senior organiser for the GMB union, said she was "treated horrendously in the first instance and this was further compounded by management at West Berkshire Council".

He added: "Racism has no place in society at all and certainly workers should not have to face this treatment when at work â in fact it is the job of employers to protect against such abuse."

The West Berkshire Council spokesperson added: "The safety and wellbeing of our staff is extremely important to us.

"We do not accept abuse, discrimination or harassment directed towards our employees and we are committed to supporting colleagues when incidents occur."

News.title: Liverpool dealt blow for Man City clash with Dominik Szoboszlai injury
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Liverpool were dealt another blow on the eve of their Premier League clash with Manchester City as Dominik Szoboszlai wasn’t named in the matchday squad.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola did not name Szoboszlai as an injury doubt during Friday’s press conference but concerns over his fitness were raised when he was not spotted at the team’s hotel on Sunday morning.

His absence is due to a hamstring injury which puts him on the sidelines alongside Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Hugo Ekititke and leaves Liverpool short of six key players.

Such is the nature of their injury-hit squad that 21-year-old Lewis Koumas makes his first start for the Reds and will lead the line against City who have won each of their five league matches this season.

Of Liverpool’s growing injury list, Iraola said on Friday: "Cody [Gakpo] has an ankle injury. He has had some before in his career and it's a matter of him dealing with the pain because when you twist your ankle... it was a really bad tackle, I think. He is doing things individually but [he is] not ready for Sunday.

"And Alex [Isak] has a thigh injury. It's a small injury but it's a muscle injury. The same [as Gakpo], whenever he feels ready. They both don't look like long term – we will be analysing day to day. But they are not going to arrive on Sunday."

open image in gallery Lewis Koumas starts up front for Liverpool as Dominik Szoboszlai is out with a hamstring injury ( Getty )

Iraola was asked whether Koumas would start the game but he remained coy and explained that there is enough depth in Liverpool’s squad for options.

He added: "Even before, we don't have Hugo Ekitike, who is another very good striker that I'm looking forward to having available also.

"We don't have Hugo, we don't have Alex. We will maybe recover Fede Chiesa but he hasn't played any minutes. He is recovering from an injury but he has been doing a good job in the international break, he has been training with the small group we had.

"A full No.9, it's true that we probably only have [Lewis] Koumas right now, but we have some other options. We have some wingers that have played up front in other teams.

"I think we will put an XI with a level enough to compete for that game."

News.title: Voices: The terrifying prospect of President Pete Hegseth
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For a country embroiled in a lengthy and escalating war with Iran, America has just provided a bizarre tribute to the rule of murderous mullahs in Tehran and Afghan Taliban’s thirst for bloody public executions. It is dreadful company to keep – and yet there are hard-boiled reasons why Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, should take this appalling risk with his country's reputation

Announcing the prospect of the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a military psychiatrist radicalised to Islamism who murdered 13 people at the Ford Hood army base in 2009 and maimed many more, Hegseth was clear that part of the appeal of this solution is that it will be livestreamed – a prospect which has discomfited even avid supporters of the death penalty, concerned about the brutalizing effect on those watching.

Army chiefs themselves were caught off guard. Vice President JD Vance also indicated that he would look away and cast doubt on whether the execution, slated for early December would go ahead in the form proposed by Hegseth – his rival for the post-Trump crown.

The plan to publicly gun down Hasan, wheel-chair bound as the consequence of injuries sustained as military police fired on him during his killing spree, has unleashed revulsion across and beyond the US. Less attention has been given to Hegseth’s rationale in provoking an internal conflict of Maga-world political manoeuvring.

A brash but often thin-skinned figure in his mid-forties, Hegseth is best understood as the man who wants to be seen to be Maga to the max – and the next generation of its leaders, with an eye to a run for the White House in 2028. And like many interactions of the Trump administration with core US institutions, he has also had a keen eye for pre-existing weak spots – like the tendency of diversity initiatives to end up in bureaucratic and legal processes which commanders found distracting or counter-productive.

It is, however, now a distraction from the bigger concern that the US’s fighting strength and technological capability is dangerously under-powered. The promise of amping up the American war machine, drained by the Iraq crisis and the humiliating retreat from Afghanistan, has not been delivered – Hegseth has, by common assent of those who know him around the Pentagon, little expert understanding of the vast institution he leads.

Instead, his relationship with Trump is based on his prominence as a Maga advocate on the most right-leaning parts of the Fox News programming inserted into the top job as a message carrier. He only just passed confirmation hearings after details of an erratic private life; allegations of sexual assault and episodes of excessive drinking were laid bare. In the end, the casting vote of the vice president, VD Vance sealed his appointment – but Hegseth’s tenure has always felt vulnerable.

Especially so, now that war in Iran and its failure to make headway, promoting Trump to pivot hard towards Moscow to secure a symbolic amount of diesel supplies from Vladimir Putin, can be laid at his door. The deadly attack on Riyadh airport as Houthi rebels take advantage of the chaos in the Straits of Hormuz also underlines the weaknesses of the US position.

Had the US remained focussed on its defensive role and protection of its allies in Saudi Arabia, the Houthi threat should have been manageable. Now it is out of control.

Hegseth speaks relatively little about the Gulf, other than in general terms, and a lot of about other things, such as refighting culture against “weirdos, beardoes” and “trannies” in the US miliary long after transgender people have been told they cannot serve in the military and exemptions for facial hair rules have been imposed already by the top brass.

It beats talking about real challenges the administration is struggling to grasp. The execution plan is a risk he has taken in the run up to punishing midterm elections – and it is no accident that Ford Hood, a Texas military base in a state which hangs the balance for Republicans and Democrats spy a potential victory, is at the centre of this story. Getting out the biggest chunk of “red meat” for voters would be seen by Trump as a success for Hegseth, if things go his way in November.

If, however, the President is left under pressure by losing control of Congress, a result even he will struggle to spin as a success, and Democrats gain more levers to investigate a wayward presidency, one senior military attaché to a European country tells me, “I would not want to be in Hegseth’s shoes in this scenario. Trump will look for someone to blame if he gets bad results there – and his is the number he will call.”

Trump surely has form in sacking those he previously anointed as close allies in the Maga movement – most recently a previous favourite Pam Bondi as the attorney general, when he feels that their problems have infected his popularity.

While Hegseth is still looking for space to define himself as one of a small group of candidates who could conceivably succeed Trump, that does not mean that he will make the final cut. He might just as easily take the rap for failures – that would essentially be a victory for his Vance, the Veep whose aim is to be the one and only crown prince.

A desperate gimmick shows how thin the Hegseth power prospectus really is. An unscrupulous showman prepared to drag the US military down to the level of its worse enemies around the globe is fighting for prominence at the expense of his country’s reputation. Yet Maga is a snakes and ladders world – and big gambles can have massive forfeits.

Anne McElvoy is executive editor at POLITICO and co-host of “Politics at Sam and Anne’s”
