News.title: Saudi Arabia goes on alert, ex-aide testifies in Netanyahu trial, and other Mideast developments
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Israel’s former attorney general took the witness stand Sunday in corruption cases against Benjamin Netanyahu, as the political future of the country's longest-serving prime minister hangs in the balance, with national elections just weeks away.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, was on high alert after a deadly attack on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, allegedly by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Saturday. Read our full coverage here.

Former legal adviser testifies in Netanyahu's corruption case

Israel's former attorney general took the witness stand Sunday in Netanyahu's long-running corruption trial.

Avichai Mandelblit indicted the prime minister seven years ago for fraud, breach of trust and accepting bribes. The charges were the first-ever against a sitting Israeli prime minister.

Netanyahu was seated in the courtroom to hear Mandelblit testify. The prime minister handpicked Mandelblit, his former Cabinet secretary, for the attorney general job. His tenure ended in 2022.

“The truth comes to light,” Netanyahu said before entering the courtroom.

Netanyahu has been accused of offering or exchanging favors with wealthy associates and media moguls for political gain. He denies any wrongdoing.

The latest proceedings come weeks before national elections.

Saudi on high-alert after deadly attack, Houthi warn of new strikes

Saudi Arabia kept its main international airport closed and moved Riyadh schools online on Sunday after a deadly strike by Yemen’s Houthi rebels the day before.

The rebels threatened new airstrikes across the kingdom after a missile attack on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 on Saturday. The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for that, but claimed two previous deadly attacks on the Riyadh airport earlier in the week.

Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, the Houthis' military spokesperson, urged “everyone to take our warnings seriously.”

The airport strike marked a major escalation in the war between the Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom, and further complicated sputtering efforts to halt the U.S.-Iran war.

U.S. President Donald Trump said he was considering whether to join Saudi strikes against the rebels, a scenario that could prompt the Houthis to halt shipping through a crucial waterway and further restrict the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf.

Gaza residents return to rubble as strikes continue amid ceasefire

Residents in central Gaza returned home Sunday morning to assess the damage caused by Israeli strikes after they had been warned to evacuate the buildings the day before.

Bassam Abed said that at least 10 residences housing some 300 families were reduced to rubble. He said families were not given enough time to flee before the military struck their buildings.

“Women slept outdoors. We did not take clothes,” Abed said.

The Israeli military said it had targeted militant infrastructure, including three weapons storage facilities, a rocket launch site and a command center used by Hamas militants to carry out attacks on Israeli soldiers.

The strikes fell one year after Israel and Hamas reached a ceasefire deal, but Israel continues to launch near-daily strikes.

Trump officially lifts ban on direct flight to Lebanon

The White House has officially lifted a decades-old ban on direct flight between the U.S. and Lebanon, following through on a commitment President Donald Trump made in July.

U.S. carriers may be reticent to begin offering flight to Lebanon soon, however, as the war with Iran continues to disrupts air traffic in the region and questions over Hezbollah’s influence in parts of the country persist. Direct flights between the two countries were suspended in 1985 by the Reagan administration after the hijacking of TWA Flight 847.

The Lebanese embassy in Washington said on social media that it welcomed the move as “a major step toward resuming direct flights.”

The U.S. embassy in Beirut said the change would make it easier for family members to visit one another and for American businesses to invest in Lebanon. “We look forward to working with our Lebanese partners to turn this opportunity into a reality,” the statement added.

News.title: Saturday Night Live skewers Pete Hegseth and RFK in cold open: ‘The only man who snorts more rhino horn than me’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Saturday Night Live is taking aim at Pete Hegseth and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. with the sketch show’s latest cold open.

Wearing a belt stocked with mini bottles of Fireball Cinnamon Whiskey, Colin Jost reprised his role as the secretary of war at the start of Saturday’s new episode to spoof the long-deployed USS Abraham Lincoln’s recent return home.

“You’re back home safe in sunny San Diego, which the president just asked Iran to blow up,” Jost’s Hegseth said. He then went on to catch the sailors up to speed on what they missed while they were away, “in case you immediately want to head back to sea.”

“In December, as we get into the Christmas spirit, we're going to execute a guy in a wheelchair on live TV,” he said, referring to the U.S. military’s scheduled execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan in December.

“That's right, public executions are back, kind of like Scrubs,” he deadpanned, adding that if a prisoner survives an execution, he will fight boxer Jake Paul.

open image in gallery Colin Jost plays Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on 'Saturday Night Live' ( SNL )

open image in gallery Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been criticized over his decision to livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan ( AFP/Getty )

Next, Hegseth revealed the Department of War’s new emblem, which has drawn comparisons to Nazi imagery, and admitted it has a “Nazi vibe.”

He then brought out Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., played by James Austin Johnson, introducing him as “the only guy who snorts more rhino horn than me.”

“I’m happy to report that America is healthier than ever,” Johnson’s Kennedy started in his signature strained voice. “That’s why I would officially like to rename cold and flu season to cold and flu and listeria and measles and trench brain season.”

open image in gallery Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is the secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery James Austin Johnson played Robert F. Kennedy Jr. during the cold open ( SNL )

He addressed recent food recalls by telling sailors that meats like catfish, pony and cricket were tested on them, declaring: “The research you provided on Operation Hell Cruise will be vital for years to come.”

Hegseth then returned and closed out his speech to the sailors by quoting Linkin Park’s song “In the End.”

“You tried so hard and got so far, but in the end it doesn’t even matter,” he sang. He then thanked the crew for their willingness to go down with the ship, which goes against his “personal rule of never going down on anyone.”

The ‘Weekend Update’ co-host — who has appeared as a rowdy caricature of Hegseth on the sketch series for nearly a year — concluded the cold open by introducing the rest of the show, which featured comedian Shane Gillis and musical guest Rosalía.

News.title: Egypt’s Fayoum mummy portraits to travel abroad for first time after restoration
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Egypt unveiled Sunday a restored version of the “Tondo of the Two Brothers,” a prized 2nd-century painting from the famed Fayoum portraits.

Specialists from Rome worked alongside conservators from the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir — where the collection is usually kept — for three weeks to restore the artwork, officials said at a press conference.

Fayoum mummy portraits were painted primarily on thin wooden panels and placed over the faces of the deceased within mummy wrappings, combining Egyptian funerary traditions with artistic influences from the wider Greco-Roman world.

Egypt will lend a major part of the collection to a temporary exhibition in Rome, marking the first time it will travel abroad.

“The restoration of the Tondo of the Two Brothers is an important example of what can be achieved through international cooperation in the preservation and study of cultural heritage,” said Sherif Fathy, Egypt’s minister of tourism and antiquities. “Egypt and Italy share deep historical and cultural ties, and this project brings together Egyptian and Italian expertise to preserve an exceptional work of art for future generations.”

Experts describe the painting as unusual because of its circular shape and its depiction of two people instead of one, and rank it among the most vivid surviving portraits from Roman-era Egypt. It was painted using a technique in which pigments are mixed with molten wax, and restorers were able to recover the features of the brother on the right.

Aly Abdel Halim, director general of the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir, said the conservation required careful intervention because both the wooden support, damaged by termites, and the painted surface were fragile.

The portraits will be featured in an exhibition in Rome from November to May 2027.

Tomaso Radaelli, chairman of MondoMostre, the exhibition’s organizer, said it will bring together more than 110 objects, including painted panels, funerary shrouds, masks, marble portraits, plaster casts and ancient jewelry.

News.title: How to watch Liverpool v Manchester City as City return to action after guilty verdict
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Liverpool host Manchester City in the blockbuster fixture of the Premier League weekend with events off the pitch equally as intriguing as the contest to take place on it.

City head to Anfield expecting the most hostile of receptions following the verdict of an independent commission which found the club guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period. The judgment found that City benefitted from more than £900m of disguised funding between 2009 and 2018 where they won three top-flight titles including one against Liverpool who finished second.

The Reds fans have already been preparing to welcome City’s squad with animosity and Enzo Maresca will have a tricky task on his hand to keep the focus on the match. The City manager admitted to having ‘complete trust’ in the club who have launched an appeal against the verdict.

City come into the match with five wins from five and sit top of the table. Liverpool are six points behind them and can close the gap with victory this afternoon.

Here’s everything you need to know:

When is Liverpool vs Man City?

The blockbuster Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Manchester City is due to kick off at 4.30pm BST on Sunday 11 October at Anfield, Liverpool.

How can I watch it?

Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League with broadcast coverage beginning at 4pm.

Sky subscribers can also stream the match live via the SkyGo app.

Team news

Andoni Iraola is without his main attacking threats as Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo will miss the match through injury. Hugo Ekitike is also missing while Dominik Szoboszlai has been left out of the squad.

For Man City, Phil Foden will miss the game due to a suspension but Nico O’Reilly, who left the England camp with a knock during the international break, is fit to start, as is Erling Haaland.

Confirmed line-ups

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Gravenberch; Munoz, Wirtz, Koumas; Barcola.

Man City XI: Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guéhi, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernández; Ndiaye, Cherki, Semenyo; Haaland.

News.title: Verstappen cruises to Singapore Grand Prix victory as Hamilton apologises for strategy error
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli, third: “It was a very tough race out there but really happy with a podium at the end, I managed to take advantage of the fight between Lewis and Lando. To take P3 is a great result from the team, very happy with that.”

He is told that he can clinch the title at the next race:

“Can I, really? Let’s not worry about that. Let’s try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job.”

Charles Leclerc, second: “We were quite strong at the beginning of the race and then we started degrading at the end of the first stint. I pushed a lot at the beginning of the last stint and then degraded a bit more than the others. I gave it all and I don’t regret anything.

“I don’t think there’s anything more we could do but be a bit more aggressive at the start. It’s true that we brought some small new parts to the car which maybe helped us to do a little step forward but it’s enough. Today I think we had a good pace overall.”

Max Verstappen, winner: “It’s taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. Very happy to win here. You always try to do your best and luckily [the start] it was just good enough.

“I think the last few races have been really positive for us. It’s great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try to deliver even more results... hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”

News.title: Three tasks to get your home ready for autumn, according to a professional cleaner
News.content:
When I was sweating away this summer, I never thought the weather would turn, but it’s almost time to crank up our radiators and crack out the big duvet.

They’re the tasks no one likes doing, but luckily for you, I’ve worked as a cleaner for more than a decade. I’ve discovered some shortcuts to make the hated jobs that bit easier.

Tip one: Keep your summer duvet fresh in storage

If, like me, you want to get your winter duvet out, your summer one needs to be cleaned and packed away to keep it fresh come spring.

News.title: Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs
News.content:
The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

News.title: Guimaraes looks a £75m bargain as ‘super sub’ makes difference
News.content:
Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.

When you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

We brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”

This year’s winners are as follows:

Black British Business Person of the Year: Ije Nwokorie, chief executive of Dr Martens

Arts and Media Rising Star: Sheniece Charway, artist partnership manager [EMEA], YouTube/Google

Arts and Media Senior Leader: Amie Parker-Williams, director, digital commissioning and production, Paramount

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

Sports.title: ‘Dragging the game through the gutter’ – Jamie Carragher fears Man City will damage football with ‘appeal after appeal’
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE CARRAGHER fears Manchester City could drag football “through the gutter” if they continue appealing their guilty verdict over financial rule breaches.

The Liverpool legend launched a direct attack on City’s wealthy owners – The City Football Group, led by Sheikh Mansour, and questioned whether they would ever accept defeat in their legal battle.



City were found guilty of 114 of 115 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

But the reigning league leaders have maintained their innocence and lodged an appeal against the verdict.



And Carragher fears the drawn-out saga could cause lasting damage to English football.

Carragher was speaking on Sky Sports ahead of City’s clash with Liverpool – the Cityzen’s first game since being found guilty – alongside City legend Micah Richards, Daniel Sturridge and Roy Keane.



He said: “I think it’s very difficult for the Manchester City owners to continue in their position, because they’re so powerful, they’re so rich.

“They’ve never been told no before in their lives.”

The former England defender also insisted City’s owners must recognise the club is bigger than them.

He added: “Manchester City have been there 100 years before, and they’ll be there 100 years after. Amazing supporters, great players before, great players after.”



But Richards challenged Carragher, questioning what would happen if City won their lodged appeal.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carragher responded: “But they’ll lose the appeal and they’ll appeal again. They keep appealing and they keep appealing.

“And what that will do is, that will just keep dragging the game through the gutter.”

He continued: “This could go on for years, and I think it’s not just gonna ruin Manchester City while this ownership is involved, it’ll ruin the game.”

City, who face Liverpool at Anfield, have insisted the commission’s findings contain serious errors and vowed to clear their name through the appeals process.

Sports.title: ‘I put my neck on the line for club’ – Emotional Micah Richards ‘devastated’ as he urges Man City: Show us the evidence
Sports.content:
Next

MICAH RICHARDS has admitted that Manchester City’s guilty verdict left him “devastated”.

And the ex-City defender went on to plead with club bosses to reveal their “irrefutable evidence” of innocence to suffering supporters.



Man City have been found guilty of more than 100 of the 130 charges levelled against them by the Premier League.

The charges, which date between 2009 and 2018, could carry heavy sanctions including points deductions, a transfer ban and even EXPULSION from the Prem.



City bosses have strongly maintained their innocence and quickly launched an appeal.

Richards, 38, came through City’s academy and played for their first team 245 times between 2005 and 2015.

During this spell he won a Prem title and FA Cup, although these achievements have now come under the microscope following the charges.

Asked for his reaction to City’s guilty verdict, Richards said on Sky Sports: “I feel devastated. More because of what the fans have had to go through and endure over this period.

“Me going through the Man City academy, going there when I was 14. All the noise around Man City – what should happen, what shouldn’t happen – and I put my neck on the line for this club.

“They’ve given me this amazing opportunity to go all the way through the academy and then break into the first team.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“My dream was to win the FA Youth Cup. I missed out on that. Then I won the FA Cup, move on to the Premier League.

“For that to be in question now is very confusing. You’ve got one side saying there’s charges. You’ve got Man City’s side saying they’ve got irrefutable evidence…

“It just leaves a situation for me, the fans, everyone at the club. So devastated.”

Further quizzed if he feels “let down” by club chiefs, Richards added: “I feel let down by the fact it dragged on so long. The fact that Man City talked about this evidence, and if they have this evidence, I want to see it, make it easier for the fans, because they’re the last to know about everything.

“But us as players, what could we possibly do? We go out on the pitch, we give 100 per cent. I’ve literally got one knee giving 100 per cent for Manchester City Football Club, that’s how much I love this club.



“I would do anything for this club because of the opportunity they’ve given me.

“I’m in a difficult situation now where I’m being questioned, whether it be integrity, my medals, or whatever it may be.

“But I know I gave everything, 100 per cent for that club, and that’s all I could’ve done as a player.”



Roy Keane, appearing alongside Richards on Sky Sports, went on to claim that he’d feel “disgusted” if put in a similar situation with Manchester United.

The Irishman, 55, said: “This is not against the players. Micah spoke about growing up and playing for city. This is not against the players or supporters, this is ownership level.

“If you’re trying to win the prizes, you want to do it honestly. You want to look back at your career and go ‘yeah we gave it everything we had, you win some games and lose some games.

“But you can’t be looking back and looking at what City have done, and been found guilty of – I know there’s an appeal.

“But for years we’ve been sitting and praising Man City, saying they’re bringing in amazing players and Pep turning really good players into superstars.



“But the way they were doing it, that is the issue, nothing on the players.

“If I was a player and there were stories coming out about what we were doing at United, I’d be disgusted. I’d be disgusted if here were any sort of dodgy dealings going on or someone cooking the books.

“People think it might be a bit strong, but I wouldn’t feel I’ve earned a league title if there was something dodgy going on in the background, absolutely not.

“We talk about lads going out and giving there all, picking up injuries, but that is your job, that is what you’re supposed to do.

“You just hope everyone else is on the same page – everyone else has been honest and trying to do it the proper way.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho refused to take Real Madrid post-match press conference ‘as he was so angry he feared El Clasico ban’
Sports.content:
Next

FURIOUS Jose Mourinho snubbed Real Madrid’s post-match press conference as he feared that Vinicius Junior would be banned for El Clasico.

Referee Isidro Diaz de Mera handed Vinicius a red card in the 72nd minute of their 1-0 win after the 26-year-old pulled the hair of Villarreal‘s Nathan Saliba.



The Real winger looked to have doubled their lead after Yan Diomande’s opener, instead the goal was overturned and he may be given a multi-match ban.

Mourinho had already sprinted onto the pitch to celebrate the second goal before it was disallowed – and his reaction to the decision has been explosive.



And instead of his usual media duties, it was decided that the boss would skip it all.

For the time being, Vinicius, who has apologised to his team-mates, will continue to be suspended for their next game against Sevilla – but the following game is against Barcelona on October 25.



Due to the significance of the rivalry between the two Spanish teams, it is usually all hands on deck.

But if Vinicius is forced to stay away, Hansi Flick’s side may see a real advantage.

Barca currently sit five points clear of Atletico Madrid at the top of the table, with Real one point behind them in third.

Though, fans will have to wait for the verdict from the committee before panicking with a possible, though unlikely, one-match ban on the cards.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Players will receive a one-match ban when they deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity.

Meanwhile, a two or three-match ban arrives when there is no genuine attempt to play the ball, moderate dissent, or unsportsmanlike gestures.

And this distinction will be made from the referee’s official post-match report.

In his match report, Diaz de Mera wrote that Vinicius had been sent off “for pulling an opponent’s hair while the ball was in play, even though the ball was not in dispute between them”.



But given that Vinicius was noted as off the ball, it seems likely that he will be forced to sit out of what would have been his 25th El Clasico.

In a bizarre turn, the Rio-born star has been in a similar situation before following a league incident versus Valencia.

Goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski looked to have pulled Vinicius Jr by his plaits in January last year.

But the 2024 Ballon d’Or runner-up blew a fuse and pushed the keeper, seeing himself get a straight red card.

Sports.title: ‘Seen enough’ – Gary Neville says Man Utd duo can’t play together and blasts ‘get a grip’ ahead of scary run of fixtures
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE has questioned a pair of Manchester United stars following a run of disappointing matches.

The United legend has not been pleased by what he has seen from Michael Carrick‘s men this season.



And that feeling only grew stronger as he watched the Red Devils concede a 92nd-minute equaliser to suffer a draw against ten-man Spurs on Saturday.

It’s safe to say he was not impressed by most of the stars at Old Trafford, but he singled out United’s midfield partnership as an area that has to see a shake-up in the near future.



He said on Gary Neville podcast: “With (Youri) Tielemans and (Kobbie) Mainoo, I think we’ve seen enough of it now.

“I’m not calling time on it because I think that’s probably too drastic – but I’ve seen enough of it to think it’s not dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.



“They are both good players individually but sometimes you have players who just don’t quite knit together and suit each other.

“When (Carlos) Baleba came on with Mainoo, that certainly looked more like there was more energy, but there is going to have to be something done in there and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip.”

That change will have to come as soon as possible, with United currently sat 12th in the Prem standings.

Neville added: “They’re going to Atletico and then to Elland Road, and if you’re not quite right there mentally and physically, you’re going to get found out. If they don’t get going, it’s going to be a worrying few weeks.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Tielemans has been criticised for his lack of mobility, a problem which the entire team have been struggling with.

Their running stats have been damning at times, while the XI has lacked the quality needed to make up for the difference in matches where the other team is willing to put in more effort off the ball.

Neville continued: “What United fans won’t accept is what they deem as a lack of effort and the reality is they’re not running enough, they’re not showing enough tenacity, determination and fighting spirit.



“The boos tell you they are really despondent with what they are watching.

“What we are seeing at the moment is a team that looks like they are curling up in a ball and the club, for some of them right now, is getting a bit big for them.

“The shake of Carrick’s head will be… ‘Are they doing it for me? What’s happening with that lot? Have they lost their confidence? Have they switched off? Are they going under? What is going on? Because these aren’t the players I was working with last season.'”

SOUTHAMPTON and Portsmouth players were involved in a furious on-pitch bust-up after a wild sliding tackle sparked chaos in the South Coast derby.

The Saints beat their bitter rivals 1-0 in what turned into an extremely heated derby.



Tempers boiled over in the 53rd minute of the chaotic Championship clash at St Mary’s.

Finn Azaz raced back before launching himself into a crunching sliding challenge on Portsmouth player Ebou Adams.



The tackle sparked an angry reaction from Pompey’s players, who rushed towards the Southampton star.

Players from both sides became involved in a heated confrontation as pushing and shoving broke out.



Azaz, 26, was eventually shown a yellow card for the challenge, while Portsmouth’s Jayden Meghoma was also booked in the aftermath.

Adams, 30, was central to the action, repeatedly drawing fouls, including the incident that saw Southampton reduced to 10 men following Cameron Bragg’s first-half dismissal.

Bragg, 21, was sent off in the 44th minute after losing possession and pulling back Adams – picking up a second yellow card.

MANCHESTER CITY face a trip to Anfield in their first game following the bombshell news of their guilty verdict.

City were found guilty of all the accusations of financial rule breaches and found the club responsible for “sham” commercial and contract deals adding up to nearly £1billion.



The Etihad outfit have vowed to fight on, with chief executive Ferran Soriano suggesting to European club chiefs the process would still “take a lot more time”.

An unprecedented punishment is looming, with the club potentially heading for relegation or a hefty fine.



The news has sent the footballing world into a tailspin, with several Premier League clubs now wanting compensation for the lost income they suffered at the hands of the Mancunian side.

One of City’s biggest title rivals since they began competing at the summit of the top flight has been Liverpool.

The Reds have been beaten to the Prem title three times by City since their takeover in 2008, including two historic title races between Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp in 2018/19 and 2021/22.

Liverpool fans are expected to create a fiery atmosphere as they welcome the league’s villains to Anfield this weekend, with Gary Neville saying “it will be brutal – a reception like you’ve never seen.”

It will not be the first time tensions have boiled over between the two sides – City’s team bus was attacked as it arrived at the stadium before a Champions League quarter-final in 2018.

In the years that followed, the clashes between Guardiola’s side and Klopp’s Reds became unmissable.



In 2022, Pep was pelted by coins from the stands as he argued with officials over a disallowed goal — while Liverpool condemned ‘vile chants’ from the away end.

Sports.title: ‘Bad look’ – Alan Shearer slams Premier League over Man City punishment delay and warns of Anfield ‘hostility’
Sports.content:
Next

ALAN SHEARER slammed the Premier League for delaying the decision to punish Manchester City following their guilty verdict, saying: That is a bad look for English football.

And the football legend warned Enzo Maresca’s under-fire side that “the level of hostility” among rival fans towards them will “rise” every time they play away this season.



Last month, City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period.

This followed a four-year investigation by the Prem but City have denied any wrongdoing and are appealing the findings.



No sanctions – which could involve a huge points deduction or relegation – have been handed out and this will be addressed separately in a further hearing with an independent Commission.

Yet the longer this goes on, the longer that everyone is in limbo over City’s future.



Shearer – the Premier League’s record scorer – said: “It’s such a bad look that we’re still having to wait for the consequences for what’s going to happen.

“They have been found guilty and the longer it goes on, I just don’t think it’s a good look for the Premier League or football in general.

“We’ve never seen anything like this, the size of it.

“This is the biggest thing to happen to the Premier League since it started in 1992. That’s how big it is.

They were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges – which fit into six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

“Every game and every opposition they play, whether they like it or not, the manager and players are all going to be asked about this question from now, until the sanctions are imposed on them.

“That in itself is not fair on everyone else in the league.

“That’s why I’m really surprised that when they have been found guilty then the sanctions haven’t followed almost immediately.”

City face rivals Liverpool today at Anfield, arguably the worst fixture they could have faced since news of the findings of the independent Commission were announced.

It is likely that every time they travel outside of the Etihad Stadium they will face the wrath of supporters at away grounds.



Former England striker Shearer, 56, said: “The level of hostility will rise wherever they go, I have no doubt about that.

“You get the feeling of what this means. The ramifications are endless to this case.

“I mean credibility matters clearly and you’re not going to get anything different from any coach, any manager, any player at Manchester City.

“Other than ‘we’re going to stick together, we believe in the club and we trust the club’.



“This is very, very different. If they don’t understand it – which I’m sure they do – they’re about to find out the anger from every other club.

“It’s probably unfair on these players that they’re having to answer on this because it’s not their fault.

“But they’re about to find out what everyone else feels, starting with Anfield.

“That’s why it needs sorting out now because they spent a fortune in the summer.

“They’ve won every game so far. That could still be the case in two months, three months, four months. They could end up winning the league.



“That’s why it needs sorting out now because it’s such a bad look if it’s allowed to fester and to continue.”

Sports.title: Ten-man Southampton secure first league derby win since 2004
Sports.content:
Ten-man Southampton secured their first South Coast derby win in the league in over two decades with a 1-0 home victory over Portsmouth.

Saints beat their fierce local rivals 2-1 in the Premier League on November 13 2004, with Kevin Phillips scoring the winner.

And they finally did it again, thanks to James Bree's neat first-half finish, despite playing the entire second half with 10 men following Cameron Bragg's red card.

Image: James Bree scored the winner at St Mary's

Portsmouth looked the more industrious team at the start of only the 35th league meeting in history between these sides - but it was Southampton who broke the deadlock.

Finn Azaz's magnificent ball found Bree, who had easily slipped from the grasp of Jayden Meghoma. He took one sharp touch to control it and another to guide it beyond Nico Schmid, before celebrating in the direction of the Pompey fans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bree fires Southampton ahead in the South Coast derby, timing his run perfectly to latch onto Finn Azaz's long ball before finishing clinically and sending St Mary's into raptures

Few chances of note followed before the break, but the hosts suffered a huge blow moments before the whistle. Boyhood Saints fan Bragg picked up a second booking for a needless pull on Ebou Adams and walked.

John Mousinho brought on Adrian Segecic at the break to try and help find the equaliser, then made a triple change just after the hour - but he was unable to refresh the visitors' attack, which increasingly lacked urgency.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton academy product and lifelong fan Cameron Bragg is shown a second yellow card after bringing down Portsmouth's Ebou Adams, leaving Saints to battle on with 10 men

That was illustrated in the numbers: 10 second-half shots, zero on target, 0.51 xG.

A run of four straight draws in this fixture comes to an end - capping a positive week for Southampton, following the news Tonda Eckert was given only a six-week suspended ban by the FA for the 'Spygate' saga.

Eckert: Derby win means everything - but we had to dig deep after red

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert speaking on Sky Sports:

"It means everything. We had to dig deep, probably a lot deeper than we thought before the game and credit to the boys because they deserved that."

On the red card: "You know how much it means to him [Bragg].

"At the end, I said to him he gave us a game we would not have had any other way, so we'll probably look back at the end of the season and say this is the game that gave us a big push and he was a part of that. In a different way than he wanted, but it happens. It will be a learning for him.

"I think it did change the game. Not on the scoreline, but the game changes then and you need to find different qualities. We knew then we had to dig deep."

Mousinho bemoans Pompey's inability to take advantage of extra man

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Portsmouth boss John Mousinho reacts to defeat in the South Coast derby, admitting he was left frustrated after feeling his side did enough to take more from the game.

Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho speaking on Sky Sports:

"When you come away from games and you're well beaten, it's easier to take in some ways. Today, it was a different game after the red card, but for the amount of pressure we had in the second half, the amount of opportunities we had, to not put the ball in the back of the net... we're devastated.

"There's very few times you come in as a head coach or manager after the game and not be frustrated by the way you've conceded goals. We lost a challenge in the middle of the park, had half-decent movement in behind, but it's something we highlighted. We have to be much better and we actually got away with one after the first or second minute.

"Against a really good side, if you get torn apart - and they had some spells in the first half where they looked good, but didn't really threaten us - you hold your hands up and take it. But it's one we'll look back on.

"For the territory and the opportunities we created, it was a good performance against 10 men - we just didn't put the ball in the back of the net."

Sports.title: Yamashita wins Korea Championship with course-record finish
Sports.content:
Miyu Yamashita put on a show on the final day of the LET's Aramco Korea Championship, firing a course record of 63 (-9) to win by three strokes with a total of 22 under par.

The world No 5 led from the 36-hole mark and was bogey-free once again at New Korea Country Club.

Yamashita began well with birdies on the third, fifth, eighth and 10th holes to put herself in a good position with seven holes to go.

However, the Czech Republic's Sara Kouskova was hot on her heels, but the 25-year-old major champion rolled in three birdies in four holes before making an eagle on 17 to seal her fourth win of 2026.

It was the Japanese star's second title on the Ladies European Tour (LET), having also won the 2025 AIG Women's Open.

"I'm so happy. Today my shot, my putting, everything was feeling so good. I had trust in my game. I like this course," said Yamashita.
