Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Hesitates Over Schofield vs. Zepeda Unification
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya agreed to a Floyd Schofield–William Zepeda unification after being pressed during DAZN’s post-fight interview, but his initial response suggested little enthusiasm for matching his two lightweight champions.

Schofield had just captured the vacant WBA title by defeating Lucas Bahdi when De La Hoya announced his interest in unifying. That invitation became less straightforward once Chris Mannix brought up Zepeda, Golden Boy’s WBC champion.

“We want to unify the titles against anybody,” said De La Hoya to DAZN.

Mannix asked whether Zepeda would be next. De La Hoya’s answer sent the conversation toward Abdullah Mason instead.

“Well, maybe it’s not the fight to do next, but let’s go with Mason or any world champion in the WBC. Whoever it is, ‘Kid Austin’ is ready,” said De La Hoya.

Mannix returned to the obvious option: “Zepeda has got that WBC world title. Let’s take that fight next.”

“We’ll make that fight happen then,” De La Hoya replied.

That was an agreement, although it came after De La Hoya had already suggested taking another route. There was no date announced or indication that either fighter had accepted the matchup.

The hesitation is understandable from a business perspective. Golden Boy now has two lightweight champions it can promote separately. Each can headline title fights, build his audience, and pursue opponents from other promotional companies. Putting them together guarantees that one leaves without his belt.

Mason is with Top Rank, making him a different proposition. Schofield could lose that fight too, but a victory would bring another title into Golden Boy while preserving Zepeda’s separate championship run. An in-house unification offers no such possibility.

That does not establish De La Hoya’s motive, but it explains why “anybody” might become less appealing when the opponent is another revenue stream within his own company.

For Schofield, Zepeda would also be a tough first defense. His sustained pressure and punch volume would test the new champion’s ability to keep control while being pushed backward.

Zepeda also has an obstacle to facing Schofield next. According to EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai, the WBC has ordered him to defend against interim champion Jadier Herrera, with purse bids scheduled for October 20. Mason’s WBO mandatory is also due, with Joe Cordina ranked No. 1.

De La Hoya’s unification plans could therefore require approval from the sanctioning bodies or agreements involving the mandatory challengers before either fight can proceed.

Sports.title: Schofield Wins WBA Title As Sergio Mendoza Upsets Sandoval
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield claimed the vacant WBA lightweight title, while Sergio Mendoza delivered the night’s biggest upset by stopping unified flyweight champion Ricardo Sandoval on Saturday at Wintrust Arena in Chicago.

The Golden Boy Promotions and Most Valuable Promotions card aired on DAZN. Schofield’s title victory came with disputed knockdown calls, while Mendoza overturned expectations in the co-feature.

Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs), of Austin, Texas, defeated Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs), of Niagara Falls, Ontario, by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. The judges scored the fight 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111.

Schofield’s speed and movement helped him win rounds, but Bahdi’s power made the contest more competitive than the widest score suggested. In the third, Schofield knocked Bahdi into the ropes, prompting referee Ben Rodriguez to rule a knockdown.

Bahdi hurt Schofield during a fierce sixth round and landed a right hand in the ninth that sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Rodriguez credited Bahdi with a knockdown in the eleventh, although Bahdi appeared to step on Schofield’s foot as he went down. Schofield stayed mobile in the final round to secure the belt.

In the co-feature, southpaw Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs), of Hermosillo, Mexico, stopped Ricardo “El Niño” Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs), of Rialto, California, at 0:24 of the fifth round to capture the WBA and WBC flyweight titles.

Mendoza dropped Sandoval twice during the final half-minute of the second round, with referee Mark Nelson administering a count each time. Sandoval rallied in the fourth, outscoring the challenger, but Mendoza dropped him again early in the fifth. After Sandoval rose, Mendoza drove him into the ropes with another attack, prompting Nelson to stop the fight.

The defeat ended Sandoval’s reign in his first defense and disrupted his plans for bigger fights following a lengthy layoff.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera (17-0, 7 KOs), of Salinas, Puerto Rico, defeated Abraham Perfecto (14-3, 9 KOs), of Tecate, Mexico, by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Rivera dropped Perfecto with a left hook in the second, prompting a count from referee Tommy Gonzalez. Rivera lost a point for a low blow in the ninth but remained comfortably ahead, winning 99-89 on all three cards.

Cruiserweight Tristan “Sweet T” Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs), of North Las Vegas, Nevada, stopped Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs), of San Juan, Puerto Rico, at 0:44 of the third round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Kalkreuth dropped Rosado with a right hand to the chin in the first. A third-round flurry brought the intervention of referee Ben Rodriguez, with Rosado still on his feet.

Light middleweight Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) at 1:48 of the second round.

Flores dropped Dahlman with a left to the body in round two. Dahlman beat referee Dave Smith’s count, but Flores followed with unanswered punches until Smith halted the contest.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Oxon Hill, Maryland, stopped Pedro Castaneda (9-2-1, 5 KOs), of Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, at 0:28 of the third round of their scheduled eight-round fight.

Boxing from a southpaw stance, Harvey landed a left hand to the chin that dropped Castaneda. Castaneda got up but was in no condition to continue, prompting referee Dave Smith to wave it off.

Super featherweight Cris Williams (15-0, 8 KOs), of Chicago, defeated southpaw Asa “Ace” Stevens (7-1-1, 2 KOs), of Waianae, Hawaii, by unanimous decision over eight rounds.

Williams controlled the opening four rounds and hurt Stevens in the seventh. The judges scored it 78-74 twice and 77-75, with Mark Nelson refereeing.

Minimumweight Naomy “Wonder Woman” Valle (16-1, 9 KOs), of San Jose, Costa Rica, defeated Sheyla Moreno by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds.

Valle’s cleaner punching helped her build a lead, and a point deduction for holding in the eighth did not prevent her from winning her professional U.S. debut. Dave Smith refereed the bout.

Heavyweight Joshua “The Rocket” Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Houston, stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs), of Detroit, one second into the third round of their scheduled eight-round contest.

Edwards controlled the first two rounds and hurt Lewis near the end of the second. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, and referee Tommy Gonzalez halted the fight at the start of the third.

Michael Vale served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Beats Lucas Bahdi To Claim WBA Title
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield won the vacant WBA lightweight title Saturday night, using his speed and movement to beat Lucas Bahdi by unanimous decision in a fight that tested his ability to recover under pressure.

The judges scored it 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111 at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) earned the belt, but Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) made him work considerably harder than the widest card suggested.

Schofield established his jab early, darting into range with combinations before moving away. Bahdi answered with heavier punches and body work, showing that he could trouble the quicker fighter when he found openings.

A left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes in round three, earning Schofield a knockdown and an early advantage. Bahdi absorbed the setback and continued looking for opportunities to land his power shots.

The sixth became a fierce round in which both fighters were hurt. Bahdi badly rocked Schofield with heavy punches, but Schofield fired back rather than allowing the Canadian to take complete control. His willingness to trade made the fight entertaining, although it also gave Bahdi the kind of contest he needed.

Schofield returned to movement and counters in the following rounds. That approach forced Bahdi to chase, and his difficulty cutting off the ring allowed Schofield to collect points without remaining in punching range.

The refereeing became a talking point in the ninth when a Bahdi right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Bahdi received credit for a knockdown in round eleven, though their feet tangled during that incident.

Schofield stayed mobile in the twelfth and reached the final bell. He showed enough boxing ability to win, along with the toughness to recover when Bahdi hurt him. The next step is tightening his defense: his speed won rounds, but trading unnecessarily repeatedly exposed him to Bahdi’s biggest weapon.

Sports.title: Sergio Mendoza Shatters Ricardo Sandoval’s Plans With Upset
Sports.content:
Sergio Mendoza Cordova wrecked Ricardo Sandoval’s plans with a fifth-round stoppage, taking the unified WBA and WBC flyweight titles in a fight the defending champion was expected to win Saturday night in Chicago.

Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs) dropped Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs) three times at Wintrust Arena, recovering from a second-round knockdown of his own to deliver the biggest victory of his career. The referee intervened in the fifth as Sandoval could no longer cope with the challenger’s attack.

Sandoval had entered his first defense looking to build on the split-decision victory over Kenshiro Teraji that earned him both belts in Japan in July 2025. Instead, his return after more than a year of inactivity ended with those titles heading to Mendoza.

This was supposed to be the night Sandoval got moving again. A successful defense would have allowed him to pursue bigger fights from the position of a unified champion. Now, he faces the task of rebuilding after a damaging defeat, with those opportunities belonging to somebody else.

Sandoval briefly appeared to have the fight moving his way when a right hook put Mendoza down in round two. That success did not discourage the Mexican southpaw, who recovered and used his pressure and punching power to turn the contest.

Mendoza’s three knockdowns made this more than a champion getting caught once. Sandoval could not regain control as the challenger kept hurting him, and the fifth-round intervention ended his hopes of rescuing the defense.

The result was especially unexpected given Mendoza’s recent form. He entered after a second-round knockout loss to Thanongsak Simsri in April, making his U.S. debut as a late replacement and heavy underdog.

Sandoval’s long absence invites questions about his sharpness, but Mendoza supplied the decisive punches. An opponent expected to help launch the champion’s next run instead took both belts and forced Sandoval to start over.

Sandoval walked into Chicago treating Mendoza like a stay-busy fight to dust off fifteen months of rust, and he paid the ultimate price for it. When a unified titleholder sits out for well over a year, thinks he can just show up against a heavy puncher, and gets dragged into a firefight, this is exactly what happens.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs Lucas Bahdi Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Lightweight Floyd Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) defeated Lucas Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) by unanimous decision to win the vacant WBA title, with scores of 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111. Schofield used his speed, jab, and lateral movement to win rounds, earning a knockdown in the third when a left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes.

Bahdi’s power kept the fight dangerous, badly rocking Schofield during a fierce sixth round in which both men were hurt. A right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas in the ninth without a knockdown being called, while Bahdi received credit for an eleventh-round knockdown despite their feet tangling.

Schofield stayed mobile in the final round and reached the bell to secure the decision after a competitive fight marked by disputed refereeing calls.

Flyweight Sergio Mendoza Cordova (28-1, 24 KOs) upset Ricardo Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs) by fifth-round stoppage to capture the unified WBA and WBC titles. Mendoza dropped the defending champion three times, turning his late replacement opportunity into the biggest victory of his career.

Sandoval scored a knockdown with a right hook in round two, but Mendoza recovered and took control with his pressure and power. The southpaw’s attack eventually forced the referee to intervene in the fifth, ending Sandoval’s first title defense.

Mendoza entered as a heavy underdog after suffering a second-round knockout loss to Thanongsak Simsri in April. Sandoval’s return after more than a year out ended with him losing both belts to a challenger making his U.S. debut.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs) stopped Pedro Castaneda Castro (9-2-1, 5 KOs) in the third round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Harvey controlled the action with his speed and accuracy before ending the fight with a sharp lead left cross.

The punch dropped Castaneda heavily and brought the referee in for a count. Castaneda managed to get back to his feet, but his condition prompted the referee to wave it off. Harvey needed no follow-up attack, with the single shot doing enough damage to force the stoppage.

The 2024 U.S. Olympian showed the value of a clean, well-timed punch against an opponent who could not match his skill. It was another early finish for Harvey, whose speed made the decisive left hand difficult for Castaneda to anticipate.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera-Pizarro (17-0, 7 KOs) defeated Abraham Perfecto Valdez (14-3, 9 KOs) by unanimous decision over ten rounds. All three judges scored the fight 99-89 for Rivera-Pizarro.

The Puerto Rican scored a knockdown in the second round, establishing an early lead that Valdez never threatened. Rivera-Pizarro controlled the action with cleaner punching and a steady work rate, preventing the taller Mexican from building momentum. Valdez struggled to establish his offense and spent much of the contest being outworked.

Despite the early knockdown, Valdez lasted the distance as Rivera-Pizarro continued collecting rounds through the final bell. It was a comfortable victory for Rivera-Pizarro against an opponent coming off a fourth-round stoppage loss to Leonardo Sanchez.

Tristan Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs) stopped previously unbeaten Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs) at 0:44 of the third round in cruiserweight action. Kalkreuth used his height and reach to control the scheduled ten-round fight, leaving the shorter Rosado struggling to get his offense going.

The 24-year-old pressed the action and overwhelmed Rosado with his power. Rosado could not adequately defend himself as Kalkreuth continued the attack early in round three. The referee stepped in with Rosado still on his feet, ending a one-sided contest. Rosado’s unbeaten record offered little protection against the larger Kalkreuth, who dictated the fight throughout.

Heavyweight Joshua Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs) stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs) at the start of the third round of their scheduled eight-round bout. The 2024 U.S. Olympian controlled the action against the 42-year-old veteran, forcing him onto the defensive.

Edwards landed a combination late in the second round that hurt Lewis and brought the fight toward its finish. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, prompting the stoppage at the beginning of round three. The injury’s exact nature was not specified in the early ringside account. Edwards needed just two completed rounds to register his seventh stoppage victory.

Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs) stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) in the second round of their scheduled eight-round light middleweight bout. Flores controlled the action with his size and punching power, putting the veteran under pressure early.

A hard left hook to the liver hurt Dahlman badly in round two and opened the door for the finish. Flores followed with a sustained attack as Dahlman struggled to recover from the body shot. With Dahlman unable to halt the assault, the referee stepped in to stop the fight. The 21-year-old Flores needed fewer than two rounds to secure his tenth knockout.

Minimumweight Naomy Valle (16-1, 9 KOs) defeated Sheyla Moreno Castillo (5-2-1) by unanimous decision over eight rounds in her professional U.S. debut. The judges scored it 78-73, 78-72, and 77-74 for Valle. Valle controlled most of the early action with her jab and right hand, landing the cleaner punches as Moreno pressed forward.

A right hand in the third round hurt Moreno, but the Mexican fighter kept coming and made Valle work throughout. The final two rounds became scrappier, with Valle losing a point in the eighth for excessive holding after repeated warnings. The deduction came too late to threaten Valle’s lead, which she had built through her more accurate punching over the first six rounds.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Seeks His First World Title
Sports.content:
Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs) has the opportunity tonight to capture the WBA lightweight world title at the Wintrust Arena in Chicago, when he faces undefeated fighter “Prince” Lucas Bahdi (20-0, 15 KOs). This is what Schofield has fought his entire life for: a world title opportunity.

He started boxing at a young age with his trainer and father, Floyd Schofield Sr. He’s dedicated his entire life to boxing, and it is his lifelong dedication and commitment to the sport that he believes will be the difference tonight. Floyd has criticized Bahdi’s resume, stating he has limited experience.

Telling The Spit Bucket Podcast, “He seems like a good dude. I respect him because I see him with his kids on Instagram all the time. A fighter and a father that’s there for the kids, I’m going to respect him either way, but I think fighter to fighter like he knows he doesn’t have more skill than me.”

Bahdi came onto the big stage after his vicious knockout of Ashton “H20” Sylve on the Jake Paul-Mike Perry undercard in July of 2024. A fight Lucas was losing, being outlanded in all six rounds before scoring the knockout that ended it all.

Sylve outlanded Bahdi in every round, outlanding him 101 to 38 in total punches with H20 landing 46 percent of his power punches (Compubox). If Lucas is as reckless defensively against Schofield as he was against Sylve, it may be a very early night for him.

As for Kid Austin, he quickly stopped Tevin Farmer in his last match, ending it in 78 seconds. Schofield surprised many with his performance by being so dominant over Farmer, who was believed to be a boxer who would truly test him.

Floyd has been training extremely hard for this match, despite some minor setbacks at yesterday’s official weigh-in, having missed weight by 6 ounces on his first attempt. He was able to redeem himself on the second attempt by meeting the lightweight limit of 135 pounds.

Bahdi had no problems making weight, coming in a full pound under at 134 pounds. Lucas then took to trolling Floyd on social media by posting a video of himself on Instagram saying it was easy to make weight and then eating a donut.

Weight shouldn’t be an issue inside the ring and may actually play to Schofield’s advantage, who will seek to utilize his full set of skills of speed, power, and experience. Similar to Sylve, he’ll look to outbox Bahdi by controlling the range and overwhelm him with tactical pressure.

Given Kid Austin’s experience and overall physical attributes, he may be too much to handle for Bahdi, who may not have an answer defensively to stop Schofield’s offensive firepower.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Prioritizes Activity Over Opponent Quality
Sports.content:
Robert Garcia wants Vergil Ortiz Jr. back in the ring, even if that means accepting an opponent who does little to satisfy fans waiting for the Jaron Ennis fight.

Keith Thurman is the likely opponent for Ortiz’s proposed December 5 return on the David Benavidez card. Talks appear promising, though the fight has yet to be finalized. Ortiz is scheduled to begin training camp next week.

“I don’t care whatever people say. I just need Vergil back in,” Garcia said. “He’s been out for a year. … It’s going to be 13 months basically. So, that’s too much.”

That explains the willingness to take Thurman. Garcia’s priority is getting Ortiz through a training camp and into a fight. Looking for someone who offers more prestige could bring another delay, leaving Vergil inactive into next year.

Thurman would give Ortiz a recognizable opponent, but beating him would leave the bigger questions unanswered. Fans want to see Vergil against the strongest fighters around his weight. A return bout can restore activity without delivering that test.

Garcia accepts the criticism. He believes the cost of waiting has become greater than the benefit of holding out for a better opponent.

“If we try to switch up, find somebody else or maybe a bigger fight, a fight that means a little bit more, then it might take longer,” he said.

The same frustration is behind the team’s decision to campaign at 160 pounds. Garcia expects Ennis to pursue Josh Kelly and then potentially Sebastian Fundora, a sequence he believes could leave Ortiz waiting another year.

He understands Ennis’s interest in unification, while maintaining that Vergil would present a harder fight. Ortiz’s team is choosing to move forward rather than keep cutting to 154 for an opportunity Garcia cannot count on.

Getting Ortiz active is a reasonable immediate goal. After that, the urgency needs to extend to finding stronger opposition. Thurman can end the layoff; he cannot replace the fights that made fans eager to see Vergil return.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Believes He Can Break Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois’ decision to take a knee in their first fight revealed a weakness he could exploit again, saying that he needed to inflict enough punishment to bring it out.

Wardley pointed to the third-round knockdown, when Dubois backed up before dropping to one knee after taking an overhand right. He viewed that sequence differently from the first knockdown, where he felt his punch connected more cleanly.

“He started to kind of back up and then chose to take a knee. It was just an overhand right. It was the same one I did in the first round,” said Wardley to DAZN.

That right hand gives Wardley something more concrete to work with than questions about Dubois’ heart. Dubois has a strong jab, but Wardley described using the overhand counter to make him think twice about throwing it.

“A way to take away someone’s jab is to let them know that a shot will be coming straight behind it,” Wardley said.

If Dubois hesitates with his jab, he could give Wardley more opportunities to close the distance. The challenge for Dubois is to keep using that weapon without leaving himself open to the same right hand. Abandoning it would make it harder to control where the fight takes place.

Wardley’s interpretation of the knee is more debatable. A hurt fighter can take a count to recover without wanting out of the contest. Wardley nevertheless believes there is a point at which Dubois can be persuaded to surrender.

“I just knew I needed to do enough to bring it out. But that still wasn’t enough for me. I still needed a bit more,” said Wardley.

The practical task is reproducing the punishment that led to that moment. Wardley has identified a punch that worked and a reaction he believes he can force again. Dubois needs an answer to the counter before he can prevent Wardley from testing that theory.

Ghana News.title: Joseph Cudjoe writes: Ghana must break free from the dangerous mindset that natural resources are the foundation for wealth
Ghana News.content:
“Resources are not; they become.” This famous observation by economist Erich W. Zimmermann should challenge one of the most deeply rooted misconceptions in Ghana’s development thinking: the belief that our natural resource endowment is the foundation of our prosperity.

We have become so obsessed with what lies beneath our soil that we risk underestimating what lies within our people. We celebrate gold, bauxite, manganese and lithium, yet pay insufficient attention to the knowledge, skills, innovation and productive capabilities that transform nations into economic powerhouses.

Countries such as Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Denmark, the Netherlands and Luxembourg have demonstrated that abundant natural resource wealth is not a prerequisite for national prosperity.

Their experiences show what education, skills, innovation, technology and industrial development can achieve. We must stop conditioning Ghana’s youth to believe that our natural resources are the foundation of our wealth.

Our greatest resource must be our people and their ability to think, innovate, invent, manufacture and solve problems. Ghana should invest heavily in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education to equip young people with the capabilities to create technologies, develop products and build competitive industries.

Mineral deposits can be depleted or lose their market value, but human ingenuity can continually create new industries, products and sources of wealth. Ghana must invest in its people as seriously as it exploits its minerals.

History reinforces this thinking. Aluminium was once more expensive than gold until technological advances made it affordable. Natural ultramarine, once more expensive than gold by weight, lost much of its commercial importance when synthetic alternatives emerged. Natural alum, once vital to textile dyeing, was displaced by manufactured chemicals.

Flint lost its importance with the development of metalworking, while asbestos declined sharply after its deadly health effects became known. Even natural saltpetre and guano lost much of their strategic value as industrial alternatives emerged.

These resources once generated substantial wealth for the nations that controlled them. If materials once considered indispensable can lose their value, why should Ghana build its economic future around the assumption that our minerals will always command the same importance they do today?

Our gold, bauxite, manganese and lithium present opportunities, but opportunities are not guarantees of lasting prosperity. Technological breakthroughs, alternative materials, recycling and changing industrial needs can alter demand and prices.

Ghana must therefore move beyond the obsession with extracting and exporting natural resources. We must invest in education, technical skills, scientific research, technology, manufacturing and enterprise. Where economically viable, we should process our minerals locally and use the proceeds to develop industries that can survive beyond mineral booms.

The fundamental question is not how much wealth nature has deposited beneath our feet, but how much productive capacity we have developed above the ground.

OUR FUTURE MUST BE EXTRACTED FROM OUR PEOPLE, NOT FROM THE GROUND.

Human resources, when continuously developed, can renew and expand their value, while natural resources are finite and can be depleted. Human capabilities can also adapt to emerging global needs through education, innovation and skills development in ways that mineral deposits cannot.

Ghana therefore cannot continue to teach its young people, implicitly or explicitly, that our natural resource endowment is the principal answer to our economic challenges. Such a mindset risks producing a nation that is rich in minerals but poor in innovation, employment creation and industrial capability.

Natural resources provide potential; human knowledge, productivity and innovation turn that potential into lasting wealth.

Our national ambition must be to raise generations of highly skilled and innovative Ghanaians capable of creating products, developing technologies, building competitive businesses and exporting knowledge to the world.

The countries that will prosper tomorrow will not necessarily be those with the richest mineral deposits, but those with the most capable people and the strongest capacity to innovate. Ghana must prepare its youth to create wealth, not merely to inherit the hope that wealth lies beneath our soil.

MY QUESTION

The Akufo-Addo and Bawumia administration demonstrated this understanding through its education policies. Is the Mahama administration investing enough in STEM education, and doing more, to equip our youth with the knowledge, skills and technological capabilities to create wealth beyond our natural resources?

Ghana News.title: Children among 109 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
Ghana News.content:
At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, have died and dozens more are still missing after a boat sank off the coast of Djibouti, the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) has said.

The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 350 people on board when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night. Around 80 people were rescued, the IOM said.

IOM's Djibouti mission chief Alexandre Coissac called the tragedy a "stark reminder" of the dangers migrants face while seeking a new life elsewhere.

Tens of thousands of migrants from the Horn of Africa make the perilous journey each year hoping to reach Gulf countries for safety and work, according to the UN agency.

In a statement on Friday, the organisation said 52 men, 42 women, nine girls and six boys were among the bodies recovered.

"This is a devastating loss of life," Coissac said.

"Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives," he added.

Local authorities are also arranging burials for those who have died, while the survivors - all Ethiopian nationals - have medical care readily available to them.

Yemen remains engulfed in a devastating civil war which has lasted more than a decade. Despite this conflict - and growing instability across the wider region - migrants still cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen driven by poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change.

Since 10 September, the IOM said its Displacement Tracking Matrix has observed more than 20,000 "movements" from Ethiopia to Djibouti.

IOM said it is providing assistance to 64 of the survivors at its response centre in Obock, including healthcare and support to "restore contact with their families".

The UN agency is working in "close collaboration" with local authorities to help migrants and "prevent deaths at sea and on land", it added.

According to IOM figures, more than 900 migrants died or went missing taking the same route in 2025, with an 18% increase in the number of people attempting the journey.

In March 2026, nine people were killed, and 45 were missing after a similar incident.

Ghana News.title: OmniBSIC Bank’s 11th health walk promotes fitness and business growth
Ghana News.content:
OmniBSIC Bank has held its 11th annual Health Walk at the University of Ghana Sports Stadium, bringing together staff, customers, businesses and members of the public to promote physical fitness, healthy living and networking.

The 12-kilometre walk took participants through major routes around Legon City Mall, PRESEC Legon, Atomic Junction, Madina Zongo Junction and Ritz Junction before returning to the stadium.

Chairperson of the Health Walk Committee, Akyaa Afreh Arhin Addo-Kufuor, said the event has become a fixture on the bank’s annual calendar, with participants returning each year because of the quality of activities and the attention given to their safety and comfort.

She said the bank has maintained the consistency of the initiative by ensuring that each edition meets participants’ expectations.

“We don't just get up and walk. We have experienced instructors, aerobics instructors. We have experienced brass band people who would give us music on the way,” she said.

She added that the bank also prioritises security to ensure participants feel safe throughout the activity.

“We work as hard as we worked for the first edition,” she said, stressing the bank’s commitment to maintaining the event’s standards as participation grows.

Head of the Corporate Communications Department, Justin Carl Arhin, said the turnout, energy and networking among participants demonstrated the value of the initiative beyond promoting physical fitness.

He noted that the event also provides opportunities for exhibitors and businesses to connect with potential customers and generate economic activity.

“Look around you, see the numbers, see the energy, see the vibe, see the networking that is going on, see the number of exhibitors who have been able to come and the kind of economic transformation that we are also achieving as a result of all the business that is going on here,” he said.

Mr Arhin said the bank was pleased with the outcome and intended to sustain the initiative, adding that it would continue to grow in scale and participation.

OmniBSIC Bank says it remains committed to initiatives that promote healthy living, strengthen community relationships and create opportunities for businesses to engage with customers beyond the banking hall.

Ghana News.title: 2026 World Maritime Day: Danish Embassy organises “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks”
Ghana News.content:
As part of activities to mark the 2026 World Maritime Day and the 10th anniversary of the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea, the Royal Danish Embassy Accra presented “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks”, a site‑specific art intervention held at the Ambassador’s Residence in Accra.

Under the theme “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”, three commissioned artworks brought human ‑ centered creative perspectives to the diplomatic maritime‑security discussions.

Curated by Fang Wang (Fang W. Linulf) and Essé Dabla‑Attikpo, the show featured Ghanaian artists Patrick Tagoe‑Turkson and Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku alongside a large‑scale floor work by Fang W. Linulf.

Tagoe‑Turkson repurposed beach‑collected plastic flip‑flops for mixed‑media assemblages addressing marine waste and coastal heritage. Aggrey Tieku also built monumental installations from salvaged second‑hand textiles to interrogate waste colonialism and global‑trade pollution. Fang’s 100 sqm floor print merges ocean imagery and maritime geographic data, letting visitors physically stand upon mapped Gulf‑of‑Guinea ocean geography.

Moving beyond official reports, the art intervention used sensory visual storytelling to highlight ocean ecology, coastal‑community realities and the human side of maritime governance for attending diplomats. Co – curator and artist Fang W. Linulf mentioned that visitors literally walk across the ocean on my floor print whilst abstract maritime data becomes something bodily and immediate.

She further stated that “policy builds frameworks for maritime security, yet art uncovers the human and material stories often missing from official documents. We wanted delegates to feel, not only read, the realities of the Gulf of Guinea coast.”

Essé Dabla‑Attikpo, also a co‑Curator “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks” stated that “waste arriving on our shores is not just an environmental problem. It carries global trade histories. Through re‑making discarded materials, we give visibility to these hidden narratives.”

Patrick Tagoe‑Turkson transformed ocean washed plastic flip‑flops collected from Ghana’s Atlantic shorelines into layered mixed‑media assemblages.

At the event, he said that “discarded flip‑flops and textiles washed onto our beaches hold cultural memories. Transforming waste into art is one way to advocate for our ocean and our coastal heritage.”

Commenting on the exhibition, Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku mentioned that “I work with second‑hand garments that end up in Ghana’s landfills and beaches. These textiles are physical evidence of waste colonialism and unequal global supply chains.”

The “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks” event was attended by maritime practitioners, diplomats and industry stakeholders and created a platform to experience maritime realities through sensory, material and visual perspectives, raising public awareness through artistic practice.

Ghana News.title: New Economy will tackle unemployment and restore hope – Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana’s New Economy will confront the human cost of unemployment and address the barriers preventing young people, farmers and small businesses from building sustainable livelihoods.

According to him, the country could no longer accept a situation in which education fails to lead to employment, talent remains unsupported and productive effort yields little opportunity.

“Unemployment is personal. It is the graduate who has finished school but cannot find work. It is the young person with talent but no capital,” he said.

Dr Forson’s message places jobs and economic opportunity at the centre of the New Economy, drawing attention to the everyday struggles behind unemployment figures.

He highlighted the plight of farmers who produce without reliable markets and small business owners whose ambitions to expand are frustrated by the cost of credit. His remarks underscored the need to address both the search for work and the obstacles facing those capable of creating it.

For families, he said, the burden is particularly painful after years of sacrifice to finance a child’s education.

“It is the family that sacrifices to educate a child, only to watch that child sit at home.”

The Finance Minister rejected the idea that such experiences should become an accepted feature of national life.

“No serious nation can accept this as normal. The New Economy says Ghana must no longer accept it.”

He made these remarks in an engagement with students and faculty of the University of Development Studies at their Nyankpala Campus.

Ghana News.title: IMMILAC president recounts personal losses as security women lead breast cancer awareness campaign in Wa
Ghana News.content:
They usually check passports at the borders. On Friday, they were raising awareness about breast cancer in Wa.

Female officers of the Ghana Immigration Service, Ghana Police Service and Ghana Prisons Service took to the principal streets of Wa in a float, dressed in their uniforms and wearing pink ribbons, as they marked Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

The exercise turned parts of the Upper West Regional capital pink, drawing attention to the importance of breast cancer awareness, prevention and early detection.

Leading the campaign was Deputy Superintendent of Immigration (DSI) Prospera Soliku, President of the Immigration Ladies Association (IMMILAC) in the Upper West Region.

In recent years, DSI Soliku has championed the welfare, health and professional development of female officers under her leadership of the association’s regional chapter.

Under her presidency, IMMILAC’s annual Pink October campaign has evolved from an internal sensitisation programme for members into a community-wide initiative involving sister security services and the general public.

This year’s campaign, however, carried a deeply personal message for the IMMILAC President, who disclosed that she had lost loved ones to breast cancer.

“This cause is deeply personal to me. I lost my beloved aunt, who actually cut my wedding cake, as well as a close friend and her sister to this breast cancer,” DSI Soliku told officers at the Regional Headquarters of the Ghana Immigration Service, where the float ended.

Held under the theme “Every Story Is Unique, Every Journey Matters,” the exercise sought to raise awareness about breast cancer prevention and the importance of early detection.

“October, particularly known as Pink October, is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Our theme this year reminds us that everyone affected by breast cancer deserves care, compassion, and support,” she said.

Beyond the street procession, the campaign focused on educating participants about breast cancer, its risk factors and the importance of seeking medical attention early.

Health Promotion Officer at the Wa Municipal Hospital, Leticia Yuorkuu, took participants through the causes, risk factors and prevention of the disease.

“Breast cancer is caused by genetic mutation of the DNA. It is inherited or acquired through our lifestyle and environment. It does not spread from person to person either by air, sex, blood or food,” she explained.

She identified alcohol consumption, smoking, an unhealthy diet, obesity, lack of exercise, early menarche, late menopause and late childbirth as factors associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.

Ms Yuorkuu also addressed a common misconception about breastfeeding and breast cancer prevention.

“Suckling by babies can actually help women prevent breast cancer. But sucking by men does not help. Sucking by men is a way of pleasure during sexual activities,” she said, drawing laughter from participants.

Medical Officer at the Upper West Regional Hospital, Dr Adam Mansura, cautioned that cancer could spread without obvious symptoms and sought to dispel misconceptions about breast cancer treatment.

“Cancer on its own doesn't cause pain, but that doesn't mean you cannot have cancer and have pain. That's why there's a need to assess and examine. Not every breast cancer treatment leads to removal of the breast. Early detection, early diagnosis saves us. If you are able to detect it early and start your treatment early, you may not have to go through removal,” she stressed.

Dr Mansura explained that breast cancer could spread to other parts of the body, including the back, brain, hip, lungs and liver. She also noted that not every breast lump was cancerous.

She demonstrated two methods of breast self-examination: using a mirror and examining the breasts while lying on a flat surface.

Participants were advised to look out for lumps, changes in breast size or shape, skin discolouration, nipple discharge and other unusual changes in the breasts.

At the close of the event, the Regional Commander of the Ghana Immigration Service in the Upper West Region, DCOI Justice Ayensu Bosomtwe, urged officers to take their physical fitness seriously.

“You cannot be a security officer and not be fit. When you are called for PT, you don't expect us to beg you. When persuasion fails, I will do what I feel is right to keep you fit. Because I believe that when we do some of these exercises, at least it will minimise our chances of getting this dreaded disease,” he said.

He added that he would enforce physical training as a mandatory parade to encourage officers to exercise regularly.

The programme also included free breast screening for participants and members of the public by a medical team from the Upper West Regional Hospital.

Those present included the Regional Second-in-Command, the Regional Passport Director, media representatives, officers from sister security services and members of the Immigration Men’s Association, who joined the ladies in supporting the campaign.

The organisers stressed the importance of sustaining breast cancer awareness beyond October, encouraging people to prioritise early detection, screening and access to accurate information.

Ghana News.title: University of Ghana postpones October 12 reopening as GAUA strike persists
Ghana News.content:
The University of Ghana has postponed its reopening for the 2026/2027 academic year, initially scheduled for Monday, October 12, 2026.

In a notice dated October 10, 2026, management said a revised reopening date would be announced in due course. The notice did not state the reason for the postponement.

However, the postponement comes amid an ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA), which has affected the effective operation and administration of public universities.

The announcement was signed by Prof Gordon A. Awandare, Pro Vice-Chancellor in charge of Academic and Student Affairs.

“Management sincerely regrets any inconvenience this postponement may cause and appreciates the patience and understanding of students as arrangements are made for the reopening,” the notice stated.

Despite the postponement, students have been urged to complete their academic registration online, following the procedure outlined in the university’s previous communication.

Management said completing registration would secure students’ places for classes and ensure their eligibility to participate in the random bed allocation exercise, which is expected to take place soon.

Read Also: KNUST postpones 2026/2027 academic year reopening indefinitely amid GAUA strike

Before the University of Ghana, the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) also announced a postponement of the reopening of the 2026/2027 academic year indefinitely specifically due to the strike.

Ghana News.title: Bahass Foundation launches vocational skills training to support mental health recovery in Wa
Ghana News.content:
The Bahass Foundation has marked this year’s World Mental Health Day with the launch of a vocational skills training initiative aimed at empowering residents undergoing rehabilitation and reducing relapses linked to unemployment and social stigma.

The initiative provides practical training in tailoring, smock dressmaking and traditional weaving to help residents acquire skills they can use to earn a living and reintegrate into their communities after rehabilitation.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Bahass Foundation, Ilyasu Yussif Baba, said clinical rehabilitation alone was insufficient if beneficiaries returned to environments where they lacked productive activities and sustainable livelihoods.

“Rehabilitation alone cannot solve all problems. Many of them, when they go back, do not have anything doing. That is why we decided to launch skills training, so when they are out, they have something productive to rely on rather than sitting idle,” Mr Baba explained.

According to Mr Baba, substance abuse accounts for approximately 80 per cent of current admissions at the facility, while other cases are associated with acute financial stress, business collapse or marital breakdown.

The facility currently houses 72 residents, comprising 60 males and 12 females. At the time of the event, 18 residents had started the vocational training, with two already able to produce woven items independently.

The potential impact of the initiative was evident among the residents. Gifty Mary Sunchebe, a resident from Nandom who developed a substance abuse problem while living in Koforidua, demonstrated how she coils thread for smock weaving.

“Coming here has given me a new skill. When I go home, I will show my parents what I can do so they can support me to start on my own,” she said.

She also urged families not to abandon relatives struggling with substance dependence.

Another resident, Bayuo Fortunatus, who is learning smock weaving, said vocational skills could help people recovering from mental health conditions overcome social stigma and achieve financial independence.

“Being in a mental home does not mean your life has ended. Employment issues affect everyone. Once you acquire a viable skill, you go out into the world able to provide for yourself and stay stable,” Fortunatus noted.

The event also featured a testimony of successful community reintegration by Mohammed, popularly known as “Killer Ntua”, a former resident who recovered at the facility, married and returned with his wife, Latifa, and young son, Abdul Rashid, to express gratitude to the foundation.

Ali Labaran, a resident undergoing rehabilitation, highlighted the facility’s dual role as a recovery centre and an addiction detoxification facility.

“Addiction, if left unchecked, will eventually drive a person into acute mental illness. We chose to be here with the backing of our families to reclaim our futures,” Labaran said.

Addressing the gathering, the Upper West Regional Mental Health Coordinator, Sylvester Basagnia, commended the foundation for placing the experiences and perspectives of people with lived experience at the centre of its activities.

However, he warned against the widespread stigma, derogatory labelling and abandonment of people experiencing mental health challenges by their families and communities.

“The fact that someone has schizophrenia, depression or an addiction does not mean their name has changed to that illness. Address people with dignity by their real names,” Mr Basagnia urged.

He cited the case of a trained senior high school teacher in Wa whose employment was terminated and payroll records erased after he developed mental health complications, leaving him destitute on the streets.

Mr Basagnia also raised concerns about substance abuse in the Wa Municipality, particularly the use of tramadol, pethidine, illicit alcohol and smokeless powdered snuff, locally known as nyee.

The chairman for the occasion, Biihee Naa, Naa Jaafar Pelpuo, emphasised that mental health challenges could affect anyone, regardless of social status or religious devotion.

“Mental illness is a common affliction that spares no one. If you find yourself in sound health, do not assume you are merely favoured while those afflicted are cursed. Supporting them to heal is supporting our own community’s wellbeing,” Naa Pelpuo stated.

The Coordinator of the Wa Community Foundation, Fatawu Dauda, described Bahass as an indispensable pillar in the Upper West Region, providing food, shelter and dignity to people living on the streets when their families are unable to care for them.

The event also attracted donations from community organisations in support of the foundation’s work.

The Jawara Foundation, led by its National Coordinator, Francis Baaladong, donated clothing, bags of rice, cooking oil, detergents, toiletries and GH₵1,000 in cash.

The Cathedral Parish branch of the Society of St. Theresa of the Child Jesus, represented by Diana Ali, donated clothing, toiletries and GH₵500 in cash.

The Upper West branch of Muslim Women in Teaching (MUSWIT), led by its patron, Sahadatu Y. Dodoo, also made financial donations and urged families to listen to relatives experiencing distress before their conditions worsened.

Despite its achievements, including the successful rehabilitation of more than 48 individuals, the Bahass Foundation faces significant infrastructural challenges. All 72 residents are currently accommodated in a single compound house.

Mr Baba appealed to philanthropic organisations, government agencies and the general public to provide building materials and financial assistance to complete an ongoing dormitory project, which has stalled at the window stage.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
