World.title: Ex-senator demands full disclosure, restitution over Kila’s fake degrees
World.content:
Former Senator Babafemi Ojudu has called on Anthony Kila to publicly disclose his true academic history, withdraw any false qualifications and make restitution for benefits obtained through misrepresentation, following a PREMIUM TIMES investigation that questioned all the degrees he claimed to have earned.

Mr Ojudu, a journalist and politician, said in a Facebook post on Sunday that Mr Kila should provide verifiable evidence to counter the newspaper’s findings or admit the findings if they are true.

He said accountability requires more than an apology, urging Mr Kila to identify the qualifications he cannot substantiate, correct biographies that repeat the claims and cooperate with any legitimate investigation.

“These are grave allegations that deserve a clear, documented answer,” Mr Ojudu wrote.

The former senator also called on Mr Kila’s family and close friends to support him through the controversy, stressing that public scrutiny should not descend into cruelty even as questions about his academic credentials demand answers.

“We can insist on the truth without turning public scrutiny into cruelty,” he said, adding that Mr Kila’s life remained worth protecting despite the allegations.

Mr Ojudu said he knew Mr Kila through their participation in a Yoruba association, where he described the public commentator as articulate, intellectually gifted and dignified.

He said Mr Kila’s apparent intellectual ability made the allegations particularly difficult to understand, questioning why someone with such abilities would need to invent academic qualifications.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“A person can be widely read, knowledgeable and useful to society without a university degree. There is no shame in that. But claiming qualifications one has not earned is a betrayal of trust,” he wrote.

Previous challenge to Kila

Mr Ojudu’s latest intervention follows his earlier reaction to PREMIUM TIMES’ investigation into Mr Kila’s professorial title.

In a Facebook post on Monday, the former senator called on Mr Kila to provide documentary evidence of his professorship and academic history rather than threaten legal action against the newspaper.

Mr Kila maintained that he was a professor, saying he stood by the title and the academic and professional credentials on which they were based. However, he did not provide evidence identifying a credible institution that awarded him the professorial rank in the response reported by PREMIUM TIMES.

In its first investigation , published on 3 October, PREMIUM TIMES found no evidence that a recognised academic institution had awarded Mr Kila the professorial title he has been using publicly for years.

He attributed the title to the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies, an institution the newspaper could not establish existed.

The newspaper’s follow-up investigation , examined the bachelor’s, master’s, doctorate and other qualifications Mr Kila claimed to have obtained from universities in Italy and the United Kingdom.

The investigation found discrepancies between his claims and the universities’ records, including institutions that said they had never offered some of the programmes he listed. The University of Essex, for instance, told the newspaper it had never offered the postgraduate diploma in media and communication that Mr Kila claimed to have obtained in 1992.

When PREMIUM TIMES presented its findings to him, Mr Kila said he was gathering his academic and professional documents and had begun contacting the institutions concerned.

“I am currently putting together my academic and professional documents, and they will be ready soon,” he told the newspaper.

University, ICPC responses

The controversy has also prompted institutional action.

The Michael and Cecilia Ibru University, Delta State, where Mr Kila served as pro-chancellor from August 2025, suspended him pending an investigation into questions surrounding his professorial status. The university cited its commitment to academic integrity, transparency and sound institutional governance.

The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has also constituted a team to investigate the allegations and determine whether the university benefited from Mr Kila’s actions.

Mr Ojudu said that if the findings of investigations are proven, Mr Kila should disclose whether the disputed qualifications secured appointments, payments or other benefits and address such matters through the appropriate processes.

He also asked Mr Kila to accept the consequences of any proven wrongdoing, warning that public trust could not be restored through persuasive speeches or an apology that failed to acknowledge the deception.

However, Mr Ojudu appealed for compassion, asking family and friends to remain close to him during the controversy. He said he had no information that Mr Kila intended to harm himself but wanted those around him to check on his welfare and seek professional assistance if necessary.

He said Mr Kila could still rebuild his life by abandoning any false claims, pursuing qualifications legitimately and contributing to society through demonstrable achievements.

“The first step towards that future is an honest account of the past,” Mr Ojudu wrote.

Mr Ojudu served as senator for Ekiti Central from 2011 to 2015 after winning the seat on the platform of the Action Congress of Nigeria, defeating former Governor Ayo Fayose of Ekiti.

World.title: NDLEA rearrests 83-year-old woman months after drug conviction
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has rearrested an 83-year-old woman in Abia State, months after she and her daughter were convicted of drug offences and fined N200,000 each.

In a statement on Sunday by NDLEA spokesperson Femi Babafemi, the woman, Uloma Sunday, was arrested at her home in Ite-Uzo, Umuaguma, Obingwa Local Government Area, on 7 October.

The agency stated that officers found methamphetamine and Colorado, a synthetic cannabinoid, concealed around her waist in a wrapper.

The NDLEA said her arrest followed intelligence reports that she was operating a drug joint where criminal suspects gathered and allegedly terrorised residents.

The agency revealed that Ms Sunday was previously arrested at the same address on 17 May 2025, alongside her 32-year-old daughter, Chisom Uchechi. Officers recovered 50 grammes of methamphetamine, 522 grammes of skunk, 260 grammes of fresh cannabis leaves and 12 grammes of tramadol.

Both women pleaded guilty and were sentenced to 12 months’ imprisonment or a N200,000 fine each. They paid the fines and were released.

The NDLEA did not say whether it charged Ms Sunday after her latest arrest.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

South African woman arrested at Port Harcourt airport

In a separate operation, officers arrested a South African woman, Gebashe Sithandiwe Jessie, at the Port Harcourt International Airport with 30 parcels of cannabis known as Thai Loud, weighing 32.74 kilogrammes.

The parcels were concealed in two travelling bags. The NDLEA said Ms Jessie arrived from Thailand through Doha aboard a Qatar Airways flight.

She reportedly told investigators that she had previously trafficked drugs through other African countries and wanted to extend her operations to Port Harcourt.

NDLEA intercepts 354,000 tapentadol tablets in Lagos

At the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos, officers intercepted nine cartons containing 354,000 tapentadol tablets shipped from Pakistan.

The consignment arrived aboard a Royal Air Maroc flight on 29 September and was examined on 6 October. The tablets were labelled 250 milligrammes each, and the shipment weighed 307.2 kilogrammes, the agency said.

Officers also recovered 70 parcels of Colorado weighing 75.9 kilogrammes from six ‘Ghana-Must-Go’ bags in a shipment from the United Kingdom.

The shipment arrived on 29 September and was placed under surveillance, according to the NDLEA. A clearing agent, John Edrah, 54, was arrested on 30 September.

Taofiq Ajibola, 54, an Uber driver, was later arrested while collecting one of the bags at a logistics company in Mafoluku, Oshodi. Adetunji Adebayo and Kazeem Damola Dosunmu, 48, a clothing trader, were arrested when they arrived to collect the remaining bags.

The agency noted that Mr Ajibola identified a UK-based associate, Lukman Sa’idu, as the person who sent his consignment, while Mr Dosunmu named another UK-based man, known as Yusuf, as the sender of his drugs.

Cannabis and opioid seizures across states

The agency reported further arrests and seizures in Cross River, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Kano, Kaduna and Lagos states.

In Cross River, officers arrested Adama Inuwa, 46, in Iyala Nkun village, Ikom Local Government Area, on 4 October. They recovered 181 bags of cannabis weighing 1,100 kilogrammes and 17.15 kilogrammes of cannabis seeds.

In Edo State, operatives intercepted a black Toyota Camry at Otuo, Owan East Local Government Area, on 5 October. The vehicle contained 1,049 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 702.83 kilogrammes. Three men — Monday Orji, 52, Monday Lawal, 40, and Precious Uduegele, 20 — were arrested.

In a separate raid in Benin City, officers arrested Ojugo Mercy, 26, in Asoro, off Sakponba Road. The NDLEA said they recovered 989 grammes of Loud, 13 grammes of Colorado and 83 grammes of methamphetamine.

In Ondo State, officers arrested Happy Endurance, 21, in the Shasha area of Akure, recovering 29 bags of cannabis weighing 290 kilogrammes. They also raided an apartment in Oba-Ile, Akure, on the same day and arrested Tunde Adebayo, 42, with 35 bags of cannabis weighing 351 kilogrammes.

In Taraba State, officers working with soldiers arrested Abdulrasheed Mohamed, 31, and Abubakar Saidu, 37, in Chanchanji village, Wukari Local Government Area, on 9 October. The agency said they were found with 166,200 tablets of tramadol, each labelled 225 milligrammes and weighing 107 kilogrammes in total.

On the same day, officers conducting a stop-and-search operation along the Kano-Maiduguri Road arrested Yahaya Musa, 32. They recovered 24,990 tramadol capsules, 50,000 tablets of diazepam and 22,000 tablets of Exol-5.

In Kaduna State, officers on patrol along the Zaria-Kaduna Expressway arrested Mohammed Musa, 29, with 31 jumbo bags and 775 blocks of skunk weighing a combined 1,027 kilogrammes.

In Orile, Lagos, operatives arrested Musbau Balogun Adekunle on 6 October and recovered 32.51 kilogrammes of skunk and 52.65 kilogrammes of its seeds.

NDLEA recovers firearms in Jos

In Plateau State, officers raided the residence of Christian Chukwudi Uju, 45, on Rukuba Road, Jos, on 8 October.

The NDLEA said they recovered 47 grammes of methamphetamine, two pump-action rifles, a locally made gun, 199 live cartridges, five rounds of 7.62mm ammunition and one round of 9mm ammunition.

The agency did not state whether the firearms were linked to any other criminal activity.

NDLEA Chairman Buba Marwa commended officers involved in the operations, praising their “professionalism and intelligence-driven approach”.

He urged personnel to sustain their efforts against drug trafficking and abuse.

World.title: ADC Leadership Crisis: What courts have decided, what remains unresolved
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) is facing separate legal challenges over its national leadership and the conduct of party congresses as preparations gather pace for the 2027 general elections.

While some court decisions have favoured the leadership headed by former Senate President David Mark, another ruling has restricted aspects of the party’s congress arrangements. A leadership challenge brought by Nafiu-Bala Gombe was reported to be awaiting judgment on 5 October.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) currently lists Mr Mark as ADC national chairman and former Osun State governor Rauf Aregbesola as national secretary.

The listing, checked on 11 October, reflects INEC’s published administrative position but does not resolve the legal disputes.

Bala’s leadership challenge

Mr Bala is challenging the process through which the Mark-led leadership emerged, claiming authority to act as the party’s chairman.

On 5 October, BusinessDay reported that Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja reserved judgement in the suit, FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, after counsel adopted their final written addresses.

The judge reportedly said the judgement date would be communicated to the parties.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES could not confirm whether a date has been fixed.

The dispute also involves Mr Bala’s alleged resignation.

In a letter dated 21 July 2025, the ADC informed INEC that Mr Bala resigned on 17 May and that the party accepted his resignation.

The retrieved letter refers to an attached resignation document, but the attachment was unavailable for examination. The letter could not independently establish whether Mr Bala resigned, as the document cited as evidence of his resignation was not available for examination.

What the Supreme Court decided

On 30 April, the Supreme Court set aside a Court of Appeal directive requiring the parties to maintain the status quo in the leadership dispute.

According to Channels Television, the Supreme Court returned the case to the Federal High Court for expeditious determination.

The ruling concerned the handling of the case, not a final decision on Mr Bala’s claim to the chairmanship.

The Mark-led ADC welcomed the judgement as an affirmation of its leadership, although the ruling did not determine the substantive dispute.

The separate Abejide case

Another challenge, brought by House of Representatives member Leke Abejide, produced a ruling favourable to the Mark-led leadership on 2 July.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court in Abuja considered questions of jurisdiction, standing and internal party remedies, alongside observations supporting the leadership transition.

The ADC described the decision as a striking out of the case and said it included directions concerning INEC’s recognition of its leadership.

The complete judgement and enrolled order were not obtained during the review, leaving the precise terms of the ruling unconfirmed.

The decision did not dispose of Mr Bala’s separate suit.

The congress ruling

The ADC suffered a separate setback in litigation concerning the tenure of elected state executives and the authority to organise replacement congresses.

On 13 July, the Court of Appeal upheld, by a 2–1 majority, restrictions on INEC recognising state congresses conducted through committees appointed by the Mark-led caretaker leadership.

The ruling followed a Federal High Court decision concerning the rights of existing state executives and the conduct of congresses.

Reports of the appellate judgement also referred to restrictions on interference with state executives and questions concerning a national convention.

The complete judgements and enrolled orders are required to establish which party structures and activities were affected.

The reported ruling does not establish that every ADC candidate’s nomination has become invalid.

Did ADC appeal the congress judgement?

Following the 13 July decision, the ADC announced plans to challenge the ruling at the Supreme Court.

Its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, maintained that the judgement did not affect the party’s direct primaries.

But the review did not obtain a filed notice of appeal, an appeal number or a subsequent order staying the judgment.

READ ALSO: ADC vows to publish independently collated 2027 election results

It remains unclear whether the appeal has been filed, listed or heard, or whether any stay has been granted.

What remains unresolved?

Two questions are central to the ADC’s legal position: whether the Federal High Court has fixed or delivered judgement in Mr Bala’s case, and whether a further appeal or stay has altered the effect of the July congress ruling.

The ADC and Mr Bala’s reported counsel were contacted for clarification but had not responded at the time of filing.

INEC’s published records identify the Mark-led leadership, but the outstanding questions concern the status of Mr Bala’s suit and the effect of the congress ruling. Whether either dispute affects particular nominations will depend on the applicable court orders, electoral law and circumstances of those nominations.

World.title: Fuel Discount: Makinde asks Tinubu to release petroleum pricing template
World.content:
Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Alliance People’s Movement (APM) and governor of Oyo State, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to publish the pricing template for petroleum products.

He said this is to enable Nigerians understand how pump prices are determined.

Mr Makinde made the call on Saturday in Yola, Adamawa State, during the APM North-east town hall meeting, where party stakeholders and candidates strategised ahead of the 2027 general elections.

His demand comes amid continued concerns over rising petrol prices and the federal government’s efforts to ease the burden on consumers.

On Friday, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited announced that it would extend a petrol discount introduced on 1 October to 31 October across its retail stations nationwide.

The state-owned oil company said the discount was intended to provide temporary relief to Nigerians amid elevated global crude oil prices linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

NNPC, however, clarified that the initiative did not amount to a restoration of petroleum subsidy or establish a uniform national pump price.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The company said the discount applied only to its retail outlets and did not change the market-based pricing framework for petroleum products.

Makinde criticises Tinubu’s policies

Speaking at the town hall meeting, Mr Makinde accused the Tinubu administration of failing to deliver on its promises, arguing that its policies had not significantly improved the country’s situation.

He questioned the effectiveness of government initiatives on compressed natural gas (CNG), electric vehicles, the naira-for-crude policy, insecurity and poverty reduction.

“Give us your pricing templates so that we can make our inputs as Nigerians, because government is for everyone, not only those in the corridor of power,” he said.

Mr Makinde said that if elected president in 2027, he would address the country’s challenges with sincerity and involve Nigerians in developing solutions.

He also promised to establish a transitional government of national unity that would give people from the six geopolitical zones an opportunity to contribute to national development.

“If given the mandate by Nigerian voters in 2027, our government will not allow one section of the country to dominate the system, rather it will be a transitional government of national unity,” he said.

APM seeks support ahead of 2027

In his remarks, Bala Mohammed, the party’s national leader and governor of Bauchi State, commended party members and stakeholders for supporting Mr Makinde’s visit to the North-east.

Mr Mohammed described the APM as a credible political platform capable of addressing Nigeria’s challenges and urged Nigerians to support the party and its candidates in the 2027 elections.

He said the party was committed to improving governance, addressing citizens’ needs and fulfilling its campaign promises.

Speaking on behalf of the party’s governorship candidates in the zone, Abdulrahaman Haske, the APM candidate in Adamawa State, said the candidates were working towards securing victory in 2027.

He urged party leaders, members and stakeholders to intensify campaigns across their states, local government areas, wards and polling units to challenge the ruling party.

World.title: Suspect arrested over farmer’s killing, kidnapping in Niger
World.content:
The police have arrested a 29-year-old man who allegedly contracted kidnappers to abduct and kill a large-scale farmer in Zawudna village, Munya Local Government Area, and took over the deceased’s farmland.

The police said Godwin Yahaya was arrested following allegations by rescued kidnapping victims that he conspired with kidnappers to abduct the farmer, Jonah Isah, and others for ransom.

In a crime bulletin issued on Saturday, October 10, Police Public Relations Officer Wasiu Abiodun said operatives of the State Security Service (SSS) attached to the Kuchi area arrested Mr Yahaya on 27 September and handed him over to the Sarkin-Pawa Police Division for investigation.

According to the police, the suspect allegedly confessed during interrogation that he contracted a man identified as Bashiru, who is currently at large, in 2024 to abduct Mr Isah so they could demand ransom and share the proceeds.

The police said the plan was not carried out until 26 June, 2026, when Bashiru and members of his gang allegedly invaded Zawudna village at about midnight.

The attackers reportedly entered the farmer’s residence, killed him and abducted members of his family alongside three other persons.

The abductors subsequently demanded a ransom of N2.1 million before releasing the victims, who allegedly told investigators that their captors identified Mr Yahaya as the person who contracted them to carry out the operation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Further police investigation reportedly revealed that after Mr Isah’s death, the suspect allegedly took over the deceased’s farmland for his personal use.

Police said Mr Yahaya is currently under investigation at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Minna. At the same time, efforts were ongoing to arrest Bashiru and other suspected members of the gang.

Police arrest three over transformer cable vandalism

In a related development, the police said they arrested three suspects in separate incidents involving the alleged vandalism and theft of armoured cables from electricity transformer installations in Niger State.

The first suspect, Mubarak Tanko, 25, was arrested by operatives of the Sarkin-Pawa Division, in collaboration with community members, at about 3:30 a.m. on 2 October.

The police said Mr Tanko was found with a vandalised armoured cable and allegedly confessed to cutting the cable at a community transformer with a modified cutlass, intending to sell it to scrap dealers.

The cable and the modified cutlass were recovered as exhibits, while the suspect was transferred to the SCID for further investigation and prosecution.

In another incident, police arrested two suspects, Abubakar Aliyu, 27, and Mustapha Zakari, 22, both residents of the Barkin-Sale area of Minna, after a report of transformer cable vandalism.

According to the police, the incident occurred at about 2 a.m. on 6 October at a transformer installation in Barkin-Sale, where armoured cables valued at more than N700,000 were allegedly vandalised and stolen.

The suspects reportedly confessed to the offence during interrogation, stating that they intended to sell the cables to scavengers and scrap dealers.

The police said they were holding the recovered exhibits as investigations continued.

Mr Abiodun reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling kidnapping, violent crime, vandalism and other criminal activities across the state.

World.title: Adedibu family, filmmaker clash over ‘unauthorised’ biopic as producer rejects ₦500 million demand
World.content:
The family of the late Ibadan political powerbroker, Lamidi Ariyibi Adedibu, and filmmaker Seun Oloketuyi are locked in a dispute over Adedibu: Alagbara Ibadan, a biographical film about the politician’s life and career.

The family has demanded the film’s removal, a public apology, and ₦500 million in damages, alleging it was produced without consent and contains false, damaging portrayals of Adedibu.

However, Mr Oloketuyi has rejected the allegations and refused to withdraw the production, maintaining that it draws on information already in the public domain.

Mr Oloketuyi produced the film through Ultimate Communications, and Abiodun Jimoh directed it.

Promotional materials announced a premiere on the Libra TV YouTube channel on 4 October. However, legal correspondence from both sides said a video titled Adedibu Latest Movie 2026 was published on 3 October.

The production chronicles Mr Adedibu’s life, political rise, relationships and influence in Oyo State.

Documents seen by PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday show that the dispute began shortly after the film became publicly available.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Family’s grievance



In a letter dated 5 October to the manager and producer of Libra Channel, Blossom Chambers said she was acting for the administrators and administratrix of Mr Adedibu’s estate and his family.

The lawyers alleged that the filmmakers produced and published the film without consulting the family or securing its consent.

They accused the filmmakers of presenting what they described as “grave untruths, fabrications and sensational falsehoods” about Adedibu’s private life and political career.

According to the letter, the family objected to the film’s portrayal of Mr Adedibu’s early years, bedroom, family, private life and personal lifestyle, which it said presented him as morally depraved.

It also disputed allegations in the film that he rigged elections through violence, practised “amala politics” to enslave the people of Ibadan and was a “puppet of doom.”

The family described those portrayals as malicious distortions of Mr Adedibu’s political activities and participation as a grassroots mobiliser.

The lawyers said the filmmakers neither interviewed family members nor accessed its archives. They also alleged that images, voice recordings and private family photographs were used without permission.

Family’s demands

The family consequently demanded the immediate removal of the film, including its excerpts, clips and reuploads, from YouTube and other social-media platforms.

It also asked the producer to preserve all raw footage, sources, and scripts, and to refrain from producing another documentary, film, skit, or social-media post about Mr Adedibu without the estate’s administrators’ written consent.

The lawyers further demanded that the filmmaker publish a three-minute apology on the same YouTube channel, pin it for 30 days, and publish another apology in the Nigerian Tribune within seven days.

They demanded ₦500 million as aggravated damages for what they described as an invasion of privacy, false light and injury to the family’s reputation.

The family gave the producer 48 hours from receiving the letter to comply. It threatened to submit privacy and defamation complaints to YouTube, petition the Inspector-General of Police’s Cybercrime Unit and institute an action at the Oyo State High Court if he failed to do so.

It said the proposed court action would seek ₦1 billion in damages and a perpetual injunction against the filmmaker, his agents and privies.

Filmmaker rejects claims



In a response dated 7 October, the producer’s lawyers, ASALAW LP, rejected the family’s allegations and demands.

The law firm said the family’s letter did not identify a specific statement in the film that was allegedly false or provide timestamps and evidence contradicting any of the disputed portrayals.

“The video referred to by you is a retelling of the public life and political career of a man who, by every account, was one of the most prominent, most discussed and most documented political figures in the history of Ibadan, Oyo State and South-West Nigeria,” the lawyers wrote.

They maintained that newspapers and magazines had previously reported the events portrayed in the film, and that books, academic publications, broadcast programmes, documentaries, and public debates had discussed them.

“Every fact depicted in the video is in the public domain,” the response stated.

The producer’s lawyers argued that Nigerian law generally does not require filmmakers to obtain permission from a deceased public figure’s relatives before producing a historical or political account of that person.

They, however, distinguished family consent from any copyright or proprietary rights that might exist over individual photographs, recordings or other protected materials.

They said the production used materials obtained from publicly accessible sources to compile a historical account of matters already in the public record.

They also argued that the family had not identified any photograph, recording or other material over which it held an enforceable proprietary right.

The lawyers rejected the privacy claims, maintaining that the film focused on Adedibu’s public career and political conduct rather than the private data of his surviving relatives.

They said the film did not publish the family members’ addresses, contact details, identity numbers, medical records or comparable private information.

The producer’s lawyers also disputed the family’s standing to sue for the alleged defamation of a deceased person, arguing that none of the contested statements referred personally to the surviving relatives.

The producer’s lawyers maintain these arguments, and a court has not tested or determined them.

Open offer

Despite rejecting the removal and compensation demands, the filmmakers offered the family an opportunity to identify any information it considered inaccurate.

The producer’s lawyers asked the family to provide, within seven days, the precise statements being disputed, their timestamps, their alleged meanings and documentary evidence showing that they were false.

They also requested proof that the lawyers had the authority and legal standing to act for all those identified as their clients.

The filmmakers said any specific and properly supported complaint would be considered in good faith but warned that they would defend the production against any legal action.

They further said they would submit a counter-notification if the family lodged a complaint with YouTube.

According to the response, the producer would seek compensation for lost revenue, audience, goodwill and reputational damage if the film were removed based on what he considered untrue assertions.

NFVCB approval

The National Film and Video Censors Board subsequently classified and approved the film.

A classification certificate issued by the NFVCB and seen by PREMIUM TIMES identifies the title as Adedibu, names Mr Oloketuyi as its producer and rates it 15, meaning it is not suitable for viewers below that age.

The certificate, numbered 061286, was dated 8 October, four days after the advertised premiere and three days after the family’s demand letter.

The NFVCB requires films and video works to be classified before their distribution or public exhibition in Nigeria.

The certificate establishes the film’s regulatory classification and approval. It does not, however, determine the separate dispute over the accuracy of its content, ownership of the materials used or the family’s legal claims.

Producer issues public notice

In a separate public notice, Ultimate Communications addressed claims circulating online that it had solicited money to produce the biopic.

The company denied requesting funds from any person or organisation before or after the production and described any contrary claim as false and misleading.

It said the material containing the allegations had been documented and referred to its lawyers, who would consider appropriate legal action against anyone publishing or circulating allegedly defamatory claims about the company.

Ultimate Communications described Adedibu: Alagbara Ibadan as a tribute to an iconic political figure and said it was created to share his story.

READ ALSO:

The company also said it held Adedibu’s family in high esteem and did not intend to engage it in a public dispute on social media.

The production

The biopic stars veteran actor Lere Paimo as Adedibu.

Its cast also includes Adekola Tijani, Taiwo Ibikunle, Segun Arinze, Afeez Oyetoro, Anike Ami, Shushu Abubakar and Kayode Olaiya.

Mr Oloketuyi first announced the project in 2022 to document the lives of notable Nigerians and preserve aspects of the country’s political history.

Mr Adedibu died on 11 June 2008. He was one of Oyo State’s most influential and controversial political figures and was widely described as the “strongman of Ibadan politics.”

His influence over political contests and the Peoples Democratic Party’s structure in Oyo State made him a prominent figure in Nigeria’s political history.

World.title: INEC list: Adebutu vows to challenge omission, says no cause for alarm
World.content:
Ladi Adebutu

The Ogun State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Ladi Adebutu, has assured his supporters that there is no cause for alarm following the omission of his name from the final list of governorship candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Adebutu, in a statement posted on X on Sunday, said he completed his digital party registration within the stipulated period and submitted his documentation to INEC before the deadline.

He maintained that he remained a duly registered PDP member and had not left the party.

“My documentation was duly submitted to INEC within the prescribed time. I have not at any point left the PDP, and my commitment to our great party remains unwavering,” he said.

Adebutu also said the party’s governorship primary that produced him as its candidate was conducted with INEC officials present as observers.

According to him, the relevant documents were presented for verification, certification and confirmation.

The PDP candidate expressed concern over his omission, alleging that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) had mounted undue pressure on INEC.

He said the omission raised questions, particularly because the names of the Ogun PDP candidates for the state House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate appeared on the commission’s published lists.

“The circumstances surrounding this omission raise serious questions, particularly when all the other party’s candidates across the House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senatorial positions have appeared on the published lists,” he said.

Adebutu said the party would pursue the matter through the appropriate channels and insist that due process was followed.

He also alleged that the PDP had faced attempts to frustrate its campaign, including restrictions on its billboards, attacks at campaign grounds and harassment of its members.

Despite these challenges, he urged party members and supporters to remain calm, saying the necessary steps were being taken to resolve the issue.

“No amount of intimidation should prevent the people of Ogun State from having a fair opportunity to choose leaders of their choice,” he said.

Adebutu expressed confidence that the matter would be resolved, adding that he remained committed to what he described as the struggle to deliver better leadership and relief to the people of Ogun State.

“Our cause is bigger than any individual. It is about the dignity of our people, the progress of our state and the right of Ogun people to determine our own future,” he said.

World.title: From Childhood Promise to ₦1m Prizes: Dr Nwanku Marks Birthday with Quiz Competition for Ebonyi Students
World.content:
Dr Ofobuike Nwanku

A childhood promise to ensure that academic excellence receives recognition has brought together 176 students from 27 secondary schools across Ebonyi State for the third edition of the Dr Ofobuike Nwanku Foundation quiz competition, with ₦1 million in prizes for the top three contestants.

The competition for senior secondary school students, held on October 10, 2026, at Government Technical College, Abakaliki, marked the birthday of the foundation’s founder, Dr Ofobuike Nwanku, a medical doctor practising in the United Kingdom and Chief Executive Officer of Moxie Homes & Properties Ltd, Abuja.

Now in its third year, the annual event encourages reading, rewards academic achievement and supports educational development in Ebonyi State.

Chima Testimony Ugomsinachi of King David Gifted Academy emerged as the overall winner, earning the ₦500,000 first prize. Nwafor Isioma Celine of St Theresa’s Secondary School secured second place with ₦300,000, while Obu David Chigozie, also of King David Gifted Academy, finished third, earning ₦200,000.

The contestants answered 50 objective questions comprising 20 in English Language, 15 in Mathematics and 15 in General Knowledge. Participation was free.

The Programme Director, Comrade Polycarp Obinna Alegu, confirmed that 176 students from 27 schools participated in the exercise. He said the competition concluded successfully, adding that teachers who accompanied their students commended the transparency of the process.

The winners received ceremonial cheques at the venue. Alegu said he would visit their respective schools on Monday, October 12, to present the cash prizes in the presence of their parents and teachers.

He congratulated the winners, thanked his organising team and commended Dr Nwanku for sponsoring the programme.

For Dr Nwanku, the initiative carries a personal significance rooted in his own experience as a schoolboy representing Ebonyi State in academic competitions.

Growing up in Umuoghara, Ezza North Local Government Area, he represented his school in competitions at local, state and national levels. He recalled emerging as a state champion on several occasions, but receiving little recognition or material encouragement for those achievements.

In 2005, he represented Ebonyi State at the Science Teachers Association of Nigeria competition in Jos and the Junior Engineers, Technicians and Scientists competition in Abuja. At the latter, he was part of a team of five students from the state that finished second.

Despite the effort involved, the absence of rewards became discouraging. His parents, concerned that the competitions offered little encouragement for his hard work, at one point urged him to stop participating.

That experience inspired a promise: if he had the means in future, he would sponsor competitions and reward deserving students so that their efforts would be recognised.

The annual quiz competition is an expression of that commitment, giving young people the encouragement he wished he had received.

Dr Nwanku said the programme was designed to strengthen reading habits among students and complement government efforts to make education more rewarding for children. He also thanked Alegu and his organising team for delivering the third edition.

Alegu said the initiative also sought to support the efforts of Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru’s administration in advancing education in Ebonyi State.

A native of Ebiaji village in Ogharugo community, Umuoghara, Dr Nwanku began his education at Community Primary School, Ogharugo. He later attended Urban Model Secondary School, Okpaugwu, Abakaliki, and St Theresa’s Secondary School, Abakaliki, one of the schools represented among this year’s winners.

He studied Medicine and Surgery at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, graduating in 2018, and completed his housemanship at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital. He subsequently undertook his National Youth Service Corps programme at the Guards Brigade Medical Centre, Mambilla Barracks, Asokoro, Abuja.

He went on to earn a master’s degree in Public Health at Teesside University in the United Kingdom, where his academic work included published articles on waste management. He has practised medicine in the United Kingdom since 2023.

Alongside his medical career, Dr Nwanku leads Moxie Homes & Properties Ltd, an Abuja based real estate company involved in property development, real estate investment, infrastructure and housing solutions. Through the business, he also contributes to employment and opportunities for young people.

His foundation focuses on healthcare, education and human development. Its activities have included free healthcare services for rural communities and people in need, assistance with school fees for disadvantaged students, and support for community development.

For Dr Nwanku, dedicating his birthday to the competition gives a personal celebration a wider purpose: recognising hard work and helping another generation of students see value in learning.

World.title: ‘Journalism going to dogs’ — ‘You’re guilty as charged’: Dabiri, Oseni clash
World.content:
Abike Dabiri-Erewa and Rufai Oseni.

Abike Dabiri-Erewa, chairperson of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM), and Rufai Oseni, co-host of Arise Television’s The Morning Show, have traded words over allegations of irresponsible journalism and a controversial social media post.

The exchange followed Dabiri’s criticism of declining journalistic standards at a panel session in Lagos on Saturday, during an event marking Kike Abati’s 20th anniversary in the media industry.

Dabiri accused some journalists of abandoning professional values, recounting how Oseni had allegedly misinterpreted her response to a social media post as an endorsement of an offensive description of Igbo people.

She said the controversy began after she responded with a smiling emoji to a post by a social media user she identified as Stephanie, who allegedly operated an X account under the name “Voice of Igbos”.

According to Dabiri, Oseni subsequently accused her of describing Igbo people as “monkeys and gorillas”.

“Somebody replies to her. Then I do a smiley. And then Rufai Oseni comes and says, Abike Dabiri calls everybody — Igbos — monkeys and gorillas,” she said.

Dabiri maintained that she had not made the statement attributed to her, faulting journalists for amplifying claims without exercising due responsibility.

“We have to ensure that you hold people responsible, but you must be responsible yourself. So we will not accept irresponsible journalism,” she said.

The NiDCOM chairperson added: “And let me tell you, some journalism is going to the dogs. There’s no journalism anymore. There are no standards. There are no values.”

Oseni fires back

Responding in a series of posts on X, Oseni accused Dabiri of using the public event to attack him instead of addressing issues affecting Nigerians living abroad.

“Abike Dabiri is more concerned about attacking Rufai Oseni in public instead of doing her job,” he wrote.

The journalist also rejected Dabiri’s explanation of the social media controversy, insisting that her use of a laughing emoji amounted to endorsing a post that denigrated an ethnic group.

“You are guilty as charged. How can you share a laughter emoji at a post that denigrates a tribal group? I put it to you, your laughter here was an endorsement of a denigrating tweet against a certain ethnic group,” he said.

Oseni challenged Dabiri to a public debate, saying he was prepared to defend his position.

“Your problem is you can’t stand the truth. I will like to challenge you to a debate on this issue where I will speak the truth to your face and prove to the world you endorse bigotry,” he wrote.

He also urged the NiDCOM chairperson to focus on the commission’s responsibilities rather than their public disagreement.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo surgery to remove lung nodule
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV delivers his speech during the weekly general audience at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican on October 7, 2026. (Photo by Andreas SOLARO / AFP)

Pope Leo XIV on Sunday announced he would have an operation “in the coming days” for a lump on his lung, saying it had been located “at a very early stage”.

“During recent medical checks, a nodule on my lung was found. It has been detected at a very early stage and is very localised,” the 71-year-old said in a weekly address in St Peter’s Square.

“The doctors believe it would be right to intervene and so, following their advice, I have decided to have the operation to remove it. The operation is already planned in the coming days,” he said.

Following the pope’s statement during his Angelus prayers, the Vatican press office said the pontiff was expected to have surgery in the next few days, and the expected recovery time from the operation would be around one week.

The operation was to take place in the Gemelli hospital in Rome, which has frequently treated popes since John Paul II.

No information has been given as to whether the surgery and recovery would affect the pope’s agenda for international trips. He is next due to go to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru between November 6 and 17.

– ‘Calmness’ –

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said in a statement that the “calmness with which he spoke during today’s Angelus reassures us”.

She expressed to the pope her “personal closeness, and that of the Italian government, as he confronts this ordeal of the coming days”.

Chicago-born Leo became the first US pope last year following the death of his Argentine predecessor Francis on April 21, 2025 at the age of 88.

Leo was elected leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics on May 8, 2025.

The former Robert Francis Prevost, while less ebullient than his predecessor, has gradually imprinted his style on the leadership of the Catholic Church, finding his voice as he takes on some of the world’s most pressing issues, from bloody conflicts to artificial intelligence.

After the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, the pope became a high-profile critic of the conflict.

He condemned US President Donald Trump’s threat to destroy Iran as “truly unacceptable” and urged Americans to demand that US lawmakers “work for peace”.

Trump slammed the pontiff as “WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy” — to which Leo replied that he had a “moral duty to speak out”.

World.title: INEC list: NDC says error caused omission of Kano governorship candidate
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has blamed an error for the omission of its Kano State governorship candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdulsalam Gwarzo, and his running mate, Mustapha Rabi’u Kwankwaso, from the list of candidates published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

INEC released the list of candidates for various positions on Saturday, but the names of the NDC governorship candidate and his running mate were missing from the Kano State section.

Dr Yusuf Ibrahim Kofarmata, Secretary of the Kwankwasiyya Caucus and the NDC House of Representatives candidate in Kano in a statement said the party had received assurances that the omission resulted from an error in entering the candidates’ details.

He said INEC was working to correct the problem.

He expressed confidence that the names would be included.

Kofarmata said Gwarzo completed his registration within the period set by INEC.

He added that the party submitted the candidate’s details through the commission’s online portal.

Kofarmata urged party supporters to remain calm and continue their activities despite the development.

World.title: Vanguard summit: Mental health neglect threatens Nigeria’s stability – Sheikh
World.content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria’s neglect of mental health is threatening social stability, weakening public trust and deepening despair among young people struggling with insecurity, and diminishing their confidence in the future, Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a leading psychiatrist, has warned.

Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry and psychopharmacology at the Department of Psychiatry, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, called on the Federal Government to implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 and expand access to affordable care, particularly at the community level, warning that untreated psychological distress could weaken families, fracture communities and erode confidence in public institutions.

Speaking at the 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit held at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, Sheikh said in a presentation titled “Mental Health as Social Capital: The Hidden Wealth of Nations” that mental wellbeing was fundamental to the trust, relationships and cooperation societies need to function.

He described mental health as one of the most neglected areas of healthcare, particularly in Africa and Nigeria, where inadequate investment has constrained access to services, especially community-based care.

“Nigeria faces a serious social capital crisis. We are a nation of about 230 million people, with a large youth population, yet our social indicators raise troubling questions about trust, cohesion and confidence in the future. Low trust in institutions and tensions between communities weaken the relationships that hold society together,” he said.

Sheikh identified insecurity, family breakdown, substance misuse and the growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country as issues that must be understood beyond their immediate economic and social dimensions.

“When you live in survival mode, you cannot plan for tomorrow. The growing desire among young Nigerians to leave the country is not only an economic or migration issue. For some, it also reflects a loss of confidence in the future.

“Family breakdown and substance use, including the misuse of codeine and other psychoactive substances, must also be understood in context. They can reflect deeper psychological distress.”

He warned that prolonged exposure to violence and trauma could undermine the trust and social bonds needed to rebuild communities and sustain development.

“Consider a child who grows up in Kaduna witnessing killings and receiving no psychological support. That child may grow up hypervigilant and deeply mistrustful. How will such an adult trust the state? How will that person nurture the next generation?” he asked.

According to Sheikh, the consequences of insecurity extend beyond deaths, displacement and property losses to include lasting psychological harm that can affect how survivors relate to others, engage with institutions and raise their families.

On the way forward, he said: “First, we must strengthen the mental health system and expand access to affordable, quality care, particularly at the community level. Second, we must implement the National Mental Health Act 2021 rather than allow its provisions to remain largely on paper. Third, we must ensure that attempted suicide is no longer treated as a criminal offence and that people in crisis receive appropriate care and support.”

Further, Sheikh stressed that mental health should be treated as a national and humanitarian priority, with services available close to where people live rather than concentrated in specialist facilities.

He also cautioned against viewing mental wellbeing solely through its economic benefits, noting that untreated mental health conditions could affect education, employment, productivity and quality of life, while access to care could produce benefits for individuals and society.

“The bridge between poverty and prosperity is not infrastructure alone; it requires mental health. The bridge between conflict and peace is not negotiation alone; it also requires trauma healing and reconciliation,” he said.

Explaining the relationship between mental health and social capital, Sheikh noted, “Psychological wellbeing could help people build relationships, participate in community life and cooperate with others. In turn, supportive family ties, friendships and wider social networks could reduce loneliness, provide emotional support and help people cope with adversity.

“The relationship works both ways. Mental health can help generate social capital, while social capital can support mental wellbeing,” he said, adding that supportive relationships and access to opportunities were essential to ensuring that people could benefit from these connections.

“Without mental health, there is no sustainable social development. Without social capital, there is no development, and without development, there is no lasting prosperity,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Be realistic ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‌⁠‍​​⁠‍‌​in campaign promises, APC chieftain tells Atiku, Obi
World.content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun, Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has urged the presidential candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, to be realistic in their campaign promises to Nigerians.

Oyintiloye, who spoke with newsmen on Sunday in Osogbo, said the campaign promises made by Atiku, Obi and other presidential candidates were unrealistic, given the country’s current economic realities.

He said the promise by Atiku and Obi to restore fuel subsidy was unrealistic and could cause chaos in the country.

According to him, all tiers and arms of government have adjusted to operating without fuel subsidy under the current administration.

“It is practically impossible to think of returning Nigeria to the era of fuel subsidy.

“Alhaji Atiku and Mr Obi should be mindful of the implications of whatever promises they make to attract Nigerians’ attention ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, also promised to peg the pump price of petrol at N300 per litre if elected. How realistic is that?

“I appeal to opposition candidates to be truthful to themselves and stop deceiving Nigerians. The majority of their promises are nothing but a recipe for public chaos,” he said.

Oyintiloye, a former lawmaker, noted that fuel subsidy removal and foreign exchange reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu had driven major fiscal adjustments, although they had also placed considerable pressure on households and businesses.

He said increased allocations from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) had given state governments greater financial flexibility to meet their obligations, execute development projects and address infrastructure and social-service deficits.

Oyintiloye urged opposition candidates to support the Federal Government’s efforts to reposition the economy or adopt alternative campaign strategies rather than make promises they might be unable to fulfil.

“Presently, salaries and wages are based on the government’s earnings after fuel subsidy removal.

“With the restoration of fuel subsidy that these candidates are promising, will salaries and wages also be reviewed downward?

“What will be the earnings of states following the restoration of fuel subsidy? What will become of the several ongoing government projects awarded based on its current earnings? Nigerians are wiser,” Oyintiloye said.

The APC chieftain, however, called on state governors to demonstrate accountability by translating increased revenue into better roads, improved healthcare, increased food production, regular payment of salaries and pensions, and more employment opportunities.

According to him, citizens expect tangible improvements in their living conditions rather than increased government revenue without visible benefits at the grassroots.

He also urged the Federal Government to sustain efforts to ease the economic burden on vulnerable households, curb inflationary pressures, expand employment opportunities and improve purchasing power.

Oyintiloye further urged Nigerians to assess the Federal Government’s economic reforms objectively, expressing optimism that they would eventually yield positive results for the benefit all.

World.title: NDDC Director Takes Over As ISMNC Rivers Chair
World.content:
. Pledges results-driven leadership

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Director of Planning, Research and Statistics at the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr Patterson Ogon, has assumed office as Chairman of the Rivers State Chapter of the Institute of Strategic Management of Nigeria (ISMNC), pledging to promote professional excellence, ethical leadership and measurable results.

Ogon formally took over the chapter’s administrative affairs following a handover ceremony held at the weekend in Port Harcourt, after his election to the position.

Speaking at the chapter’s inaugural meeting, swearing-in ceremony and handover of administrative responsibilities, the new chairman said his administration would consolidate the achievements of his predecessors while strengthening the institute’s role in professional development and strategic leadership.

He said the chapter would serve as a platform for strategic thinking, intellectual development, mentorship and collaboration, stressing that membership must offer tangible opportunities for learning, networking and professional growth.

“Strategy must translate into practical outcomes. Every programme and initiative undertaken by this chapter must have clear objectives, create demonstrable value and deliver measurable results,” Ogon said.

He identified continuous professional development as a major priority, noting that technological advancement, artificial intelligence, changing economic realities and evolving leadership expectations had made adaptability essential for professionals.

According to him, his administration will promote seminars, workshops and knowledge-sharing engagements while strengthening mentorship and intergenerational learning to combine the experience of established professionals with the innovative ideas and technological awareness of younger members.

Ogon also pledged to promote transparency, accountability and professional ethics, assuring members that the chapter’s resources would be managed prudently in their collective interest.

He called for stronger collaboration among members, state chapters, regional structures and the institute’s national leadership, urging professionals to contribute their expertise and opportunities towards advancing the organisation.

The National President and Chairman-in-Council of ISMNC, Ndudi Enebeli, welcomed the leadership transition, describing the Rivers State chapter as particularly significant to him.

Enebeli, however, expressed concern over growing apathy among members of professional bodies in Rivers State, challenging the new executive to develop strategies to encourage participation and re-engage inactive members.

He urged members to see the institute as a platform for continuous learning rather than participating only when specific programmes offered immediate personal benefits.

“Communication, cooperation and collaboration are essential elements of successful leadership and teamwork,” he said, while encouraging the outgoing executive to mentor and support the new leadership.

Enebeli also commended the Rivers chapter’s contributions to the institute’s national leadership, noting that it had produced the national president and had been recognised as the institute’s best-performing chapter in successive periods.

Earlier, a former chairman, Nathan Excellence, thanked members of his executive committee for their support during approximately two years in office.

Excellence said his administration was handing over a more structured institute with improved capacity to deliver on its objectives, expressing confidence that the new leadership would consolidate the gains recorded and advance the chapter’s growth.

World.title: NCWS Demands Urgent Action Against Child Marriage
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

More than 24 million Nigerian women and girls alive today were married before their 18th birthday, the National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) has warned, demanding urgent action to end child marriage.

In a statement on Sunday to mark the International Day of the Girl Child, the council said Nigeria, which is among countries with the highest numbers of child brides globally, cannot meet its 2030 deadline to end the practice without funded interventions and enforcement of the law.

The NCWS, under the theme ‘End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights,’ cited UNICEF figures and the 2023-2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, which showed 33.4 per cent of women aged 20-24 were married before 18, with prevalence approaching 50 per cent in the North-east and North-west.

Its National President, Princess Edna Azura, described child marriage as a national development crisis, not a private family matter.

The council said poverty is a major driver, with girls from poor households far more likely to marry in adolescence. It warned of severe health consequences such as eclampsia, infections, obstetric fistula, prematurity and low birth weight, as well as lifelong loss of education and economic opportunities.

It cited about 7.6 million out-of-school girls nationwide, noting that women without formal education marry at a median age of 16.6 years compared to 21.7 years for those who complete secondary education.

According to the council, investing $114 million in out-of-school girls in two northern states alone could generate $2.5 billion (about N3.6 trillion) in economic benefits, based on a 2025 study by UNICEF and the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs.

The NCWS said despite all 36 states adopting the Child Rights Act, implementation remains weak.

It demanded enforcement of Section 21 of the Act, which sets 18 as the minimum age of marriage, and called on the National Assembly to review Section 29(4)(b) of the Constitution which deems a married woman to be of full age.

It also called for free birth registration, compulsory registration of all marriages with age verification, training for police, prosecutors, judges and customary and Sharia court officials and functional family courts.

The council outlined an eight-point action plan including enforcement of the marriage age, safe completion of secondary education for girls, school feeding, conditional cash transfers, menstrual hygiene support, recruitment of female teachers, second-chance education for married girls and young mothers, targeted financial assistance for poor households, and funded child protection desks, helplines, safe shelters and adolescent-friendly healthcare.

It urged traditional rulers, imams and pastors to promote later marriage and called for release of funds for the Costed National Action Plan to End Child Marriage with dedicated budget lines and annual public reporting.

“A girl’s childhood is not ours to give away,” Azura said, urging government, families and communities to protect girls’ health and allow them to determine their futures.

World.title: Igueben Attack: Imansuagbon, Okonofua Petition Police, DSS, Seek Probe
World.content:
A former Edo State governorship aspirant and African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain, Kenneth Imasuangbon, and the party’s Edo Central senatorial candidate, Hon. Herberta Okonofua, have petitioned the police and Department of State Services (DSS) over an alleged armed attack last week on their entourage in Igueben Local Government Area of Edo State.

In the petition dated October 8, 2026, and addressed to the Edo State Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daor, with a copy to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Tunji Disu, the petitioners demanded a thorough investigation into the October 6 incident.

They alleged that an ADC supporter, Jerry Oliha, sustained serious gunshot injuries and was rushed to Irrua Specialist Hospital. Campaign canopies, chairs, musical equipment and other materials were also reportedly destroyed.

According to the petition, the entourage encountered confrontations in Wards 4 and 5 before armed men allegedly opened fire at the premises of the Enogie of Igueben.

The petitioners urged investigators to identify two Sienna buses allegedly linked to the incident, trace their ownership and movements, and establish whether they were used to transport the suspected attackers.

They further alleged that the vehicles’ number plates were removed and that the vehicles or plates were taken to a property reportedly associated with Igueben Council Chairman, Endurance Azemegbe, who had earlier denied involvement in the incident.

Imasuangbon and Okonofua asked the security agencies to investigate whether Azemegbe or any other persons directed or facilitated the alleged attack.

They stressed that the allegations were for investigation and did not constitute proof of guilt.

They also called for the preservation and forensic examination of evidence, including bullet casings, medical records, photographs, video footage, CCTV recordings and vehicle documents.

Names of individuals reportedly linked to the incident were also submitted to assist investigators.

The petitioners urged the police and DSS to determine whether the attack was isolated or connected to previous alleged threats against members of their political camp.

They also requested adequate security for themselves, campaign officials and supporters during lawful political activities.

“We remain committed to pursuing our political activities through constitutional and democratic means,” they said, calling for an impartial investigation free from political interference to establish the facts and prevent further violence.

World.title: Nnaji Promises Free Shops for Traders Displaced by Market Demolitions In Enugu
World.content:
* Pledges tax relief, free healthcare for elderly

Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has promised to rebuild demolished markets and provide free shops to affected traders if elected governor in 2027.

He also pledged tax relief, industrialisation and free healthcare for elderly residents, saying his administration would prioritise job creation and the welfare of citizens.

Nnaji made the promises while receiving a coalition of interest groups at his campaign office in Enugu Saturday. The delegation included leaders of the Arewa Northern Forum, traders and artisans displaced from Gariki Market, members of the Inter-Faith Council and non-indigene communities.

The groups expressed support for his candidacy but lamented the hardship allegedly caused by market demolitions, multiple taxation and difficulties in securing trading spaces.

Responding, Nnaji said his administration would review the circumstances surrounding the demolitions and construct replacement markets, with shops allocated to affected traders free of charge where resources permitted.

“My intention is to use public resources to build the markets and give the shops to their original owners free of charge,” he said, adding that a phased arrangement involving minimal payments might be considered if necessary.

Nnaji also promised to review the state’s tax regime, abolish what he described as excessive taxes and pursue industrial development in the oil, cement, iron ore and steel sectors to create jobs.

“I will run a government that is participatory, transparent and accountable,” he said. “We will make sure that public funds reflect the needs of residents across the state.”

Earlier, the leader of the Arewa Northern Forum, Innocent Iwual, said the association had existed for 19 years, with members across Enugu State, adding that members of the northern community had participated in previous elections but were disappointed by what he described as unfulfilled political promises.

Also speaking, a PDP chieftain, Basil Ani, described Nnaji as a man who kept his promises, expressing confidence that the candidate would fulfil his commitments if elected governor.

World.title: GBB Promises to Increase Numbers of Digitalised MDA’s from Current 30, Says Adeyanju
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The Managing Director of Galaxy Backbone (GBB), Prof. Ibrahim Adeyanju, has disclosed that with 30 Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDA’s) digitalised, going forward GBB is going to digitalise more MDA’s.

Prof. Adeyanju made the disclosure at a breakfast engagement with GBB customers organised to celebrate and commemorate customer service week 2026, with the theme: “Going the Extra Mile” on Friday in Àbuja

Prof. Adeyanju speaking on GBB’s achievements and what they hope to achieve going forward he said , “We’ve gone quite far. So even with the last head of service, Mrs. Didi, Esther Watson-Jack, we are able to digitalize no less than over 30 MDAs that actually moved to one government platform and are now using our platform to approve documents, memos and basically ensuring that we have less paper. So we’re also saving government a lot of money because less paper is being used, less trees can fall and then you have a lot of cost savings from that.

“Moving forward, like I said, we want to continue to improve our services. We want to increase adoption of the paperless service and we want to continue to satisfy our customers and extend our tentacles to some of the places where we don’t currently have a presence.”

Speaking earlier he said, “We’re involved in the digital transformation of the federal government, moving from the paperless workflows to an automated workflow. We are working with basically all the ministries, departments and agencies to ensure that digital is not just something on paper. It’s something that would improve the efficiency of government, improve transparency and improve the effectiveness of our civil servants as well.

In his response to a complaint by Head ICT/Marketing and Business Development National Power Training Institute of Nigeria, Dr. Olalekan Oregbefon, who said, “I must commend GBB for the quality of service they’re providing but I must also urge them to improve on their response to customers complaints by not just telling us, we’ll fix the issue but stating the exact time it will take.

Prof. Adeyanju said, “Don’t get tired because there are times where you have multiple escalations. The people that report first are the ones that get attended to. Not because others were not attended to, but it might take a bit more time.

“Please don’t get tired of calling. Don’t get tired of escalating issues when there are issues.” This was his response to .

Earlier in his speech he said, “at Galaxy, we believe our customers are much more than the organisations we serve. You are the reason we keep pushing, improving and sometimes working long after the normal working day should have ended. And if we’re being honest, there have been quite a few of those days.

In his opening remarks, the Executive Director, Customer Centricity and Marketing, GBB, Olusegun Olulade who was represented by the Group Head Human Resource, Mr. Olugbenga Omoniyi , said “At Galaxy Backbone, customer centricity is not simply a phrase we use during Customer Service Week. It is one of our core values and a fundamental part of who we are as an organisation. It reminds us that technology, infrastructure and digital solutions only have meaning when they solve real problems and create real value for the people and organisations we serve.”

In her presentation the Head Marketing and Business Intelligence, Ifeatu Anafulu, said, “Our mission is to deliver secure, scalable, innovative digital solutions that empower government and businesses

“Digital transformation is not just at the center here in Abuja, but also including the sub-nationals in our mission to become the digital transformation partner of the country. One of the ways that we achieve this, the thing that makes us unique, is our GBV advantage.”
