World.title: PDP: Adebutu’s Name Will Be Published on INEC List
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State has expressed confidence that the name of its governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, will be published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The party, in a statement signed by its Publicity Secretary, Arc. Kayode Adebayo, urged the people of Ogun State to remain calm, assuring them that Adebutu would emerge as governor in the 2027 general elections.

The PDP attributed the omission of its candidate’s name from INEC’s list to what it described as “the undue pressure mounted by the ruling party on INEC out of fear of losing the election to our party.”

The party stated that Adebutu had never left the PDP and had duly registered as a member within the designated period of the digital registration exercise.

It added that his party membership card had been “printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time.”

While urging the people of Ogun State not to be perturbed or distracted from its focus of voting out the All Progressives Congress (APC), the PDP said it remained “resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident” about its candidate’s prospects in the 2027 governorship election.

The statement added that “no amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts, or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State.”

The party also called on its supporters, party faithful and the general public to remain “steadfast, vigilant, and unintimidated” as its movement to rescue Ogun State and bring relief to the people continued to gain momentum.

World.title: Pantami, Adebutu, Gwarzo Missing in INEC’s Final List of Gombe, Kano, Ogun Guber Candidates
World.content:
*Gwarzo remains our candidate, Kano NDC insist

Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has published its final list of candidates for the February 6, 2027 governorship elections, with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidates for Gombe and Ogun states, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, missing.

However, INEC cleared the APC governorship candidate in Rivers State, Kingsley Chinda for the 2027 governorship election in the state.



Chinda was number five in the 19-man list of Rivers State governorship candidates released by the electoral commission.

The lists, signed by INEC Secretary, Rose Oriaran-Anthony and published on the INEC website yesterday, showed 16 governorship candidates of other political parties in Gombe State and 13 in Ogun State, and none of them was from the PDP.

The governorship candidates missing were Ali Pantami of PDP in Gombe State, Aminu Gwarzo of NDC in Kano State and Ladi Adebutu of PDP in Ogun State.



However, the Kano State Chairman of NDC, Alhaji Hussaini Mairiga, has insisted that Gwarzo remains the governorship candidate of the party in the state.

INEC did not publicly state the specific reason for dropping the candidates’ names but the decision was believed to be connected to a Supreme Court ruling in the case of INEC v. Zenith Labour Party, which confirmed the continued validity of Section 77 of the Electoral Act 2026.



The commission released the list in line with the promise of its Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, who spoke at a press conference in Abuja early last week.



Pantami, who was on the provisional list published on August 29, was missing from the new list.

Pantami had earlier emerged as a PDP candidate after dumping APC on May 19. But Ahmed Mailantarki, one of the aspirants who sought the PDP ticket, challenged his victory in court.



A Federal High Court in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which he won again.

Pantami won the rerun primary conducted on September 29, defeating Khamisu Mailantarki and Usman Aliyu Garry.

But his biggest obstacle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgment, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, barring parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time.



While uncertainty trailed his participation in the election, Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had hinted that in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027.

Under Section 32(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, parties have 14 days to notify INEC in writing, with an affidavit, if a nominated candidate’s name is missing.



In Kano State, Gwarzo’s removal from the final list means he cannot contest the governorship election on the NDC platform.

In Ogun State, neither Adebutu nor his running mate, Kolapo-Sowunmi, appeared in the list, raising questions about the status of the PDP’s governorship ticket ahead of the poll.



Speculations have emerged that Adebutu’s name may not have been included in the party register submitted to INEC, as required under the provisions of the Electoral Act.



Hoever, the PDP has urged residents of the state to be calm and rest assured that its governorship candidate, Adebutu’s name would be published by INEC and he will emerge as the Governor of Ogun State in the 2027 general election.



A statement by the publicity Secretary of PDP in Ogun State, Kayode Adebayo urged the public to be informed that the omission of its candidate’s name in the INEC’s list was as a result of the undue pressure mounted by the ruling party on INEC out of fear of losing the election to our party.



“We state emphatically that our candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, who has never left the Peoples Democratic Party at any time duly registered as a member of the party within the designated period of the digital registration with his party membership card printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time.



“While we urge the good people of Ogun not to be perturbed nor distracted from our focus of voting out the APC, we remain resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident that our candidate is marching straight to a decisive victory in the Ogun 2027 Governorship election.



“No amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts, or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State who are overwhelmingly eager for true leadership and positive change.”

Reacting to the omission of his name from the final list of candidates, Pantami, in a statement shared on his personal social media handles, assured his supporters that efforts were underway to resolve the issue, describing the omission as a temporary challenge in the electoral process.



In the statement signed by Professor Suleiman Mohammed Gombe, he said the development has reportedly raised questions among supporters of the PDP and the Pantamiyya Movement across Gombe and beyond.

He urged supporters to remain calm and hopeful, insisting that the omission did not represent a final determination of the matter.



According to the camp, its legal and liaison teams are engaging with relevant organs of the PDP and INEC to ensure compliance with the court order and correct the omission within the period allowed by law.

Gwarzo Remains Our Candidate, Says Kano NDC Chairman

Meanwhile, the Kano State Chairman of NDC, Alhaji Hussaini Mairiga, last night dismissed any notion of a change in the party’s ticket, insisting that the structure of the ticket remained entirely intact as originally planned.

Speaking during a telephone interview, Mairiga insisted that the joint ticket of NDC’s gubernatorial candidate and his running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, was duly processed, finalised, and submitted to the electoral body in strict accordance with all established electoral guidelines and statutory deadlines.



“Gwarzo’s name was submitted to INEC, and he and his running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, are the authentic flag bearers of the party,” Mairiga stated emphatically, reiterating the party’s unwavering backing for their chosen candidates.

Addressing the discrepancies observed in the newly published list, the chairman attributed the development to administrative friction rather than an official rejection by the commission.



He suggested that human error or a logistical miscommunication within the broader bureaucratic process likely triggered the anomaly.

“I believe there is a mix-up somewhere, and I do not think the list is from the commission, since we are sure that the name we submitted is what stands,” Mairiga added.

World.title: Akume: 1999 North-South Power Rotation Agreement Favours Tinubu’s Re-election Bid
World.content:
*North-central endorses president as sole candidate for 2027 election

*First Lady, govs, SGF, Yilwatda defend Tinubu’s second term ambition

*Tinubu inaugurates APC Presidential Campaign Council October 14

Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, has disclosed that the 1999 agreement between northerners and southerners to rotate power for eight years between the North and the South is in favour of the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the North will only produce the president in 2031 when the incumbent completes his eight years.



Akume stated this yesterday in Lafia, Nasarawa State, during the endorsement of President Tinubu at a grand rally organised for the president’s re-election by the North-central zone of the All Progressives Congress (APC), under the auspices of the North-Central Grassroots Mobilisation Network.



This comes as the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu; governors of Benue, Plateau, Niger, Kogi, Kwara, and Nasarawa states; and Akume have given reasons why Tinubu deserves a second term, saying his administration has transitioned from difficult reforms to visible prosperity.



Meanwhile, President Tinubu will inaugurate the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14, with former Zamfara State governor Senator Abdulaziz Yari, Imo State Governor Senator Hope Uzodimma, and other party chieftains expected to play key roles.



The North-central APC rally drew governors, senators and elders from Benue, Plateau, Niger, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).



Addressing APC supporters who intermittently chanted “Tinubu! Tinubu!”, the First Lady said the president believed in the country’s unity, security, and prosperity.

She said her address was centred on the president’s Independence Day message on October 1 titled “From Reforms to Prosperity.”



According to her, “after two years of reforming critical sectors, it is now time for benefits to reach Nigerians”.

“Mr. President is saying that they have gone reforming a lot of sectors, but now is the time for prosperity. And we can see our economy is stabilising, foreign exchange is going down, and investors are coming back to Nigeria,” she noted.



Drawing on her 12 years in the Senate, she said the current dispensation witnessed unusual infrastructure activity.

“I have been in the Senate for 12 years. This is the first time I have seen governors fixing roads and building a lot of infrastructure. And we’ve seen now in the health sector,” she stated.



She highlighted a food bank initiative providing free nutritious food for children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers, as well as treatment for malnourished children. She urged students to take advantage of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).



Describing Tinubu as bold and courageous, she charged supporters to become ambassadors.

“Tell everyone that Mr. President, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, is a leader who is very bold and not afraid to take difficult decisions. He’s a leader who can be trusted to lead us into prosperity,” she said.

“Vote for continuity, vote for capacity, vote for prosperity, vote for the reelection of Mr. President, and all the candidates of APC all the way from top to bottom,” she added.



Speaking at the rally, Akume insisted that the parties agreed to rotate power between the North and the South in 1999.

“I want us to consider one thing – that we agreed in Kaduna in 1999 to ensure that power rotates between the North and the South – eight years in the South, and eight years in the North.



“Yesterday, our father (Buhari) made his sojourn in peace. He was on the throne for eight years. Today, Asiwaju (Tinubu) is expected to serve eight years. In 2031, northerners can field over 1,000 candidates. So, anybody from the North who is running for President today is not sincere. Let’s reject him 100 per cent, and I urge you not to accept him,” Akume told APC leaders and supporters.



“You talk of education; more universities have been established, and above all, you have the NELFUND student loan scheme so that because of the circumstances of your birth, you can never be denied tertiary education,” Akume declared.



Moving the motion for Tinubu’s adoption as sole presidential candidate in 2027, the SGF said: “There are so many things that this great man, this visionary, has done. He deserves something more than that, and therefore, by the authority of this great congregation, I, Senator George Akume, former Governor of Benue State for eight years, former Senator for 12 years, former Minister for four years, and now Secretary to the Government of the Federation, do now propose that the people of the North-Central zone meeting in this great congregation have resolved that come 2027, our sole candidate for that election is His Excellency, Bola Ahmed Tinubu; there is no other candidate.”

Akume also described all the presidential candidates who had previously promised subsidy removal but made a U-turn, promising to reverse it if elected, as insincere to Nigerians.



According to him, “that is what we call policy flip-flop, policy flip-flop. The idea is to deceive you; don’t be deceived”.

Akume’s motion was seconded by the Governor of Nasarawa State, Abdullah Sule, on behalf of the governors of Kogi, Benue, Niger, Kwara, Plateau states and the people of the FCT.



Governor Sule argued that “for a man who has actually improved our oil production from less than one million to now 1. 8 million barrels per day, a man who has improved our foreign reserves from less than $20 billion to now $40 to $50 billion, for a man who has improved the capital market capitalisation of less than N80 trillion to now over N160 trillion; a man who has introduced students’ loan for education; a man who has introduced all the infrastructure that you are seeing, I second the motion that Bola Ahmed Tinubu becomes our one and only candidate for the 2027 election”.



On his part, the National Chairman of APC, Prof. Nantawe Yilwatda, also highlighted Tinubu’s major achievements in many sectors, especially the construction of roads across the North-central and several political appointments given to the region and urged the voters in the region to reciprocate that kind gesture on January 16, 2027, by voting massively for the president’s re-election.

Tinubu Inaugurates APC Presidential Campaign Council October 14

In a related development, President Tinubu will inaugurate the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14.

Former Zamfara State governor, Senator Yari; Imo State Governor Uzodimma; former minister Dr Edu; and other party chieftains will play key roles.



The inauguration is scheduled to take place at the Presidential Villa’s Banquet Hall in Abuja.

In a statement issued yesterday, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Yari, disclosed this on Friday after meeting with the President at the Presidential Villa, where he briefed State House correspondents on preparations for the forthcoming campaign.



Yari said: “The President had approved the proposed campaign timetable; activities would commence with a rally in Kaduna on October 24.”

According to the campaign schedule, the rally will be followed by engagements in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State.



Ahead of the formal inauguration, Nigeria’s First Lady, in collaboration with the Director of Women Mobilisation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Edu, and other members of the directorate, has commenced grassroots mobilisation of women across the country.



Edu and her team have set a target of mobilising 40 million women voters for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket through a strategy covering 176,846 communities and polling-unit structures across the 36 states and the FCT.

The planned inauguration will precede the October 24 rally in Kaduna, which is expected to mark the beginning of the party’s nationwide campaign activities.

World.title: Orlando Pirates midweek fixture confirmed after MTN8 heartbreak
World.content:
Following their MTN8 final defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns, Orlando Pirates will be eager to dust themselves off and get back to winning ways.

The Buccaneers have little time to dwell on their disappointment as they prepare to face TS Galaxy in the Betway Premiership on Tuesday evening.

A victory could see Pirates move above Sundowns at the top of the league standings, providing some consolation after missing out on another MTN8 title.



After seven league matches, Abdeslam Ouaddou’s men have won six and drawn once, underlining their impressive start to the campaign.

However, their challenge will be to ensure that Saturday’s defeat does not affect their confidence and momentum in the league.

TS Galaxy could capitalise if the Soweto giants struggle to put their MTN8 heartbreak behind them. The Rockets will be hoping to make life difficult for Pirates as they look to return to domestic action with a positive result.

When Do Orlando Pirates Play TS Galaxy?

Pirates host TS Galaxy on Tuesday evening at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

The Buccaneers have enjoyed success against the Rockets in recent meetings, including an emphatic 5-0 victory at the Mbombela Stadium earlier this year.

With only three days between the MTN8 final and their next league fixture, changes to the Orlando Pirates starting XI could be expected.



The likes of Mohau Nkota and Thalente Mbatha could be in contention for their first starts of the season after recently recovering from injuries.

Ouaddou will also have to manage his squad carefully, with Pirates set to turn their attention to the CAF Champions League preliminary round next weekend.

The clash against Galaxy therefore presents an opportunity for the Buccaneers to respond immediately to their cup disappointment while maintaining their strong start to the league campaign.

Will the Buccaneers bounce back?

World.title: In one year, drug crime increased by 57% in this Gauteng suburb
World.content:
The impact of drug use spreads further than its users. Image: Pexels

Drug crime in Gauteng is up 8.7%.

According to the South African Police Service’s (SAPS) recent data, 11 619 drug-related crimes were reported in Gauteng between April and June 2026.

But in a handful of police precincts, drug-related crime has increased by concerning figures.



Drug-Related Crimes Up Significantly

In Gauteng, drug-related crime is trending upward. About 76% of precincts reported a rise or no change in this kind of crime.

Eden Park, however, recorded a 57.7% increase in drug crimes between April-June 2026 and the same period last year.

Sebokeng in Sedibeng experienced the second-highest increase in the province.



In one year, drug-related crime in the area rose 45.1%.

Only 35 of the province’s 146 SAPS precincts recorded a decrease. Some of these weren’t even that substantial.

Rosebank, for example, had drug-related crimes drop from 1 in the first quarter of 2025 to 0 in the first quarter of 2026.



In Muldersdrift on the West Rand and Fairland in Johannesburg, drug-related crime also decreased by 1 incident, from 3 reported in the first quarter of 2025 to 2 reported in the first quarter of 2026.

Police Precinct # Drug-Related Crimes % Increase Eden Park 112 57.7% Sebokeng 148 45.1% Soshanguve 96 33.3% Sharpeville 183 29.9% Duduza 105 26.5%

Johannesburg Central is Gauteng’s drug capital.

In 3 months, 358 drug-related crimes were reported in Johannesburg, up 5.9% from the same time last year.



Tembisa was next with 309 drug-related crimes, a 6.9% decrease from the year before.

The township was 1 of only 3 precincts in the province’s top 10, where drug-related crimes decreased.

In areas like Krugersdorp, Tsakane, Kliptown, and Orange Farm, all in the top 10, drug-related crimes are up double digits.



Reporting Drug Crimes

Drug-related crimes are frequently underreported.

A 2025 study suggests all crime in South Africa, not only drug crime, is underreported.

Therefore, when drug reporting spikes, it can point to more production, distribution and use rather than more informed policing efforts.



Impact of this Worrying Trend

The impact of drug-related crimes on a community is far-reaching.

According to data from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) World Drug Report 2026, the number of people using drugs rose to 331 million in 2024, up 34% from a decade earlier.

Seizures, production, and cocaine use also reached record highs in 2024.



But as UNODC highlights in its report, besides impacting communities and families, drug use impacts healthcare, social services and the criminal justice system.

Drug use drains resources.

Furthermore, the report spotlights three areas where drug abuse has real financial and social impact on communities.

World.title: Mkhwebane calls for South Africa to withdraw from UN, AU conventions
World.content:
Former Public Protector Advocate Busisiwe Mkhwebane has called for South Africa to withdraw from all United Nations (UN) and African Union (AU) conventions and rejoin with reservations, following violent protests over the Department of Home Affairs’ directive on asylum applications.

Protests in Durban and Soweto turned violent amid opposition to the directive, which has since been withdrawn.

MKHWEBANE WEIGHS IN ON HOME AFFAIRS ASYLUM DIRECTIVE

Mkhwebane took to X, formerly Twitter, to share her views on the issue.



The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party member described South Africa’s Constitution as the biggest source of the problem.

“We need processing centres of asylum seekers to be kept there until approval. We cannot allow people to roam SA without status or abuse asylum papers,” she wrote.

Mkhwebane also argued that the courts were established to protect constitutional democracy, not to destabilise the country, replace elected government or make far-reaching decisions without considering their consequences.



“About 350 people died after one intervention. Vehicles are burning after another. Communities have revolted, highways have been blocked, and confidence in the judiciary is deteriorating.

“The choice is no longer only between modest court reform and another crisis. It is between abolishing this Constitution and waiting for another judgment to ignite a crisis the country may no longer be able to contain,” she added.

MARCH AND MARCH SUPPORTS CALL

Meanwhile, March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma has also called for the government to withdraw from United Nations agreements and hold a referendum on the Constitution.



Ngobese-Zuma said South Africa should not be an option for people who felt unsafe in their home countries.

“We’ve got our own safety concerns, we’ve got our own economic crisis, we’ve got our own problems and ideally now we are going to call for government to withdraw from the United Nations agreements and call for them to have a referendum on the South African Constitution because we can’t glorify a Constitution that does not serve its people,” she said.

World.title: Bafana Bafana striker nets on full MLS debut
World.content:
Bafana Bafana striker Lyle Foster netted on his full Major League Soccer (MLS) debut for Houston Dynamo against Minnesota United on Sunday.

The two sides played to a thrilling 2-2 draw with Houston Dynamo needing a late equaliser to rescue a point.

Foster had already featured for Houston Dynamo but that appearance came from the substitute bench.



BAFANA BAFANA STRIKER LYLE FOSTER SCORES ON FULL MLS DEBUT

Foster was named in the starting line-up for the first since joining Houston Dynamo on loan from English side Burnley FC.

And he made an immediate impact as he opened the scoring in the 18th minute, much to the delight of team’s technical team.

Nonetheless, Minnesota came back stronger in the second half as they equalised in the 48th minute through Kelvin Yeboah before Marcus Caldeira fired them ahead in the 78th minute.

Houston Dynamo, did not give up as they threw everything at the home side, and deep into stoppage time, Duncan McGuire restored parity and rescued a point for his team.

HLONGWANE ALSO STARTED FOR MINNESOTA

Meanwhile, another Bafana Bafana attacker in Bongokuhle Hlongwane also started for Minnesota United in the same match.

Hlongwane, though, was replaced in the 64th minute as the home side continued to search for that important lead.

World.title: Mthokozisi Sithole: Three convicted of murdering IFP branch secretary
World.content:
Three men have been convicted of the murder of Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) Branch Executive Committee (BEC) secretary Mthokozisi Sithole.

Sthembiso Nkululeko Xulu, Mduduzi Mncube and Sthabiso Mncube were convicted in the Estcourt Regional Court on Thursday, 8 October. They are expected to be sentenced on 28 October 2026.

THREE CONVICTED OF MURDERING IFP ACTIVIST MTHOKOZISI SITHOLE

According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), the IFP activist was shot and killed outside a tavern in Weenen on 27 January 2024.



NEWS: The IFP activist in Estcourt in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands who was gunned down last week Saturday is being buried today. Mthokozisi Sithole was gunned down last by unknown gunmen while in the town of Weenen. Speaking on the sidelines of the funeral, the chairperson of the… pic.twitter.com/Wu64o24VXY — Sihle Mavuso (@ZANewsFlash) February 2, 2024

Following an investigation by the KwaZulu-Natal Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), four suspects were arrested and charged with murder and the possession of an unlicensed firearm and ammunition.

Police said the investigation also linked the firearm used in Mthokozisi Sithole’s murder to another case involving the killing of Thembinkosi Manana.

Sthabiso Mncube was also charged in connection with Manana’s murder, and the two cases were prosecuted jointly.

Judgment was handed down in both cases, with the court finding three accused guilty of murder and possession of an unlicensed firearm.

“The PKTT remains resolute in its efforts to ensure that perpetrators of political killings are identified, arrested and prosecuted, while continuing to work closely with the National Prosecuting Authority to strengthen cases brought before the courts,” police said.



IFP chairperson in KwaZulu-Natal Thami Ntuli, applauded the work of the police in this case following the arrest of the suspects.

World.title: ONLY bad light could come to Proteas’ rescue against Australia
World.content:
The Proteas are facing an uphill battle to salvage a draw against Australia in the first Test at Kingsmead in Durban.

After an impressive opening day with the ball, Temba Bavuma’s men were frustrated by poor light conditions, with play abandoned around 15:00 on Day 1.

South Africa appeared on course to bowl Australia out for fewer than 200 runs, but Day 2 proved a different story as the visitors’ lower order staged a remarkable fightback.



A 134-run partnership between Matt Renshaw and Nathan Lyon turned the game around and helped Australia post a formidable first-innings total of 390.

Australia frustrate Proteas bowlers

In reply, the Proteas ended Day 2 on 27/1, but their situation deteriorated on the third morning. By lunch, South Africa had slumped to 114/6, leaving them with a mountain to climb to stay in the contest.

The Proteas will now be relying on Wiaan Mulder and Tristan Stubbs to produce a crucial partnership and give the lower order a chance to fight back.

South Africa need to reach 191 runs to avoid the follow-on, which would allow Australia to enforce another innings and put further pressure on the hosts.

Avoiding the follow-on would be an important first step, but the Proteas would still need to bat for a significant period to keep their hopes of a draw alive.

Poor light could potentially work in their favour if it interrupts play again, although South Africa cannot afford to rely on the weather alone.



With Australia likely to strengthen their advantage if given another opportunity to bat, the Proteas need their remaining batters to show resilience and occupy the crease.

A substantial partnership between Mulder and Stubbs, followed by a determined effort from the lower order, could give South Africa a chance of surviving the Test.

Ultimately, the Proteas will need to bat with patience and discipline if they are to avoid defeat and salvage a draw against Australia at Kingsmead.

Can the Proteas salvage a draw?

World.title: ‘Kaizer Chiefs are specialists in failure’
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs need to arrest a poor run of results when they get back to action in the league. Worryingly, their bogey team lies in wait.

Chiefs have already dropped too many points to be title contenders

Heading into a lengthy break for internationals, Chiefs produced a sequence of indifferent results. They’ve drawn four of their last five, the only win in that sequence was a 3-2 success over Siwelele. Next up is a clash with bogey team Stellenbosch, with ex-Stellies man Thabo Moloisane now lining up for the Glamour Boys. Chiefs now trail newly-crowned MTN8 champions Sundowns by seven points, so they can’t drop too many more before Christmas to stay in the title race. Chiefs vs Stellenbosch on Tuesday, 13 October kicks off at 19:30.

Since 2014-15, Chiefs have just a solitary piece of silverware to show for their efforts. A win against Orlando Pirates in the 2025 Nedbank Cup final was a solid fillip for the club, but it’s not enough. Chiefs have to mount credible title challenges year on year otherwise their work must be considered incomplete.



Latest injury news

lavio Silva is back in training alongside Khanyisa Mayo, who has recovered after a hernia operation. 21-year-old winger Langelihle Phili is also nearing a return after a serious ankle injury he sustained in late August during training. Phili could return towards the end of October. The fitness of playmaker Lebo Maboe is also a concern.

World.title: Police launch festive season operations
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The SAPS is ramping up its crime-fighting efforts ahead of the festive season.

Its national Safer Festive Season Operations will be launched in Mpumalanga today.

Police have vowed to intensify operations to boost visibility, prevent crime and keep communities safe.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia is expected to receive the national operational plan from Acting National Commissioner Puleng Dimpane.

World.title: 109 migrants dead, 116 missing in boat wreck off Djibouti: UN
World.content:
DJIBOUTI - At least 109 migrants died, including 15 children, and 116 went missing when a boat sank off the shores of Djibouti on the night of October 8-9, a UN agency said Sunday.

Survivors said the vessel, which was carrying 305 people from Djibouti to Yemen, capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock, according to a statement from the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

"Survivors told me that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it," Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, told AFP.

"This is a devastating loss of life," he said earlier in the statement.

"Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives."

Coissac said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.

"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities" by trying to cross the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then reach Gulf countries.

Among the 109 bodies recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children, nine girls and six boys, the statement said.

More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

"Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East," the IOM said.

- Perilous Yemen route -

The IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.

"Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing."

It said that 178,000 people had arrived in Djibouti from Ethiopia from January to October this year.

Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia, despite a surge in conflict in Yemen.

The country is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.

Coissac said 150 of the people on the boat that sank off Djibouti had previously been turned back from Yemen but had attempted the crossing again.

He said he had also spoken to one survivor of the wreck who came from the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, where rebels are battling the federal government in a recent flare-up of violence.

In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen and the number attempting the journey increased by 18 percent, the IOM said.

A shipwreck in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.

IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that most of the people attempting the journey were from Ethiopia or Somalia.

He said many of them were ending up stuck in Djibouti.

The IOM urged "donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti's response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance".

World.title: Government eyes supervisory order on asylum ruling
World.content:
PRETORIA - Home Affairs needs more time to prepare for the implementation of the Constitutional Court’s asylum ruling.

Government has said the department needs to strengthen its systems, staff and processing capacity before the judgment can be fully implemented.

Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi said government may ask the court for a supervisory order to oversee the process.

"Following a detailed legal consultation, we have been duly advised that government can approach the courts to seek a supervisory order in this regard. A supervisory order in practical terms would enable the court to retain oversight of the implementation process and provide guidance on how the order should be operationalized.

“Such an order may also include a suspension period to allow the Department of Foreign Affairs the necessary time to develop and strengthen administrative, human resource, infrastructure, and processing capacity required to implement the judgment effectively and sustainably.

“We believe that this approach represents a responsible and lawful mechanism to ensure that constitutional obligations are fulfilled in a manner that is orderly, practical and in the public interest. It will allow government to avoid administrative disruption while ensuring that the rights recognized by the court are progressively and meaningfully realized.”

World.title: All systems go for matric exams
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Basic Education Department has put plans in place to ensure this year’s matric exams run without disruption.

Minister Siviwe Gwarube said strict quality control measures and a zero-tolerance for examination irregularities will be enforced.

“This year we will have a network of around 7,100 examination centers and to ensure a secure environment, have audited an entire network and implemented risk-based monitoring approach, directing our supervision and resources exactly to where they are needed most.

“I want to assure the public that the setting, the moderation, the quality assurance, and all the examination materials are complete. All question papers and examination instruments have been rigorously reviewed by the DBE and have been approved by UMALUSI.

“Crucially, learning from the past challenges, have significantly strengthened our security controls of the entire production and distribution chain. Through the district vetting and examination officials and close collaboration with national and provincial law enforcement structures, we are safeguarding examination materials very closely.

“We have established 189 marking centers, successfully recruiting 51,104 qualified and experienced education markers to mark our scripts. We will apply a standardized national approach to marking, underpinned by strict quality control processes strengthened and the moderation of school-based assessment.

“Let me be clear; the DBE is taking a proactive, zero-tolerance approach to examination irregularities. The candidate and parent pledge agreements to instill a culture of integrity to our young ones and 24-hour examination hotline which is active for the public to report any and all suspicious activity. Furthermore, we have robust contingency plans in place to manage operational challenges including severe weather conditions, community disruptions, because we want no learner to be disadvantaged.”

World.title: Cachalia to foreign nationals: ‘don’t take the law into your own hands’
World.content:
PRETORIA - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has warned undocumented foreign nationals, against taking the law into their own hands.

He's condemned the use of firearms during confrontations in KwaZulu-Natal,

and says those who break the law will face the consequences.

“ I do have a message for those people who are in the country illegally or maybe here from other countries. And the message is the one that we have addressed to our citizens, which is that your responsibility is to observe the law, not take the law into your own hands, not to confront protesters who have a view about illegal immigration in this country.

“When you do that, you can only worsen your own situation. It's, it's intolerable, for instance, that incident in KwaZulu-Natal. Why were they armed? Why were they discharging their firearms? There can't be fiefdoms in South Africa that are in effect occupied by groups confronting South Africans."

World.title: Prince Harry, Meghan to carry out first joint engagement since UK return: reports
World.content:
LONDON - Britain's Prince Harry and his wife Meghan will on Thursday carry out their first joint engagement since returning to live in the UK in August, according to media reports.

King Charles III's 42-year-old younger son and Meghan will on that day visit Nottingham in central England, the city where they made their first joint appearance after announcing their engagement in 2017, the Sunday Times reported.

The visit signalled the couple's "determination to be viewed as public figures", the report said.

That resolve is at odds with a letter last month in which the king made it clear that their position was "akin to private citizens" rather than public figures and that they should not be addressed as his and her royal highness.

They are expected to visit projects at three charities that support young people and local communities through music, film, sport and tackling food poverty, the report said.

The couple left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud.

Although they have since built bridges with Charles, they remain estranged from Harry's older brother and heir to the crown Prince William.

The couple had settled in California, but in a surprise move Harry and Meghan, 45, returned to live in the United Kingdom with their two young children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, in August.

The report added that they would return to the United States for Christmas, quoting a friend as saying "they know they're not going to be invited (to the royal family's get-together) and they're not waiting for an invitation".

The royal family traditionally gathers at the king's Sandringham estate in eastern England at Christmas.

World.title: Department to scrap use of drivers’ licences as ID
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As South Africa marks Transport Month, the department is moving to stop drivers' licences and Traffic Register Numbers (TRN) from being used as ID documents.

The move follows a 2023 investigation which found widespread misuse of Traffic Register Numbers.

Minister Barbara Creecy said her department has already blocked 300,000 inactive numbers, with holders of the remaining ones being asked to verify their details with Home Affairs.

“We have already embarked on the first phase of this process that has led to us being in a position to block 300,000 of dormant TRNs on the system. So it's almost half of those that were found to be fraudulent. We're in phase two, which is the balance of these TRN. And what we have done is we have called on those who believe that their numbers are bona fide and their identification is bona fide to seek the necessary verification from Home Affairs.

“It's not a huge number, I must say, that have come forward. I think the last time I looked there were about 8,000, which is about 1% of the numbers that were found to be fraudulent. We have given Home Affairs this information. We have also advised the relevant parties to contact Home Affairs and ensure that they are appropriately verified."

World.title: Gift of the Givers helps Imizamo Yethu fire victims
World.content:
HOUT BAY - A major fire has swept through Imizamo Yethu in Hout Bay.

Firefighters have managed to contain the blaze, but are monitoring the site in case of flare-ups.

Gift of the Givers is providing emergency humanitarian aid to residents of the informal settlement.

The organisation has mobilised hot meals and bottled water for affected residents.

Damage assessments are under way, led by Disaster Management officials,

and community leaders, to determine the extent of the destruction and the urgent needs of displaced families.

World.title: Optics tell it all: Why William Ruto looks tell of a desperate politician
World.content:
President William Ruto has taken on a worrying look of late – sweating profusely, eyes wild and blazing, teeth bared in a rictus smile, absolutely furious, panicking and shouting, and with no apparent control of what comes out of his mouth. Things fall apart, and this is the look and sound of a desperate man. And optics matter.
